About the Role

We are looking for a Regional Director of Sales to lead revenue growth across a defined region within the Americas. This is a critical frontline leadership role for someone who has managed high-performing enterprise Account Executives, understands complex technical sales cycles, and is excited to help build the go-to-market motion for one of the most important categories in software.

As Regional Director, Sales, you will own regional revenue execution, pipeline development, forecast accuracy, and team performance. You will lead a team of quota-carrying Account Executives selling to technical, product, and business stakeholders at high-growth startups and large enterprises.

This role is ideal for a hands-on sales leader who combines strong operating discipline with curiosity about AI, developer platforms, and emerging infrastructure markets. You should be comfortable staying close to deals, coaching sellers through complex cycles, and helping customers understand both immediate use cases and long-term strategic value.

What You’ll Do

  • Own regional revenue targets, pipeline generation, forecast accuracy, and overall sales execution.

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of enterprise Account Executives.

  • Build a culture of accountability, customer obsession, strong qualification, and consistent execution.

  • Partner closely with Sales Engineering, Customer Success, Product, Marketing, and Sales leadership to improve win rates and customer outcomes.

  • Drive disciplined execution across territory planning, account strategy, opportunity qualification, mutual action plans, forecasting, and expansion motions.

  • Stay deeply engaged in strategic opportunities, including executive alignment, deal strategy, negotiation, and closing.

  • Coach the team on selling to technical and executive audiences, including engineering leaders, AI teams, platform teams, product leaders, and business stakeholders.

  • Inspect pipeline rigorously, identify risks early, and ensure clear next steps across priority opportunities.

  • Develop a clear view of market demand, buyer personas, competitive dynamics, and customer pain points across your region.

  • Help refine LangChain’s enterprise sales motion as we scale from early GTM into a more repeatable, predictable sales organization.

  • Recruit, onboard, and retain high-performing sales talent as the region grows.

What We’re Looking For

  • 7+ years of enterprise software sales experience, including 2+ years leading quota-carrying sales teams.

  • Proven track record managing teams that sell complex technical products to enterprise customers.

  • Experience hiring, coaching, and developing high-performing Account Executives.

  • Strong command of enterprise sales fundamentals: qualification, discovery, value selling, mutual action plans, forecasting, negotiation, and executive engagement.

  • Experience selling to technical buyers such as engineering, infrastructure, data, AI/ML, developer platform, or product teams.

  • Ability to operate in a fast-moving, early-stage or high-growth environment where playbooks are still being built.

  • Strong cross-functional instincts and a collaborative approach to working with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success.

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to simplify complex technical concepts for different audiences.

  • High ownership, low ego, and a willingness to be hands-on with customers, deals, and team development.

Nice to Have

  • Experience selling developer tools, infrastructure software, observability, data platforms, ML/AI tooling, or open-source commercial products.

  • Familiarity with LLMs, AI agents, RAG, observability, evaluations, or modern AI application development.

  • Experience helping scale a regional sales function at a company moving from founder-led or early GTM to a more repeatable enterprise sales motion.

  • Experience with MEDDIC, MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, or similar enterprise sales methodologies.

  • Prior success selling into both digital-native and large enterprise accounts.

  • Experience working in a highly technical, product-led, or open-source-influenced sales environment.

Why Join Us

AI is changing how software is built, deployed, and operated. LangChain is at the center of that shift. This is an opportunity to help build the sales organization for a category-defining company, work with highly technical and ambitious customers, and shape how enterprises adopt production-grade AI systems.

You’ll join a team that values ownership, clarity, curiosity, and pace — and you’ll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the company’s growth trajectory.

At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.

With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.

Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

About the Role:

We’re hiring Sales Development Representatives to join our founding SDR team and help shape the future of how companies adopt LangChain. As part of our SDR team, you’ll turn high inbound interest and targeted outbound demand into qualified opportunities and create an exceptional first-touch experiences for prospects.

You’ll work closely with our Marketing, Sales, and Operations alongside using LangChain and LangGraph-powered agents to automate list building, enrichment, and outreach freeing you to focus entirely on high-impact prospecting and conversations with teams exploring agentic AI.

What makes this role different: You’ll drive pipeline and revenue while learning to leverage AI, automation, and LangChain itself to become a next-generation GTM operator.

What You'll Do:

  • Follow up with inbound and outbound prospects via phone, email, and LinkedIn to uncover fit, needs, and potential value.

  • Partner closely with Account Executives to hand off qualified opportunities and ensure a smooth buyer experience.

  • Capture and share insights from conversations to inform our sales plays, product roadmap, and agent development.

  • Experiment with new channels, messaging, and automation to continuously increase conversion and efficiency.

  • Use LangChain powered agents to test, learn, and improve prospecting strategies

How to be successful in this role:

  • 1–2 years of experience in a Sales, SDR, or BDR role within SaaS or technology (or strong curiosity and drive if you’re early in your career)

  • Clear, confident communicator who can engage both technical and business audiences

  • Motivated by learning, iteration, and experimentation you treat outreach like a craft

  • Comfortable with a mix of structure and ambiguity you can execute repeatable processes while improving them along the way

  • Excited about modern sales tech, AI tools, and shaping how next-generation GTM teams operate

  • Positive, persistent, and highly organized you follow up, follow through, and bring energy to every interaction

Compensation Philosophy:

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Millions of developers trust LangChain to power AI teams at companies like Replit, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, and 35% of the Fortune 500.

With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.

About the Team

The LangChain Deployed Engineering - Federal team works directly with U.S. Government customers — including the Department of Defense (DoD), Civilian Agencies, and the Intelligence Community (IC) — who are building and operating AI agents in mission-critical environments.

This is a hands-on, highly technical team that partners closely with government engineers, technical program managers, and system integrators across the full lifecycle — from pre-award technical shaping and evaluations to post-deployment advisory work in secure environments. The focus is on achieving the technical win, architecting secure and compliant agent systems, and enabling agencies to operate AI agents reliably at scale using the LangChain suite.

Deployed Engineers sit at the intersection of engineering, product, security, and go-to-market. You will shape how LangChain is adopted across classified and unclassified environments, ensuring alignment with federal compliance requirements while feeding mission-driven insights back into the platform.

About the Role

As a Deployed Engineer, you’ll work on some of the hardest problems in applied AI — not demos or experimental research, but production systems supporting real-world missions.

You’ll help defense, civilian, and intelligence customers design, deploy, and operate AI agents in secure, regulated, and high-stakes environments. The feedback loop is fast, the mission impact is tangible, and your work directly influences how AI agents are deployed across the federal landscape.

You will operate in environments that demand security, reliability, compliance (FedRAMP, IL levels, etc.), and operational rigor.

What You’ll Do

  • Co-architect and co-build production AI agents with federal engineering teams and system integrators

  • Own the technical win in federal pre-sales engagements by designing secure POCs, supporting RFI/RFP technical responses, and guiding technical evaluations

  • Design architectures that meet federal security and compliance requirements (FedRAMP, DoD IL2–IL6, NIST, etc.)

  • Help agencies deploy and operate agent-based applications such as mission support copilots, intelligence analysis agents, research automation systems, and multi-step operational workflows

  • Advise customers post-award on architecture, scalability, observability, evaluation, and long-term roadmap decisions

  • Deliver technical demos, workshops, and enablement sessions tailored to government developer and operator audiences

  • Partner with security teams to navigate ATO processes and accreditation pathways

  • Surface field feedback from federal use cases and contribute reusable patterns, secure deployment guides, and example code that scale across agencies

  • Occasionally contribute code upstream when it meaningfully improves federal customer outcomes

What You’ll Bring

  • Must have zctive or prior U.S. security clearance (Secret, TS/SCI)

  • 3+ years in a relevant technical role (software engineering, customer engineering, solutions engineering, product engineering), ideally supporting federal or regulated customers

  • Experience working with DoD, Civilian Agencies, Intelligence Community, or federal system integrators

  • Strong Python and JavaScript fundamentals, with deep systems thinking

  • Experience designing agent-based or LLM-powered systems beyond simple API calls, including multi-step workflows, orchestration, guardrails, and failure handling

  • Familiarity with secure cloud environments (AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, etc.)

  • Comfort operating in regulated environments with security, compliance, and documentation requirements

  • Experience supporting technical evaluations, architecture reviews, and competitive down-select processes

  • Ability to clearly explain technical tradeoffs to government stakeholders and build trust across engineering and program leadership

  • Ownership mindset — you take responsibility for mission outcomes, not just recommendations

  • Bias toward action and comfort operating in ambiguity

  • Excitement about running AI agents in real-world, production federal environments — not just building demos

Nice to Have

  • Experience deploying AI systems in classified or air-gapped environments

  • Familiarity with FedRAMP authorization processes or DoD Impact Levels (IL2–IL6)

  • Experience with LLM evaluation, observability, red-teaming, or guardrails in high-assurance settings

  • Hands-on experience with AWS, Azure, containers, Kubernetes, and secure networking architectures

  • Experience working alongside federal system integrators (Booz Allen, SAIC, Leidos, etc.)

  • Production experience with LangChain, LangGraph, or similar agent frameworks

Compensation & Benefits

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. Benefits include things like medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, and life insurance. Actual compensation and offerings will vary based on role, level, and location. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Annual OTE range: $185,000–$300,000 USD

Compensation Philosophy:

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

About the team

SmithDB is LangChain's internal database team. We're building a storage and query layer purpose-built for AI observability and evaluation. Within six months we went from idea to a production system that offers industry leading performance and scalability for agent observability data. We're a small, fast team of systems engineers tackling genuinely hard problems: storage layout, query execution, compaction, and scaling toward trillions of agent traces. We develop in Rust, run on Kubernetes, and integrate tightly with S3/GCS/Azure Blob. There are no legacy constraints; this is a greenfield system with real production load and ambitious engineering goals.

 

About the role

We're looking for a hands-on Engineering Manager to lead the SmithDB team. This is not a pure people-management role. You'll write production code, review PRs at the systems level, make architectural calls, and be in the weeds alongside your engineers. At the same time, you'll own team health, hiring, technical roadmap, and coordination with the broader LangSmith platform. The ideal candidate has deep systems or database engineering experience and genuinely prefers to stay technical while growing a team.

 

What you'll do

  • Write and review production Rust code across ingestion, query execution, and storage layers

  • Lead architectural decisions on storage format, compaction, indexing, and query planning

  • Drive performance investigations using memory and CPU profiling tools; own the path from profiling to shipped fix

  • Design and harden the distributed deployment of SmithDB services on Kubernetes (multi-tenant, high-throughput, low-latency)

  • Contribute to cloud object store integrations (S3, GCS, Azure Blob) and set the standard for how SmithDB manages data at rest and in flight

  • Build and maintain observability for the engine itself: metrics, tracing, debug tooling

  • Manage a small but growing team of systems engineers: set goals, run 1:1s, provide technical mentorship, and grow careers

  • Own the SmithDB technical roadmap in partnership with LangSmith product and engineering leadership

  • Communicate progress, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to the broader organization: you write concise, decision-ready updates

 

What you'll bring

  • 7+ years in systems or database engineering, with at least 2 years in a technical lead or engineering management role

  • Production Rust experience — you can write it, review it, and have opinions on how to structure it at scale

  • Deep understanding of database or storage engine internals: query execution, storage layouts, indexing, compaction

  • Proficiency in systems performance analysis: memory allocators, CPU hotspots, lock contention, async runtimes (Tokio)

  • Experience deploying and operating distributed services on Kubernetes in a production, multi-tenant environment

  • Familiarity with cloud object storage (S3-compatible APIs, consistency models, cost/performance tradeoffs)

  • Proven track record of managing engineers — you can recruit, retain, and level-up a team without losing your technical edge

Nice-to-have:

  • Experience building or contributing to columnar storage formats (Parquet, Arrow), OLAP query engines, or time-series stores

  • Background in observability infrastructure or tracing pipelines (OpenTelemetry, ClickHouse, Prometheus)

  • Experience scaling a system from early-stage to hundreds of billions / trillions of records

About the team

SmithDB is LangChain's internal database team. We're building a storage and query layer purpose-built for AI observability and evaluation. Within six months we went from idea to a production system that offers industry leading performance and scalability for agent observability data. We're a small, fast team of systems engineers tackling genuinely hard problems: storage layout, query execution, compaction, and scaling toward trillions of agent traces. We develop in Rust, run on Kubernetes, and integrate tightly with S3/GCS/Azure Blob. There are no legacy constraints; this is a greenfield system with real production load and ambitious engineering goals.

About the role

We're a fast-moving team looking for a systems / database engineer to help design, optimize, and harden our system. Within 6 months, we've gone from idea to production system but there is still lots to build and optimize. You'll be working on execution, storage layout, performance profiling, and scaling to trillions of traces. This role is based in San Francisco.

 

What you'll do

  • Engineer performant Rust code for ingestion and query execution

  • Optimize for cost and speed, heavily utilizing memory and CPU profiling

  • Integrate tightly with cloud object stores (S3/GCS/Azure Blob)

  • Deploy our distributed database services on Kubernetes (multi-tenant, high throughput, low latency)

  • Contribute to observability for the storage engine itself (metrics, tracing, debug tooling)

 

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years in systems/database engineering with strong experience in a systems programming language (Rust, C++). Rust strongly preferred, as it is the language we use.

  • Knowledge of database internals is a plus: query engines, storage systems, indexing, and compaction

  • Proficiency in systems performance analysis: memory allocation, CPU hotspots, lock contention, async runtimes.

  • Familiarity with similar query execution engines is a plus

  • Experience with Kubernetes, distributed systems, and cloud object storage is a plus.

  • Strong fundamentals in networking, OS concepts, and systems debugging.

description:

We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

About the Role:

LangChain has strong technical credibility, a large developer community, and a lot worth saying. What we need now is someone to make sure we're saying it — consistently, strategically, and in ways that land.

We're looking for a Head of Narratives to own how LangChain shows up in the world across communications, brand, social, and design. This is a role for someone who thinks like a media company operator: always-on publishing, sharp editorial judgment, a clear point of view on the themes that matter, and a relentless focus on getting great narratives in front of the right people at the right time.

You'll lead an existing team of rockstars across brand, social, and design — each with deep expertise. Your job is to give the team a shared narrative direction, keep the output sharp and consistent, and make sure LangChain is building an audience that wants to hear from us.

This is a player-coach role. You'll set the direction but you'll also be in the work — shaping editorial, giving creative feedback, and reviewing and writing. The right person is opinionated about what good looks like and hands-on enough to help get there.

 

What You'll Do:

Communications

  • Define the themes and narratives LangChain is hitting. Spearhead the direction on what LangChain should be known for and translate that into a rolling communications strategy the whole team is working from. This is the backbone of everything else.

  • Own press and media relations. Kickstart our comms efforts, building and managing relationships with key journalists and outlets, drive proactive press coverage, and act as the point of contact for inbound media inquiries.

  • Shape executive visibility and thought leadership. Identify the moments, platforms, and formats where LangChain's leaders should have a voice, and help them show up with a clear, consistent point of view.

  • Lead announcement strategy. Plan and execute communications around major launches, funding, partnerships, and company milestones, working cross-functionally to make sure the story lands with the right audiences at the right time.

  • Set and uphold the communications standard. Define LangChain's voice in the outside world and the quality bar for anything that goes out under its name.

Brand

  • Shape brand direction in close partnership with the brand lead. The brand lead focuses on brand voice, visual identity, and standards. You'll work closely together to align on where the brand is headed, what it stands for, and how it shows up — with narrative and brand informing each other rather than operating separately.

  • Stay close to major brand moments. Bring a point of view on concept and messaging for out-of-home, awareness campaigns, and other brand initiatives. Work with the brand lead to make sure what we're saying and how we're showing up are pulling in the same direction.

  • Make sure brand and narrative feel like one thing. The brand should feel like a natural extension of the editorial point of view, and vice versa.

Social & Rich Media

  • Partner with the social lead on strategy, themes, and goals. The social lead focuses on growing LangChain's social channels and ways to amplify our content and messaging. Work together to ensure social is amplifying the themes and narratives the broader team is driving.

  • Shape LangChain's rich media approach together. Work with the social lead to develop a shared point of view on how video, audio, and other formats fit into the content mix — where they build audience, where they deepen credibility, and how to build the right execution muscle over time.

  • Track what's working, what's not, and use it to sharpen direction. Stay close to performance across content, comms, brand, and social to have a better sense on where to focus, what narratives are resonating, and where to double down.

Brand Design

  • Lead the creative direction for brand design in close partnership with our brand designer. Own the visual vision for how LangChain looks and feels — and work day-to-day with our brand designer to translate that into execution across campaigns, content, comms, social, and brand moments.

  • Be a strong creative partner. Have a real point of view on what looks right, what earns trust with a technical audience, and where the work needs to go further. Give clear direction and help the designer do their best work.

  • Keep visual identity consistent across every channel. A media company looks like itself everywhere it shows up. Make sure LangChain does too.

Team Leadership

  • Lead by being in it. Develop your team by being close to the work — giving useful feedback, shaping output, and raising the bar through example.

  • Build the operating rhythm. Establish the rituals and shared workflows — editorial planning, cross-functional reviews, publishing cadences — that help brand, social, comms, and design operate as a unit.

  • Connect narrative to the rest of the business. Translate what marketing, sales, product, and leadership need into a narrative strategy your team can execute — and keep everyone aligned as priorities shift.

 

What We're Looking For:

  • Ability to work like a media company operator. You think in publishing cadences, audience development, and narrative arcs — not just campaigns. You know what it takes to build an always-on narrative engine and keep it running at a high standard.

  • Player-coach. You've led creative, comms, or content teams and know how to develop people — but you stay close to the work and make it better by being in it.

  • Strong narrative instincts. You have a clear point of view on what makes a brand story work and can translate that into real direction across comms, brand, social, and design.

  • Analytically grounded. You track what's working, form a view on why, and use that to make better decisions about where to focus. You connect creative work to business outcomes.

  • Developer audience instincts. You understand what earns trust with technical audiences and can orient a creative team around that bar.

  • Collaborative and clear. You work well with strong practitioners who own their domains — building alignment without stepping on what they own.

Nice to Have

  • Experience leading narrative, brand, or comms teams at a developer-focused company

  • Background in technical or developer marketing

  • Familiarity with the AI/ML ecosystem and the tools developers use to build

  • Track record running brand campaigns, including out-of-home or awareness programs

This is a high-leverage, senior individual contributor role where you will build and drive our federal partner strategy from the ground up — focused primarily on establishing deep, revenue-generating relationships with the major Federal Systems Integrators (FSIs) and a curated set of specialized boutique partners.

You are an operator at heart who loves the ambiguity of a fast-growing startup. You understand how developer tools and enterprise AI stacks fit together within the unique compliance and regulatory requirements of the federal space, and you have a track record of driving sourced and influenced revenue through partner channels without needing a heavy management playbook to guide you. This role sits within our GTM organization and will work closely with our field sellers, customer engineering teams, and product leaders to embed LangChain into the delivery practices and solution portfolios of the partners who win and execute the biggest federal AI programs.

Drive structured engagement across their AI/ML practices, solution architects, and business development teams to embed LangChain into active and upcoming program pursuits.

  • Support Hyperscaler Relationships Selectively: Maintain a lightweight working relationship with AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, and GCP Public Sector teams, primarily to support event sponsorships, joint visibility opportunities, and marketplace presence — without making this a primary focus of the role.

  • Execute Co-Marketing Motions: Partner with marketing to show up effectively at key federal industry events (AFCEA, AWS Summit DC, industry days) and develop technical content and co-branded materials that reinforce LangChain's credibility with FSI and agency audiences.

  • Build the Playbook: Create the operational blueprint for how LangChain scales federal partnerships — from initial relationship mapping and partner tiering to joint pipeline tracking and executive engagement cadences.

What You'll Bring

  • Experience: 6+ years of experience in federal partner management, business development, or alliance roles, with a strong track record of building and monetizing relationships with major FSIs and federal primes. Direct experience working within or alongside Leidos, Booz Allen Hamilton, Northrop Grumman, SAIC, or similar organizations is a significant plus.

  • FSI Network: A genuine, pre-existing network within the business development, AI/ML practice, and solutions architecture communities at the major federal primes. You should be able to get meetings quickly and have credibility with the people who shape program pursuit decisions.

  • Technical Foundation: Enough technical fluency to speak credibly with enterprise architects and engineering leads in federal environments. You don't need to write code, but you must understand how LLMs, agentic frameworks, and developer tooling operate within federal infrastructure, including FedRAMP, IL4/IL5, and zero-trust requirements.

  • Startup Agility: Proven ability to navigate a high-growth environment with limited structure. You are comfortable building the playbook as you run it, executing independently with minimal supervision in the often long-cycle federal sales environment.

  • Operational Rigor: Strong pipeline management skills. You track partner activity with clean CRM hygiene, maintain accurate opportunity attribution, and communicate clearly and consistently to internal stakeholders.

  • Strong Communication & Influence: Equally comfortable writing sharp internal strategy docs as you are presenting to senior BD and practice leaders at major federal integrators.

Nice to Have's

  • Active security clearance (Secret or higher) or existing clearance eligibility.

  • Prior experience at an open-source, developer tools, or infrastructure software company bringing a new technology into the federal FSI ecosystem.

  • Familiarity with federal procurement vehicles (GSA Schedule, OTAs, BPAs) and how primes use them to structure program delivery.

The Deployed Engineering team is the technical front line of our go-to-market motion. We partner with account executives from the first technical conversation through production rollout, helping companies evaluate LangChain, prove it out on their hardest use case, and get agents running reliably at scale.

This is a hands-on, highly technical team. We sit at the intersection of engineering, product, and sales. What we learn in the field shapes both how customers adopt LangChain and what we build next.

 

About the role

You will work on some of the hardest problems in applied AI, in front of customers, on a clock. Not demos, not research: systems real teams depend on in production. The feedback loop is fast, the impact is measurable in closed deals and live deployments, and the work directly shapes how AI agents get built in the real world.

 

What you'll do

  • Own the technical win. Partner with AEs to scope evaluations, run technical discovery, and design POCs that map to the customer's real use case rather than a canned demo

  • Be the technical authority in the room during architecture reviews, security and infrastructure questions, and head-to-head evaluations

  • Co-architect and co-build production AI agents with customer engineering teams, from prototype through rollout

  • Help customers deploy and operate agent-based applications such as conversational agents, research agents, and multi-step workflows

  • Run demos, trainings, and workshops for developer audiences, from single-team sessions to larger technical enablement

  • Advise customers post-sale on architecture, best practices, and roadmap-level decisions, and find the expansion opportunities that come out of those conversations

  • Surface field feedback to product and build reusable POC assets, cookbooks, and example code that scale across accounts

  • Contribute code upstream when it meaningfully improves customer outcomes

 

What you'll bring

  • 6+ years in a relevant technical role such as solutions engineering, sales engineering, customer engineering, software engineering, or founding and product engineering, ideally at a startup or scale-up

  • Comfort owning the technical thread in a sales cycle: discovery, POCs, architecture reviews, and competitive evaluations

  • Ability to explain technical tradeoffs clearly and build trust with developer audiences, then translate that into a decision the customer is ready to make

  • A track record of taking responsibility for outcomes, not just recommendations

  • A bias toward action and a willingness to figure things out as you go

  • Genuine interest in operating AI agents in production, not just building demos

 

Nice to haves

  • You've deployed AI agents in production, especially using LangChain, LangGraph, or similar frameworks

  • Experience carrying a technical number or working against pipeline alongside a sales team

  • Experience with LLM evaluation, observability, or guardrails

  • Experience with cloud environments (AWS, GCP, Azure), containers, and basic Kubernetes concepts

Annual OTE range: $200,000–$300,000 USD. Final compensation will depend on experience, skills, and location.

Cloud providers and Systems Integrators help LangChain reach customers that our direct sales and customer engineering teams can't reach on their own. This role is the technical foundation behind that ecosystem.

You'll build the reference architectures, integration patterns, and enablement programs that make partner motions work technically: co-sell with cloud hyperscalers, and independent delivery capability at systems integrators and global systems integrators (GSIs). You build with and for a partner, whose technical team then takes what you built to dozens of their own clients.

About the role

AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure help LangChain reach customers that our direct sales and customer engineering teams can't reach on their own. This role is the technical foundation behind those cloud alliances.

You'll build the reference architectures, integration patterns, and co-sell assets that make our cloud motions work technically. That covers marketplace listings and private offers, joint solutions with cloud field teams, and technical wins on named accounts. You build with and for each cloud provider, and their partner and field teams then take what you built to many of their own customers. When a cloud deal involves a services partner, you make sure that partner can deliver on LangChain.

Key responsibilities

Cloud partner engineering (AWS, GCP, Azure)

  • Own the technical relationship with partner and field teams at AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure

  • Build reference architectures and integration patterns for running LangChain, LangGraph, DeepAgents and LangSmith on each cloud, including integrations with each provider's native AI and data services (for example Amazon Bedrock, Gemini Enterprise, AzureAI)

  • Support the technical side of co-sell: joint solution briefs, deployment guides, and validated architectures that cloud sellers can bring to their customers

  • Partner with cloud account teams on solutioning for named accounts, from discovery through technical win

  • Keep our marketplace listings, deployment options, and co-sell technical assets current as the product evolves

  • Enable cloud field and partner teams through workshops, demos, and technical briefings so they can position LangChain without pulling in our engineers for every deal

  • Build and maintain joint technical plans with each cloud provider, turning shared account and industry priorities into a concrete set of reference assets

Marketplace motions with services partners

  • Support systems integrators and resellers when they're part of a cloud deal, such as marketplace private offers transacted through a channel partner or joint deployments on a customer's cloud

  • Give those partners the technical assets they need to scope and deliver LangChain on AWS, GCP, or Azure, using existing reference architectures and implementation guides rather than a standalone enablement program

Partner technical evangelism and feedback

  • Serve as a technical escalation point for complex deployments sourced through cloud partners

  • Represent LangChain at cloud provider events, summits, and joint webinars

  • Gather feedback from cloud partners and the field, and route it back to product and engineering

What we're looking for

7+ years of experience in a technical, partner-facing or customer-facing role such as Partner Engineer, Partner Solutions Architect, Solutions Architect, or Sales Engineer. Experience at or alongside a hyperscaler is a strong plus. We also like former founders and technical leaders, so if you have an unusual background but the right skill set, you're welcome to apply.

Cloud and partner experience

  • Track record of working with AWS, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure partner and field teams to drive co-sell, from joint solution design through technical win

  • Familiarity with cloud marketplace mechanics such as listings, private offers, and channel partner offers, and with hyperscaler co-sell programs

  • Experience enabling a partner's field or technical teams so they can position and deploy a product without depending on you for every deal

  • Comfortable working across engineering, partnerships, and sales at the same time

  • Strong presentation and technical communication skills, able to translate between technical and business stakeholders, including C-suite executives

Agent engineering and development

  • Hands-on experience building with LLM frameworks such as langchain, langgraph, or similar, including RAG patterns and agent architecture

  • Experience designing evaluation frameworks and iterating on prompts and agent behavior based on results

  • Strong Python skills

Cloud architecture and integration

  • Deep working knowledge of at least one of AWS, GCP, or Azure, and familiarity with the other two. Strong background in GCP or Azure preferred.

  • Hands-on experience with cloud AI platforms and managed model services

  • Experience designing integrations, sample repositories, or reference architectures that other teams can pick up and reuse

  • Familiarity with vector stores, tool integration, and API design in agentic systems

Key attributes

  • You build credibility with a cloud provider's technical and field teams and act as their trusted advisor on LangChain

  • Building and evangelizing are both part of the job. You're equally comfortable writing an integration and presenting it at a cloud summit

  • You build assets that scale. A reference architecture should work across every cloud account team, not only the one in front of you

  • You're comfortable with variety. AWS, GCP, and Azure each have their own programs, sellers, and ways of working, and switching between them doesn't throw you off

We design and ship internal product for the GTM organization. AI agents do a growing share of the building: they draft design docs, open changes, and run Salesforce deployments, while humans hold the approval gates. Build capacity — engineers plus the agent bench — sits on this team, and you'll help decide what it works on next.

About the Role:

You'll own the requirements, prioritization, and quality bar for LangChain's Salesforce-centered GTM systems, turning ambiguous revenue-team needs into shipped process and systems changes that scale.

This is not a ticket queue role. You'll be accountable for a small number of high-leverage GTM systems programs at a time: defining the problem, aligning stakeholders, specifying the solution, and ensuring what ships changes how the revenue org operates.

You'll work across Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance in a fast-changing environment where priorities move quickly and influence matters more than reporting lines. The core challenge is operating with authority but not control: aligning teams around tradeoffs as the business changes underneath the plan.

You won't be expected to write production code. You will be expected to write clear enough specifications that engineers and AI coding agents can build from them, and to review the output with enough Salesforce and systems judgment to decide whether it is correct.

Location: San Francisco Bay Area — in office 4 days a week. The people whose processes you're redesigning are in this building, and so are the engineers who build LangGraph.

What You'll Own:

Carry multi-quarter programs

  • Own the Salesforce sales process from lead to close — routing, qualification, territory assignment, and stage progression — driving each initiative from discovery through UAT, change management, and adoption.

  • Be the person stakeholders come to before they file a request, especially when the system was never designed for what the business now needs.

  • Own the intake and prioritization model for hundreds of quarterly GTM systems requests, ensuring the team works on the highest-leverage business problems rather than the loudest tickets.

Own what gets specified and what ships

  • Run discovery and turn ambiguous asks into BRDs, process flows, data models, and acceptance criteria — with a clear problem statement and ROI justification, precise enough to execute without a second conversation.

  • Hold the quality gate: you write the specification, engineers and coding agents write the code, and nothing reaches production without your sign-off.

  • Run vendor evaluations when the right answer is buy, integrate, or replace rather than build.

Protect revenue data integrity

  • Trace anomalies in revenue fields — Net ARR, initial pipeline, lead source — back to the automation, trigger, or integration that wrote them.

  • Own the reconciliation seam between Salesforce, usage-based billing, and cloud-marketplace transactions.

  • Identify which design decisions are load-bearing and which are cosmetic, and catch the downstream failure modes before they reach production.

What Success Looks Like:

In your first 6–12 months, you might:

  • Redesign the lead-to-opportunity process so routing, qualification, and stage progression are measurable, enforceable, and adopted by the field.

  • Create a prioritization model for hundreds of GTM systems requests per quarter, with clear tradeoffs and business rationale.

  • Ship a Salesforce change that improves pipeline hygiene, quote-to-cash accuracy, provisioning reliability, or cloud marketplace reconciliation.

  • Establish a specification and UAT standard that engineers and AI agents can reliably build against.

  • Build enough trust with Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance that stakeholders bring you the problem before they prescribe the solution.

What You'll Need to Be Successful:

Systems and domain depth

  • Domain and tenure — 6–8 years in business systems, sales systems, revenue systems, or GTM systems, with Salesforce as your primary platform throughout.

  • Sales process depth — you've partnered with Sales Ops on the things reps feel every day: territory and account coverage, lead qualification and routing, stage gates, and pipeline and forecast hygiene.

  • Sales systems / RevOps depth — experience across quote-to-cash, CPQ, territory and lead routing, forecasting, or adjacent revenue processes.

  • Technical fluency — you can read a data model, a Flow, and enough Apex to design against what's really there, even though you are not expected to write production code.

Program leadership

  • Program ownership — you've been the single accountable owner, at the working level negotiating the commitments yourself, of a program that spanned four or more functions and changed how a revenue org works day to day.

  • Release risk — you've delivered a program into a core system on a release process you didn't control, where another team's change could break your release.

  • Re-scoping under change — you've re-scoped a program mid-flight because the business changed under it, a sponsor moved, or the original scope no longer matched reality.

  • Holding the line — you've turned down a request with executive backing and kept the relationship; you hold the line when something breaks pricing discipline, a legal constraint, or the architecture, and you arrive with the alternative.

Judgment and communication

  • One tradeoff, two audiences — you write for the reader in front of you, not the one you find easiest: the VP gets the page, the engineer gets the spec.

  • Maximum agency — you find the friction and start the project. You don't wait for a ticket.

  • AI judgment — you give an agent the same brief you'd give a new engineer, and you check its work the same way.

  • Architecture judgment — you know which design calls are load-bearing and which are cosmetic: why a usage event belongs on its own object rather than a field on Account, and how you'd catch that renaming one picklist breaks the provisioning saga before anyone deploys it.

Strong Signals:

None of these is a screen; any one makes you useful faster.

  • You've owned a core Salesforce object domain — Account, Contact, Lead, or Opportunity — through a full redesign.

  • You've traced a Salesforce field into a usage record into a provisioning step, and seen what broke downstream when it moved.

  • You've worked with cloud marketplace operations — AWS or GCP private offers, co-sell, entitlement mapping, metering, and the failure modes when they break.

  • You've worked with usage-based billing systems such as Metronome, Orb, or similar, and CRM↔billing identity reconciliation.

  • You have LangChain or LangGraph experience, or you're excited to learn it here from the people who build it.

Annual salary range: $180-200k USD

Compensation Philosophy:

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

title: Solutions Marketing Manager
description:
About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.

With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.

Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Solutions Marketing Manager to shape how LangChain brings its full platform to priority industries, enterprise buyers, and high-value use cases.

This role sits at the intersection of product and GTM. You’ll translate customer problems into clear solution narratives, repeatable sales plays, campaign themes, and customer-facing assets that help teams understand where LangChain fits in their AI strategy.

You’ll develop industry solutions, use case solutions, and enterprise solution stories for segments such as financial services, healthcare, life sciences, and other priority markets. You’ll work closely with sales, solutions, product, demand generation, field marketing, education, and customer teams to understand what matters in the field, turn those insights into messaging and collateral, and help create programs that support pipeline and revenue generation.

The role covers the full LangChain platform, including Observability & Evaluation, Deployment, Sandboxes, LLM Gateway, Fleet, Engine, and OSS. The goal is to explain how these products work together to help companies build, deploy, monitor, and improve agents in production.

You’ll define the problems we solve for specific audiences, package those into repeatable narratives, and help GTM teams take them to market.

What You’ll Do

Develop industry and use case solutions

  • Build solution narratives for priority industries and enterprise use cases. Initial focus areas include financial services, healthcare, and life sciences, with room to expand based on GTM priorities.

  • Translate customer problems into clear solution stories. You’ll connect LangChain’s platform capabilities to the business, operational, governance, and technical needs of specific audiences.

  • Define repeatable use case messaging. You’ll identify where agents can create value across functions and industries, then turn those patterns into solution briefs, use case pages, campaign assets, sales decks, webinar narratives, and customer-facing content.

  • Build a point of view on enterprise AI adoption. You’ll help explain how companies move from prototypes and isolated experiments to production deployments with the controls, visibility, and evaluation practices they need.

  • Stay close to the market. You’ll synthesize customer conversations, sales feedback, competitive activity, industry trends, and product signals into sharper messaging and GTM recommendations.

Support enterprise GTM motions

  • Partner with sales, solutions, field marketing, demand generation, and customer-facing teams on targeted enterprise campaigns and account motions.

  • Build sales enablement for industry and enterprise conversations. This may include talk tracks, discovery questions, objection handling, use case maps, executive-ready decks, demo narratives, and competitive context.

  • Turn field learnings into reusable sales plays. You’ll work with account teams to understand what resonates with buyers and turn those insights into repeatable messaging, collateral, and campaign programs.

  • Create materials for complex buying committees. You’ll help LangChain speak clearly to technical buyers, AI leaders, IT and security stakeholders, business leaders, and functional teams.

  • Support pipeline and revenue programs. You’ll help connect solution narratives to campaigns, events, webinars, ABM motions, field programs, and sales follow-up.

What You’ll Bring

  • You have 3–6+ years of experience in solutions marketing, enterprise marketing, product marketing, developer marketing, industry marketing, or a related GTM role.

  • You’ve built messaging, collateral, or campaigns around technical products, AI/ML products, developer tools, B2B SaaS, infrastructure, automation, productivity tools, or platform products.

  • You can turn customer problems into clear solution narratives. You know how to move from “what the product does” to “why this matters for this audience, industry, or use case.”

  • You understand enterprise buying motions. You know how to create assets for complex buying committees, regulated industries, sales-led motions, and executive conversations.

  • You’re comfortable with technical products. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you should be able to learn technical concepts quickly, ask good questions, and translate details into customer-facing messaging.

  • You like working with sales and customer-facing teams. You’re interested in what happens in the field and know how to turn that feedback into stronger messaging and enablement.

  • You’re comfortable working across many audiences, including developers, technical buyers, operators, admins, AI leaders, business stakeholders, and nontechnical end users.

  • You can balance strategic thinking with execution. You can define a messaging POV, then build the deck, brief, landing page copy, or sales asset that brings it to life.

  • You’re comfortable with ambiguity and iteration. The market for production-ready AI agents is still being defined, and you’re excited to ship, learn, and improve.

  • You have genuine curiosity about agents, enterprise AI adoption, and how they will change how teams work.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building industry or solutions marketing programs for financial services, healthcare, life sciences, public sector, or other regulated industries.

  • Experience supporting enterprise sales teams through enablement, account-based campaigns, customer-facing storytelling, competitive support, or executive-facing collateral.

  • Familiarity with the LLM, agent, or AI application development ecosystem.

  • Experience with PLG motions, onboarding, activation, lifecycle marketing, or self-serve adoption.

Why Join

  • You’ll help build the solutions marketing motion at LangChain. There is room to shape how we define priority industries, package use cases, support enterprise campaigns, and enable the field.

  • You’ll work on a category that is moving from experimentation to enterprise adoption. Companies are trying to understand where agents can create real value and how to deploy them with control.

  • You’ll join a small, fast-moving team. You’ll get real scope, close access to product and GTM leaders, and the ability to ship meaningful work quickly.

title: Order Management Operations & Automation
description:
About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.

Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

About the role

The ways customers buy from us are multiplying as fast as the business is growing. Enterprise order forms. Private offers through AWS, GCP, and Azure. A self-serve business running on usage-based pricing, with commits, drawdowns, and true-ups behind it. Each one is a distinct path from signature to cash, and each one runs today on some mix of manual steps and automation that grew up with the business.

This role owns what comes next. You'll run order operations end to end - booking, provisioning, invoicing, amendments, and renewals - on a stack we picked deliberately and recently: Salesforce, Metronome for metering and billing, Rillet for ERP. The stack is modern, but the processes on top of it were built to keep up with growth, not designed to scale. Your job is to decide what each one should become: keep it, rebuild it, automate it, or retire it.

Our bias is to invest in systems rather than in a growing queue of manual work, so you'll be setting the automation roadmap at the same time you're operating the function - deciding what a person should touch, what a workflow should handle, and what should never have been a step in the first place. Getting that right is what lets order volume grow by an order of magnitude without ops growing with it.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll own order operations, working closely with Deal Strategy and Operations, GTM Systems, Finance and Accounting, and Enterprise Engineering. Those teams are your partners and much of your build capacity. Bringing them onto one shared order-to-cash roadmap is a core part of the job, and the reason we're hiring someone senior to do it.

What you'll do

  • Own the order-to-cash path end to end: order form intake from Deal Desk, booking in Salesforce, plan and entitlement setup in Metronome, invoicing and revenue recognition through Rillet, and the amendments, true-ups, and renewals that follow

  • Build out cloud marketplace operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure: private offer setup, usage reporting to each marketplace, and reconciling marketplace disbursements back to what we billed. Every new channel launches against defined readiness criteria, so marketplace deals run on the same clean path as direct ones

  • Own self-serve billing operations: usage metering, plan changes, dunning, credits, rebills, refunds, and the escalations behind them

  • Own billing and usage completeness at month-end close. Every order, credit, and metered event is reconciled between Metronome and Rillet before revenue is recognized, not after

  • Partner with Deal Strategy and Product as our pricing evolves. Bring the billing view into pricing and deal-structure decisions early, so new models and non-standard terms can be billed accurately and automated, not handled by hand

  • Set the automation roadmap. Instrument the path, put a number on every place a human touches an order, and decide what gets automated, what gets designed away, and what stays manual on purpose

  • Treat every billing error as a defect: find the root cause and fix the class of problem, not just the one invoice

  • Ship automations yourself where that's fastest, and partner with GTM Systems and Enterprise Engineering where the work belongs in core systems or the product

  • Write the playbook and the controls behind it: approvals, segregation of duties, reconciliations, and exception handling, built so order ops scales through systems rather than headcount and holds up under audit

  • Own three numbers and move them: touchless order rate, signature-to-provisioned cycle time, and billing accuracy

What we're looking for

  • 6+ years in order management, order-to-cash, billing operations, or revenue operations at a B2B SaaS company, including time building the function at an early-stage or fast-scaling one

  • Hands-on fluency with a modern billing and ERP stack. We run Salesforce, Metronome, and Rillet - you should know something comparable well enough to have opinions, and get to depth on ours quickly

  • Real experience with usage-based pricing. Per-seat is straightforward; metered consumption, commits, drawdowns, overages, and true-ups are where order ops gets interesting, and that's most of our business

  • Working knowledge of ASC 606 and month-end close. You don't need to be an accountant, but you should know what Revenue Accounting needs from billing data and why

  • Cloud marketplace experience (AWS, GCP, or Azure private offers), or a track record of getting deep on a system like that fast

  • A history of automating your own job. We'll ask you to walk us through a manual process you deleted: what it cost before, what you built, and what it costs now

  • The ability to build alignment across teams with different priorities and get to a decision, without relying on org authority

  • Comfort shipping a v0 earlier than feels comfortable, then iterating with real feedback

Nice to have

  • SQL, Python, or low-code tooling in your own hands rather than on someone else's backlog

  • Experience building agents or LLM workflows for internal operations. We'd like to run more of our own back office on the LangSmith Platform, wherever it's the right tool and meets the same accuracy bar as the rest of order-to-cash

  • Audit prep or SOX readiness experience

About the role

The ways customers buy from us are multiplying as fast as the business is growing. Enterprise order forms. Private offers through AWS, GCP, and Azure. A self-serve business running on usage-based pricing, with commits, drawdowns, and true-ups behind it. Each one is a distinct path from signature to cash, and each one runs today on some mix of manual steps and automation that grew up with the business.

This role owns what comes next. You'll run order operations end to end - booking, provisioning, invoicing, amendments, and renewals - on a stack we picked deliberately and recently: Salesforce, Metronome for metering and billing, Rillet for ERP. The stack is modern, but the processes on top of it were built to keep up with growth, not designed to scale. Your job is to decide what each one should become: keep it, rebuild it, automate it, or retire it.

Our bias is to invest in systems rather than in a growing queue of manual work, so you'll be setting the automation roadmap at the same time you're operating the function - deciding what a person should touch, what a workflow should handle, and what should never have been a step in the first place. Getting that right is what lets order volume grow by an order of magnitude without ops growing with it.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll own order operations, working closely with Deal Strategy and Operations, GTM Systems, Finance and Accounting, and Enterprise Engineering. Those teams are your partners and much of your build capacity. Bringing them onto one shared order-to-cash roadmap is a core part of the job, and the reason we're hiring someone senior to do it.

What you'll do

  • Own the order-to-cash path end to end: order form intake from Deal Desk, booking in Salesforce, plan and entitlement setup in Metronome, invoicing and revenue recognition through Rillet, and the amendments, true-ups, and renewals that follow

  • Build out cloud marketplace operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure: private offer setup, usage reporting to each marketplace, and reconciling marketplace disbursements back to what we billed. Every new channel launches against defined readiness criteria, so marketplace deals run on the same clean path as direct ones

  • Own self-serve billing operations: usage metering, plan changes, dunning, credits, rebills, refunds, and the escalations behind them

  • Own billing and usage completeness at month-end close. Every order, credit, and metered event is reconciled between Metronome and Rillet before revenue is recognized, not after

  • Partner with Deal Strategy and Product as our pricing evolves. Bring the billing view into pricing and deal-structure decisions early, so new models and non-standard terms can be billed accurately and automated, not handled by hand

  • Set the automation roadmap. Instrument the path, put a number on every place a human touches an order, and decide what gets automated, what gets designed away, and what stays manual on purpose

  • Treat every billing error as a defect: find the root cause and fix the class of problem, not just the one invoice

  • Ship automations yourself where that's fastest, and partner with GTM Systems and Enterprise Engineering where the work belongs in core systems or the product

  • Write the playbook and the controls behind it: approvals, segregation of duties, reconciliations, and exception handling, built so order ops scales through systems rather than headcount and holds up under audit

  • Own three numbers and move them: touchless order rate, signature-to-provisioned cycle time, and billing accuracy

What we're looking for

  • 6+ years in order management, order-to-cash, billing operations, or revenue operations at a B2B SaaS company, including time building the function at an early-stage or fast-scaling one

  • Hands-on fluency with a modern billing and ERP stack. We run Salesforce, Metronome, and Rillet - you should know something comparable well enough to have opinions, and get to depth on ours quickly

  • Real experience with usage-based pricing. Per-seat is straightforward; metered consumption, commits, drawdowns, overages, and true-ups are where order ops gets interesting, and that's most of our business

  • Working knowledge of ASC 606 and month-end close. You don't need to be an accountant, but you should know what Revenue Accounting needs from billing data and why

  • Cloud marketplace experience (AWS, GCP, or Azure private offers), or a track record of getting deep on a system like that fast

  • A history of automating your own job. We'll ask you to walk us through a manual process you deleted: what it cost before, what you built, and what it costs now

  • The ability to build alignment across teams with different priorities and get to a decision, without relying on org authority

  • Comfort shipping a v0 earlier than feels comfortable, then iterating with real feedback

Nice to have

  • SQL, Python, or low-code tooling in your own hands rather than on someone else's backlog

  • Experience building agents or LLM workflows for internal operations. We'd like to run more of our own back office on the LangSmith Platform, wherever it's the right tool and meets the same accuracy bar as the rest of order-to-cash

  • Audit prep or SOX readiness experience

title: Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack
description:
About the Role

Hinge Health uses software, including AI, to deliver care for joint and muscle health, and has expanded into pelvic health, migraine, and digestive health. We partner with employers and health plans to provide this care at scale, improving members' quality of life and reducing healthcare costs.

The Visits team owns scheduling for all of Hinge Health, along with the visit experience in our member app and in the tools our care team uses. That covers HingeSelect (our network of specialists, in-person providers, and surgeons) and visits in every Hinge Health program, from physical therapy to migraine and GI care.

Next, we want every visit at Hinge Health to feel like the best doctor's office you've been to, minus the clipboards and hold music. Members should be able to find the right visit, book it in a few taps, show up prepared, and afterward see what happened and what to do next, whether the visit was by video or in person. Providers should be able to act on a visit without leaving our tools, from referrals to labs to prescriptions. Each visit leaves a structured record that shapes the next one, from the follow-up booking to AI experiences that help members act on their care.

As a Senior Software Engineer on Visits, you'll own projects across that experience, from technical design through launch, while visit volume grows many times over. Your strength might be mobile, web, or the services behind them. There's central work here for each, and nobody is expected to be an expert in all three. It's 0-to-1 work at a startup's pace, backed by the resources and data of a market leader.

What You'll Accomplish

  • Lead projects from ambiguity to launch: Partner with product, design, and clinical teams to turn loosely defined goals into sequenced plans that several engineers can build against, then ship them at a high, steady pace.

  • Extend the scheduling platform: Grow the system every Hinge Health visit is booked through to support more specialties, more providers, and real-time booking with outside provider networks, while keeping every booking correct as volume climbs.

  • Close the loop after each visit: Build encounters, our record of what happened at each visit, along with the visit history and after-visit summaries that members see in the app, providers work from, and our AI experiences build on.

  • Bring new specialties onto one platform: Launch specialties like migraine and GI care on shared visit infrastructure, so adding the next one is mostly configuration rather than a rebuild.

  • Run what you ship: Define SLOs for the systems you own, roll out launches and migrations safely, lead incident response through to root-cause fixes, and protect member health data in every design and code review.

  • Raise the engineering bar: Write design docs for key decisions, give high-signal code reviews, and mentor earlier-career engineers. Use AI tools to multiply your own output and help teammates do the same.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related technical field.

  • 3+ years of non-internship, full-time professional software engineering experience.

  • Professional experience with at least one of the languages or frameworks we use: TypeScript, Go, React Native, or React.

  • Experience leading a production feature or system from technical design through launch, working closely with product and design partners.

  • Professional experience using AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Claude Code) in your day-to-day engineering work.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building products 0-to-1 in a rapid-growth environment, using data and experiments to decide what to build next.

  • Experience shipping product features powered by LLMs or agentic workflows to production.

  • Experience building scheduling, booking, or marketplace systems at scale.

  • Experience with clinical data and healthcare integrations, such as FHIR or HL7 data, EHRs, claims, labs, or pharmacies.

  • Familiarity with our core stack: React Native, React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, GraphQL, Go, gRPC, Postgres, Temporal, Kafka, Docker, and AWS.

  • Experience in healthcare, insurance tech, or other high-compliance industries (HIPAA, SOC 2).


Beware of Phishing Attempts: We've noticed an increase in phishing where fraudsters impersonate employees and send fake job offers to steal sensitive information. We'll never ask for financial details during the hiring process and only use "@hingehealth.com" emails.   • Familiarity with distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, or scalable architectures

  • Experience with healthcare technology or regulated environments

  • Experience with Agile development practices

title: Staff Software Engineer, Enrollment & Onboarding
description:
The Opportunity

Enrollment and Onboarding is the front door to Hinge Health. Every member's care starts here: registering, answering the clinical questionnaire that determines eligibility and program fit, getting accepted, and then calibrating their first exercise therapy so day one feels made for them. The pod owns that whole path, on web and in our React Native app, for every program we offer, from chronic and acute musculoskeletal (MSK) pain to pelvic health and migraine.

This stretch is where members decide whether Hinge Health is for them. Small improvements in how quickly and confidently someone gets from sign-up to their first session compound into large gains in how many people actually start care.

As the Staff Software Engineer on this pod, you'll be the technical lead for a team of six engineers, working full-stack across NestJS services, a GraphQL backend-for-frontend (BFF), React web, and React Native. The system is a clinical intake pipeline and a server-driven mobile experience at the same time, and you'll set its architecture. Day to day you'll partner with Product, Design, Data Science, and User Research to turn what we learn about members into a better first week.

What You'll Accomplish

  • Own the enrollment and onboarding architecture: Set technical direction for the services and clients that take a member from registration through questionnaire, acceptance, and baseline calibration. Keep it coherent as programs, surfaces, and clinical rules multiply.

  • Build durable, observable member workflows: Design the multi-step, long-running orchestration behind enrollment on Temporal, with the idempotency, retry, and failure semantics a clinical intake flow demands.

  • Ship native, server-driven experiences: Lead the mobile and web experience for clinical questionnaires and calibration. Render data-driven survey and layout definitions in React Native and React so clinical and product teams can change content without an app release.

  • Turn intake signals into a personalized start: Connect what we learn about a member during enrollment to their first exercise therapy session, working with Data Science and partner teams so onboarding feels calibrated to the person.

  • Move the funnel: Instrument and experiment on the enrollment and onboarding funnel with Product, Design, and User Research. You'll be measured on accepted members who reach their first session.

  • Retire legacy safely: Lead migrations off legacy systems while they stay in production, and hold the line on quality, testing, observability, and protected health information (PHI) handling across the pod's repositories.

  • Lead through influence: Mentor the team's senior and mid-level engineers and raise the bar through design and code review. Represent the pod technically with partner teams across accounts, mobile platform, care, and data.

  • Participate in the team’s weekly on-call rotation, helping ensure the reliability and timely support of the systems we build.

Who You Are

  • A full-stack owner: You've shipped and operated user-facing flows end to end, from React Native or React through the services behind them, and you're comfortable moving the boundary between client and server when the product needs it.

  • A systems thinker about state: You've built or run durable, multi-step workflows in production and you know what it takes to make them correct, from retries, idempotency, and versioning to what happens to the user when a step fails.

  • A builder across horizons: You're equally at home defining new architecture and hardening a legacy path that still serves real members.

  • A force multiplier: You raise everyone around you through mentorship, review, and standards that reduce friction.

  • A partner across disciplines: You work closely with Product, Design, Data Science, and User Research, and you can explain a technical tradeoff to a clinician as clearly as to an engineer.

  • Outcome-driven: You measure your work by what changed for members.

Basic Qualifications

  • 5+ years of non-internship, full-time professional software engineering experience

  • Led the design and delivery of complex user-facing products end to end, across mobile or web clients and the backend services behind them

  • 3+ years of TypeScript/JavaScript across the stack: Node.js (NestJS or similar) on the backend, React Native or React on the frontend

  • Production experience with durable workflow or long-running state orchestration (Temporal, Cadence, Step Functions, or a state machine you built and kept correct)

  • 2+ years mentoring or leading other engineers and working with partners in product, design, and data

Preferred Qualifications

  • NestJS, GraphQL, PostgreSQL, Kafka, and Temporal in production

  • Server-driven UI or configuration-driven presentation layers on mobile: dynamic forms, survey engines, conditional logic defined in data rather than code

  • Signup, onboarding, intake, or application flows where completion rate was your metric

  • Migrated or decomposed a legacy system while it remained in production

  • Experimentation on critical-path product surfaces: A/B tests, feature flags, funnel instrumentation

  • Healthcare or another regulated, data-sensitive domain, including PHI constraints on logging and storage

  • Track record as a Staff-level individual contributor who shapes direction without direct reports
