title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, API Platform)
description:
Perplexity API Platform

Perplexity innovates at the frontier of AI infrastructure, search, and orchestration to serve the world's most discerning users. The Perplexity API Platform brings our technology to the world's most discerning developers. From exabyte-scale knowledge indexes to codegen-first agent runtimes, the building blocks behind Perplexity's applications are some of the most battle-tested AI systems in the industry.

We believe these same building blocks can and should power the aspirations of builders everywhere. It's one thing to solve planet-scale retrieval, long-horizon orchestration, and other foundational AI challenges within a single product ecosystem. The true measure of success is to turn those solutions into elegant APIs that delight developers and agents alike. Our API Platform delivers frontier intelligence to thousands of customers: startups, trillion-dollar enterprises, U.S. and allied governments, and everyone in between.

We've achieved incredible scale, yet we're just getting started. Join us to build tools for curious minds.

About this role

Perplexity is seeking strong engineers with a passion for delivering frontier intelligence and infrastructure to developers. Our company builds technology that reshapes how people search, reason, and interact with the world around them. Week after week, we observe increasing demand for programmatic interfaces to that technology. The API Platform engineering team is charged with designing, implementing, and scaling these interfaces.

As a member of our team, you'll work on an eclectic portfolio spanning distributed systems, performance optimization, agent orchestration, and frontier topics that often change with each passing month. Throughout this work, you'll prioritize great developer and agent experience alike. You'll also define technical strategy for how we scale to meet compounding growth exponentials (number of customers, agents per customer, compute/retrieval per agent, etc.).

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate mission-critical APIs that provide our customers the building blocks for frontier intelligence.

  • Own and evolve the API gateway and routing layer: authentication, authorization, rate limiting and quotas, usage metering, and request routing across heterogeneous upstream services.

  • Build the paved road for API services: standardized service scaffolding, container builds, CI/CD, Kubernetes and Helm deployment, and progressive rollouts with fast rollback, so a new API product goes from idea to production in days, not weeks.

  • Build API governance into the platform: contract-first schemas, breaking-change detection in CI, versioning and deprecation workflows, and SDKs and documentation generated from a single source of truth.

  • Unify cross-cutting capabilities (billing and usage, rate limiting, organization and identity settings, analytics and observability) so every API product gets them by default instead of rebuilding them.

  • Ensure low latency and high throughput through aggressive performance optimization (including on upstream systems).

  • Harden system security and reliability across heterogeneous compute environments, and operate what you build: SLOs, on-call, and incident response.

  • Collaborate across teams to bring novel frontier capabilities into the API Platform, and partner with infrastructure teams on compute, networking, secrets, and security.

  • Continually reimagine the customer needs of tomorrow (and the architectures to serve those needs), while faithfully serving the customer workloads of today.

  • Uphold engineering excellence through design reviews, code quality, and internal documentation.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of backend engineering experience with Python, Go, or Rust, including significant time building platforms or infrastructure used by other engineering teams.

  • Strong understanding of high-traffic API design: schema evolution & versioning, idempotency, authentication patterns, rate limiting, and performance tuning.

  • Hands-on experience building and operating API gateways, reverse proxies, or routing layers: authentication and authorization, rate limiting and quotas, request routing, traffic shaping, and per-request observability.

  • Experience building API governance tooling: contract-first API design, breaking-change detection and API linting in CI, versioning and deprecation workflows, and SDKs and documentation generated from the contract.

  • Platform depth across the build and deploy path: you have owned CI/CD pipelines, container builds and base images, infrastructure as code, and progressive delivery (canary or blue-green) on a major cloud.

  • A track record of owning a platform end to end: identifying the need, designing it, aligning the teams that depend on it, shipping it, and operating it, while raising the engineering bar for the teams building on it.

  • Strong customer empathy and product sense, ensuring the APIs you build are ergonomic, well-documented, and easy to adopt for developers and agents alike.

Strong plus:

  • Experience with modern AI APIs (including latency tuning, streaming, model orchestration, emerging technical standards).

  • Usage-based billing and metering systems, multi-tenant organization and identity models, and usage analytics pipelines.

  • Observability for API platforms: structured logging pipelines, metrics, tracing, and SLO tooling.

title: Recruiting Coordinator
description:
We're looking for a dynamic, highly organized Recruiting Coordinator to help us scale our team without ever compromising on experience. This is a high-velocity role at the heart of our hiring engine. You'll keep dozens of moving parts in sync, bring order to ambiguity, and make every candidate and hiring partner feel like they're our only priority. If you thrive when the path isn't fully mapped out, move fast without dropping details, and genuinely care about how people are treated, you'll do great here.

 

What You'll Do

  • Own the end-to-end candidate experience, making every interaction from first touch to final decision, feel seamless, human, and high-touch

  • Coordinate and schedule interviews across complex calendars, time zones, and competing priorities, keeping things moving at speed

  • Serve as a trusted partner to recruiters, interviewers, and hiring managers, anticipating needs, communicating proactively, and making their jobs easier

  • Operate independently in ambiguity: spot gaps, make judgment calls, and create structure where none exists yet

  • Identify, initiate, and drive projects that improve and scale our recruiting processes as the team grows

  • Manage logistics, administrative tasks, and ad-hoc recruiting support with accuracy and urgency

  • Continuously look for ways to raise the bar on both the external candidate experience and the internal stakeholder experience

 

What You Bring

  • 2–4 years of experience as a Recruiting Coordinator, ideally in a fast-paced or high-growth environment

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity. You take initiative, make decisions with incomplete information, and don't wait to be told what to do

  • A natural high-velocity operator who moves quickly without sacrificing accuracy or attention to detail

  • Exceptional organizational skills and the ability to juggle multiple priorities simultaneously without losing the thread

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with proactive, clear, and warm follow-through

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively, adapting fast in a rapidly changing startup environment

  • Proficiency with various ATSs (Ashby preferred)

title: Go-to-Market Recruiter
description:
About the Role

We are seeking an experienced GTM Recruiter to partner closely with our GTM leadership team and drive a best-in-class hiring experience across our go-to-market org. The ideal candidate will have a proven track record as a full-cycle GTM recruiter in high-growth environments, with deep experience hiring Account Executives, Customer Success Managers, Support, and the broader sales team. Success in this role requires strong stakeholder management skills, creative AI-augmented sourcing strategies, and the ability to deliver high-quality hires in a fast-paced startup setting.

Beyond the expected; this role requires both a superior level of operational wizardry; and a mastery of storytelling, steeped in a comprehensive understanding of the AI market and the GTM talent landscape. title: Social Media Manager
description:
Perplexity is looking for a Social Media Manager to expand how Perplexity shows up online. You'll run the channels day to day, writing posts, setting strategy, scaling our accounts, and writing for leadership and the team, working closely with our Communications and marketing team, product managers, and engineers.

This is a hands-on role. You'll write most of what goes out yourself. Excellent judgement and high taste are required. The role is mostly Instagram with some community initiatives like Reddit, and interacting with our developer audiences.

Responsibilities

  • Run social channels day to day. Maintain our brand and product accounts across all channels. This includes writing social copy, planning content, and managing engagement.

  • Set the social strategy. Decide and execute how we grow each account, what we post where, and how we measure it.

  • Scale our team accounts. Help employees post in our voice and grow our presence across platforms.

  • Build and moderate community. Engage on Reddit and in developer communities, and represent Perplexity where our users already are.

  • Adapt and ship fast. Partner with Comms and marketing, PM’s, founders, and engineers in a fast-paced launch environment.

Qualifications

  • 3+ years running social for a brand, ideally tech and AI.

  • You can write. Send us posts you wrote that performed and tell us why they worked.

  • Native fluency on Instagram and LinkedIn, with a track record of growing an account.

  • Demonstrated experience being entrusted with a brand voice

  • You know how to write for different audiences and platforms, and adjust the voice for each.

  • Comfortable in a fast launch cycle where the plan changes often

  • You've written on behalf of leadership or other voices.

title: Internal Communications Manager
description:
Perplexity is seeking an Internal Communications Manager to build that function from the ground up. You will own how information moves through Perplexity. You will be responsible for what Perplexity employees think, feel, know, and do. This is a 0→1 role with executive exposure from day one.

If you believe internal comms is a strategic function and want to shape how an n(1) company talks to itself, this role is for you.

Responsibilities

  • Listen and learn across the company. Understand what’s happening, how, and why in order to make sound recommendations on what should be amplified or addressed.

  • Run all-hands and executive content. Planning, execution, measurement, and evolution.

  • Internal storytelling. Turn strategy, launches, and hard decisions into messages that bring clarity to every team.

  • Be the signal in noise. Cut through Slack sprawl. Establish the channels, cadences, and norms that keep a fast company informed without drowning it.

  • Own change management. Deliver hard and easy news with equal clarity and candor. Earn trust for the message and the messenger..

  • Protect the culture. Words set the tone. Make sure ours sound like us as we grow.

  • Measure what matters. Perplexity is a high-velocity high-humility organization.

  • Partner across the company. Work with every team, brief executives directly, and earn standing as a truth-teller.

Qualifications

  • 6+ years in internal, executive, or corporate communications, ideally inside a high-growth technology company.

  • A builder, not a maintainer. You've stood a function up, not just kept one running.

  • World-class writing and editing. You can ghostwrite for an executive, draft an all-hands, or defuse a sensitive announcement in any voice or format.

  • Proven change-management instincts. You've delivered complex news to a whole company and kept trust intact.

  • Sharp judgment under pressure. You decide fast, say the hard thing kindly, and hold the line on quality on launch day.

  • Comfort with executives who hold a strong vision. You can advise, challenge, and make recommendations to senior leaders without flinching.

  • Deep familiarity with the rules of corporate comms, and a clear point of view on which ones to break and when.

  • Comfort using AI tools in your workflow, and the ability to say exactly where and how you use them.

  • A passion for the truth well-told

title: Senior Editor
description:
Perplexity is seeking a Senior Editor to lead the quality and velocity of everything we publish. Our content spans a range of audiences, channels, and objectives. You will set the editorial bar for excellence and make every writer around you measurably better.

If you treat a clunky sentence and a sprawling launch narrative as the same kind of craft, take pride in language without being precious about deadlines, and want to build a world-class editorial function from the ground up, this role is for you.

Responsibilities

  • Own editorial quality end to end.

  • Reject mediocrity.

  • Demand clarity. Ensure accuracy.

  • Be Perplexity. Evolve and enforce our voice. Everything we ship should sound like we shipped it.

  • Be accountable. Hold objective authority in a sea of subjective opinions.

  • Plan and manage the editorial calendar. Run prioritization and production for a fast-moving pipeline in a high-growth environment.

  • Edit at every level. Player-coach plus team owner and stadium sponsor. Move fluidly from high-level editorial vision to developmental editing to line-level copy editing. Deliver feedback that makes the writing and the writer better.

  • Mentor, elevate, and attract excellent writers. Earn the respect of strong writers by making them stronger.

  • Make sense of things. Make sense to people.

  • Build the editorial system. Evolve and own the style guides and workflows.

  • Work productively across the company. Everyone wants content, and you’re the content.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years in editing, writing, or editorial leadership, with a body of published or edited work that demonstrates exceptional command of language.

  • High flexibility of tone and mind. You must be able to demonstrate an ability to adapt styles and voices for different channels or audiences.

  • High competence throughout the editorial stack: developmental editing, copy editing, content planning, and managing production.

  • A demonstrated track record of mentoring writers and improving the quality of a team's output, not just your own.

  • Exceptional ability to learn.

  • Refined judgment on all matters of structure, argument, and voice

  • A proven eye for narrative in messy, ambiguous, or highly technical material.

  • Deep familiarity with the rules of grammar, style, and storytelling.

  • Enough experience in the bullet above that you have a clear perspective on which rules you intend to break and when.

  • Comfort using AI tools and the ability to articulate exactly where and how you incorporate them into your workflows.

  • A passion for the truth well-told.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Integrations)
description:
Description

In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. As an engineer on the Integrations team at Perplexity, you’ll define the technical direction of products that connect Perplexity to workflows across multiple verticals and work full-stack to build these applied AI systems. You’ll move quickly, owning outcomes end-to-end, and building useful products people reach for every day.

Why Perplexity is different

title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Enterprise AI Products)
description:
About the Role

The Enterprise AI Products team builds products that make AI part of how teams work together, not just a tool people use on their own.   • Work directly with customers and internal teams to identify high-impact problems, validate ideas through rapid prototyping, and turn successful use cases into scalable, reusable products.

  • Own products end to end, from problem definition and technical design through full-stack implementation, launch, and production reliability.

  • Measure and improve activation, repeat usage, and workflow completion, using customer feedback and product experiments to drive sustained AI adoption.

  • Partner with Product, Design, Sales, and engineering teams to turn customer needs and emerging AI capabilities into reliable product experiences.

Qualifications

  • 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of building and shipping production products end to end.

  • Hands-on experience shipping applications with LLMs or AI agents, with good judgment about their capabilities and limitations and experience improving product quality through evaluation and user feedback.

  • Strong software engineering and system design skills, with proficiency in Python or Go and the ability to work across backend services and user-facing applications.

  • Strong product judgment and the ability to translate ambiguous customer needs into simple, effective product experiences for users with different levels of technical expertise.

  • Comfort working directly with customers, moving quickly between discovery and implementation, and owning problems without a fully defined specification.

  • Experience with enterprise, growth, or collaboration products is a plus.

title: Brand Designer, Growth
description:
We're looking for a Growth Brand Designer to sit at the intersection of brand craft and growth performance. You'll be the designer who makes Perplexity's highest-volume, highest-leverage marketing surfaces — paid ads, social, lifecycle email, and campaign assets — look unmistakably Perplexity while actually moving the numbers.

This is a shipping role, but it's equally a thinking role. Strategic concepting is a big part of the job: you'll sit with the Growth team as an ideator — generating campaign concepts, testing hypotheses, and shaping the creative strategy behind the work — not just executing briefs handed to you. The ideas you bring to the table matter as much as the assets you ship.

You'll produce a steady stream of ad and campaign creative across formats and channels, then work with Growth to read the results and iterate. You care about conversion and craft in equal measure: you'd never ship an off-brand asset to win a test, and you'd never hide behind polish when the data says a concept isn't working.

You'll report into the Brand/Creative Studio team and work closely with Growth, Product Marketing, Brand, and our motion and web designers.

What you'll do

  • Drive strategic concepting for growth campaigns — bring original ideas, angles, and creative territories to the table, and shape the brief rather than just receiving it

  • Operate as a true ideation partner to the Growth team: co-develop campaign strategy, propose test hypotheses, and pitch concepts that open up new creative directions

  • Own the design of growth creative end-to-end — paid social and display ads, campaign assets, and lifecycle email — from concept to shipped asset

  • Design for volume and velocity: build variant sets, test hypotheses, and iterate on winners with the Growth team using real performance data

  • Turn product launches and GTM campaigns into ad creative that lands on every channel it runs — static, animated, and everything in between

  • Build and maintain scalable ad and email templates so high-frequency asset production stays fast and on-brand

  • Partner with Brand to keep visual consistency across every growth touchpoint as our brand system evolves

  • Collaborate with our motion designer and web designer so campaigns feel cohesive from the first ad impression to the landing page

  • Bring a strong point of view on what makes performance creative great — and push back when a "best practice" would cheapen the brand

What we're looking for

  • A strong portfolio of growth and brand design work — paid ads, social campaigns, lifecycle email, campaign systems — that shows both craft and results

  • Proven strategic concepting ability: you can show campaigns where the idea was yours, not just the execution, and articulate the thinking behind them

  • Excellent visual design skills with a clear sense of brand, typography, layout, and composition

  • Hands-on experience designing performance creative at a consumer or prosumer tech company, including working directly with growth or performance marketing teams

  • Fluency reading creative performance data (CTR, conversion, hook rates) and translating it into design decisions

  • Ability to work fast, manage a high volume of deliverables across channels, and iterate quickly without dropping the quality bar

  • Fluency in Figma and the Adobe Creative Suite

  • An instinct for building repeatable systems — templates, variant frameworks, asset kits — rather than one-off files

  • 5+ years of industry experience

Nice to have

  • Motion design skills — animated ads, short-form video for social, or After Effects fluency

  • Familiarity with ad platform specs and constraints (Meta, Google, TikTok, X, YouTube) and how they shape creative decisions

  • Experience using AI-assisted design and image-generation workflows to scale creative output

  • Copywriting instincts — you can tighten a headline when there's no writer in the room

title: Growth Manager, Enterprise Lifecycle
description:
Perplexity is seeking an Enterprise Product Growth Manager to own the full nurture and engagement engine for our enterprise and business buyers — from the first outbound touch through closed-won and into expansion. You will partner closely with Demand Generation, Sales, Product Marketing, and Revenue Operations to move accounts through every stage of the funnel, and you will build the AI-native tooling that makes those programs run.

We are not looking for someone to operate yesterday's marketing stack. If you are the kind of marketer who writes their own SQL, prototypes their own agents, and treats every flow as something to automate rather than execute by hand — this role was written for you.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Develop and own Perplexity's end-to-end enterprise lifecycle user states — outbound nurture, MQL-to-SQL conversion, opportunity acceleration, post-sale activation, expansion, and renewal — with direct accountability for pipeline created, pipeline progressed, and revenue retained.

  • Build and operate AI-native lifecycle tooling — agents that segment audiences from the warehouse, personalize copy at the account and persona level, choose channel and send time, QA before send, and read out results — replacing manual work in our stack wherever it appears.

  • Design and run multi-channel nurture across email, in-product, notifications, Slack, and emerging surfaces, tailored to enterprise personas with content tied to where each account sits in the funnel.

  • Partner with Demand Generation and Sales on top-of-funnel outbound: turn cold and intent-signaled accounts into engaged conversations, and instrument the handoffs that move them to opportunity.

  • Own post-sale lifecycle: admin onboarding, end-user activation, feature adoption, at-risk intervention, and expansion plays that grow seats and ARR inside existing accounts.

  • Run every program as an experiment. Define the hypothesis, the control, the primary metric, and the readout. Kill what doesn't work, double down on what does.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

  • 7+ years in product growth, lifecycle, or growth marketing at a fast-paced startup, with a proven track record of moving activation, retention, and revenue metrics — including enterprise pipeline.

  • Experience owning growth end-to-end across the full user journey — from first touch and activation through expansion, monetization, and win-back. You've built growth loops and lifecycle programs that turn signups into engaged users and engaged users into revenue.

  • Deep understanding of audience segmentation. You think natively in personas, behavioral triggers, lifecycle stages, and product signals, and you know how to translate that into journeys, experiments, and in-product experiences that actually convert.

  • Great taste. You know how to craft copy and experiences that resonate across email, push, and in-product surfaces — for end users, admins, and executives alike — and you can tell the difference between a polished experience and a generic one at a glance.

  • Experience and deep interest in building homegrown AI-driven growth engines — programmatic personalization, agentic workflows, and rapid experimentation platforms to scale yourself.

  • Builder mentality toward tooling. You don't just operate the modern growth stack (Omni, HubSpot, Loops, Intercom, or equivalents) — you extend it. You've built your own internal tools, scripts, and automated systems to close gaps off-the-shelf software can't, and you'd rather automate a workflow than run it manually twice.

  • Comfortable with SQL. You can pull your own cohorts, validate your own segments, and read a dashboard without waiting on a data analyst.

  • Operates at high velocity. You ship daily, iterate weekly, and thrive in fast-paced, early-stage environments where processes are still being defined. Urgency is a default setting, not a mode you switch into.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Secure Intelligence Institute)
description:
Perplexity is seeking energetic researchers and engineers to join our Secure Intelligence Institute (SII), Perplexity's flagship research center for advancing security, privacy, and trust in frontier intelligence. SII’s goals are to advance frontier AI security research, translate those advances into concrete improvements in Perplexity's systems, and share knowledge and resources that strengthen the broader AI ecosystem.

As a member of SII, you'll conduct original and impactful research on improving the security and privacy of frontier intelligence systems. Your goal will be to conduct research that is not only rigorous in theory, but practical enough to improve the systems people rely on every day. This work will be informed by the realities of operating general-purpose AI systems used by millions of people and thousands of enterprises, and you'll be expected to translate both your own research and advances from the broader community to practical improvements that protect and defend Perplexity's users.

Responsibilities

  • Develop threat models for emerging attack surfaces in AI-native products, including browser, search, and autonomous agents.

  • Identify and analyze security and privacy threats across AI systems, infrastructure, and user-facing products.

  • Develop novel defenses, mitigations, and detection mechanisms for security and privacy in AI-native products.

  • Build security evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, and datasets to measure the effectiveness of different defense mechanisms.

  • Partner with Perplexity’s Security Engineering team to translate state of the art research into shipped security features and hardened system architectures.

  • Collaborate with top-tier academic and industry researchers in SII's external research network.

  • Publish findings at premier venues and contribute to the broader security research community.

Qualifications

  • Hold a PhD (or equivalent research experience) in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, with a primary focus on security and/or privacy.

  • Experience publishing at top security conferences (IEEE S&P, USENIX Security, ACM CCS, NDSS) demonstrating original, impactful research contributions.

  • Deep expertise in one or more of: security of agentic systems, systems security, web and applications security, program analysis, and software security.

  • Proficiency in Python (bonus points for TypeScript, Go, and/or Rust).

  • Ability to operate with high independence, willing to dive in and take ownership, and comfortable in a fast-paced environment where research directly informs product.

  • Clear and concise communcation, translating complex attack narratives into actionable insights for engineering and leadership.

title: AI Strategist, Legal
description:
Perplexity is an AI-powered answer engine founded in December 2022 and growing rapidly as one of the world's leading AI platforms. Perplexity has raised over $1B in venture investment from some of the world's most visionary and successful leaders, including Elad Gil, Daniel Gross, Jeff Bezos, Accel, IVP, NEA, NVIDIA, Samsung, and many more. Our objective is to build accurate, trustworthy AI that powers decision-making for people and assistive AI wherever decisions are being made.

Throughout human history, change and innovation have always been driven by curious people. Today, curious people use Perplexity to answer more than 780 million queries every month—a number that's growing rapidly for one simple reason: everyone can be curious.


About the Role

Perplexity is building the AI platform for professional legal work: Perplexity Computer, our agentic platform that navigates tools, completes multi-step workflows, and connects to the case law, statutes, filings, contracts, and internal documents that legal professionals already rely on, and our API Platform, which powers search, retrieval, and automation across structured and unstructured legal data.

At the center of this is our Applied AI / Forward Deployed motion: we work closely with law firms and in-house legal teams to distill their core legal processes and embed them into bespoke solutions built on our platform. That means sitting with partners, associates, and counsel to understand how they research, review, draft, and advise, then translating those workflows into custom skills, agents, and connector configurations that run inside their daily process—and feeding what we learn back into the product so it compounds across customers.

As an AI Strategist on our Applied AI team focused on the legal vertical, you are the subject matter expert who makes this real for legal professionals. This is a commercial and sales engineering role: you will own strategic customer engagements end to end—leading discovery, defining what to build, demonstrating frontier capabilities against real legal workflows, and driving deployments from first conversation through production and expansion. You are part customer owner, part product strategist, part sales engineer—fluent in both the language of the practice group and the language of the platform.

Responsibilities

Own strategic legal engagements

  • Lead discovery with law firms and in-house legal departments: what matters to the practice, what problems they are solving, and which workflows are worth automating

  • Define scope—what is the right thing to build—and own success metrics, pilot design, and commercial structure

  • Drive deployment and rollout across practice groups and legal departments, with real revenue responsibility alongside Sales

Be the demo and technical proof engine

  • Build and deliver compelling, workflow-specific demonstrations: legal research, contract review and analysis, due diligence, drafting, deposition and discovery summarization, regulatory monitoring

  • Prototype workflows, skills, and connector configurations hands-on in Perplexity Computer and the API Platform to prove value in the customer's own use cases

  • Run pilots and evaluations that hold up to scrutiny from skeptical partners and general counsel

Bring domain judgment to the product

  • Translate how practice groups, legal departments, and legal ops teams actually work into product, connector, and data-partnership priorities

  • Assess whether we have the right research, contract, docket, and document-management integrations to serve each legal segment—and drive the roadmap where we do not

  • Codify repeatable engagement patterns: discovery templates, practice-specific reference workflows, demo libraries, and deployment playbooks

Operate as the commercial lead

  • Own senior relationships with partners, general counsel, and legal-innovation leaders; move engagements through qualification, scoping, proposal, pricing, legal, and close

  • Create urgency, write crisp follow-ups, and know when to push and when to wait

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of direct experience practicing law at a leading firm or in-house—litigation, transactional, or regulatory—or in legal ops / legal innovation with deep workflow exposure; you have run diligence, drafted and negotiated agreements, and lived the workflows you will now automate

  • 5+ years of total experience spanning legal and some combination of technical GTM, sales engineering, solutions architecture, AI product strategy, or applied AI with customer exposure

  • Deep fluency in legal workflows: research, contract review, diligence, drafting, discovery, regulatory analysis, and matter management

  • Strong intuition for AI products, agents, and workflows, with the ability to understand technical systems without needing every detail pre-digested

  • Demonstrated ability to turn ambiguous customer problems into scoped, executable deployment plans with clear success metrics

  • Strong commercial instincts and comfort operating with partners, general counsel, CIOs, and heads of innovation

  • Excellent written and verbal communication; able to write proposals, customer memos, technical scopes, and launch narratives

  • High agency and low ego, with the ability to run multiple complex customer workstreams in parallel and make progress before the playbook exists

Nice-to-Haves

  • JD and bar admission

  • Hands-on experience building with agentic systems, tool-use workflows, MCP, or LLM APIs

  • Working knowledge of legal technology platforms: Westlaw, LexisNexis, iManage, NetDocuments, Relativity, Ironclad, or similar

  • Experience selling or deploying technology into law firms or regulated enterprises, including outside-counsel guidelines, privilege, and security review

  • Founder or early-startup operating experience

  • Strong network across AmLaw 100 firms and Fortune 500 legal departments

If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed above.

  • Deep fluency in front-office workflows: screening, comps, diligence, earnings, research synthesis, portfolio construction and monitoring

  • Strong intuition for AI products, agents, and workflows, with the ability to understand technical systems without needing every detail pre-digested

  • Comfortable working shoulder-to-shoulder with Forward Deployed Engineers and technical teams: scoping builds together, pairing on prototypes, and translating customer requirements into engineering-ready specs

  • Demonstrated ability to turn ambiguous customer problems into scoped, executable deployment plans with clear success metrics

  • Strong commercial instincts and comfort operating with MDs, partners, PMs, CIOs, and CTOs

title: Program Manager, Talent Acquisition
description:
Perplexity is scaling at a pace few companies ever experience, and talent is the surface where our biggest bets get won or lost. We're hiring a Program Manager to sit at the center of that motion, owning the mission-critical, cross-functional programs that shape how we plan, prioritize, and hire.

This is a uniquely visible seat, reserved for operators who thrive in ambiguity and have a track record of driving companywide initiatives to measurable outcomes. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with recruiting leadership, executives, and cross-functional partners to architect the systems, operating rhythms, and decision-making frameworks that let the company move faster and with more clarity. When a complex, high-stakes program needs an owner, you're the person leadership turns to.

What You'll Do

  • Own Perplexity's most consequential talent programs end-to-end, from ambiguous mandate to shipped outcome

  • Partner directly with executives and recruiting leadership to turn strategy into programs with clear owners, milestones, and accountability

  • Drive cross-functional initiatives across Recruiting, People, Finance, and business leadership, aligning stakeholders and clearing blockers before they escalate

  • Design the operating cadence of the org: planning cycles, prioritization, reporting rhythms, and executive updates that keep leadership decisive

  • Build the systems, tooling, and workflows that let recruiting scale, automating the repetitive so human judgment goes to the highest-leverage work

  • Stand up the metrics and dashboards that turn hiring data into faster, sharper decisions

  • Anticipate risk on the highest-visibility programs, communicate crisply under pressure, and drive to resolution when priorities shift

  • Set the bar for program excellence and codify repeatable playbooks the rest of the company can adopt

What You Bring

  • 7+ years of program or project management experience, including ownership of companywide, mission-critical initiatives

  • Direct experience partnering with and presenting to executives on high-stakes, cross-functional work

  • Track record of driving ambiguous programs to measurable outcomes in fast-paced, rapidly scaling environments

  • Operational rigor. You build order out of chaos and design systems that outlast you

  • Strong analytical instincts, with the ability to structure messy data into clear direction for leadership

  • Sharp communication and stakeholder judgment, with the discretion to operate on sensitive, high-visibility work

  • A builder's mindset and a bias for action, aligned with Perplexity's ethos of building what hasn't been built before

  • Recruiting, talent, or People-org program experience is a plus, but we're optimizing for the best operators first

title: Design Engineer, Growth & Marketing
description:
Perplexity is looking for a Design Engineer to help turn perplexity.com into a real growth engine, not a pile of one-off pages. You'll sit shoulder to shoulder with brand designers, PMMs, growth, and content teams, shipping product launch pages, campaign landing pages, and the components and tooling that let those teams move fast without lowering the bar.

This is a hands-on role for someone with real taste, sharp attention to detail, and the speed to turn a Figma file, a Slack thread, or a rough sketch into a polished, shipped page quickly.

Tech stack: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Sanity


What you'll do

  • Ship product launch pages and evergreen marketing pages for products like Comet, Computer, Deep Research, Search, and Hub. Own the work from Figma handoff to production.

  • Partner with brand designers to build interactive experiences that make the site feel alive and drive engagement.

  • Maintain and extend our brand design system and component library, keeping Figma and production in sync so brand and creative can scaffold pages with guardrails.

  • Work closely with the paid ads and growth teams to run A/B tests on landing pages, popups, and upsell modules. Read the results, then iterate.

  • Migrate the leftover Framer collections to Sanity, model schemas that non-engineers can actually use, and help ship new content types like changelog, customer stories, and academy pages.

  • Design and unblock yourself when design resources are constrained. You can take a rough direction and turn it into something worth shipping.

  • Improve the tools around the work: CMS workflows, i18n, SEO, experimentation, and internal tooling for marketing self-serve. If a manual process is slowing the team down, you should want to fix it.

What you need

  • 3+ years of experience as a front-end or design engineer, ideally on a marketing or growth site.

  • A portfolio site that shows your previous work on marketing sites and design work.

  • Strong skills in React, CSS, and modern frameworks.

  • Deep understanding of responsive design and design-to-code workflows. You know what the platform can do and you stay current on what's new.

  • Experience maintaining a reusable component library and sweating the design details in code.

  • A real eye for design. You can tell the difference between "almost right" and "actually right," and your work reflects it.

  • Attention to detail that shows up unprompted. The 2px misalignment, the wrong easing curve, the widow at the end of the paragraph.

  • Stellar communication skills and a track record of working effectively in cross-functional teams. You can defend a decision, push back constructively, and explain trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Desire to work in a fast-paced environment, continuously grow, and master your craft.

Nice to have

  • Experience running A/B tests and reading experiments results in a growth context.

  • Knowledge of SEO principles, structured data, and localization workflows.

  • Experience with web animations (GSAP, Motion, Web Animations API), 3D libraries, or interactive storytelling.

  • Experience working with a headless CMS (Sanity, Contentful).

  • Experience building internal tools or AI-assisted workflows that made a marketing or design team faster.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Enterprise Agent Evals & Efficiency)
description:
About the Role

The Enterprise Agent Evals & Efficiency team makes Perplexity's agents better at completing real work across enterprise connectors, tools, and data. Our goal is to help agents choose the right tools, use the right context, and complete complex workflows reliably, with less time and compute. This team owns the improvement loop: define what successful work looks like, build evaluations that measure it, understand where agents fail, and ship changes that improve outcomes.

This is a hands-on engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from building realistic enterprise evaluation environments to shipping improvements across the agent harness, tools, and skills. You'll create complex scenarios spanning connected systems, data, and permissions, use them to identify where agents struggle, and improve the tools agents call, the skills they follow, the context they receive, and the models they use. Working with AI Research, Connectors, and Platform teams, you'll turn experimental results into measurable gains in task success, latency, and cost per successful task. The goal is not just to measure agents, but to make more enterprise work reliable and practical to automate.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build realistic enterprise evaluation environments spanning connected applications, representative datasets, user roles, and permissions, with complex, multi-step workflows and reproducible system state.

  • Own evaluation infrastructure, task suites, and automated graders that measure how well agents complete enterprise work, calibrated against human judgment and grounded in end-to-end outcomes.

  • Analyze agent trajectories and production failures, identify root causes, and ship improvements across the agent harness, tools, and skills that measurably improve task success and reliability.

  • Develop reusable skills and improve tool descriptions, schemas, and result handling so agents can select the right tools, execute workflows correctly, and recover from errors with fewer unnecessary calls.

  • Build and evaluate model-selection and routing strategies that match each task to the right model and effort level, balancing quality, latency, reliability, and cost.

  • Improve agent efficiency through context management, skill loading, caching, and execution strategies that reduce wasted tokens and cost per successful task without compromising quality or safety.

  • Build regression gates and launch-readiness signals for model, connector, tool, skill, and harness changes, and validate that evaluation gains translate into better production outcomes.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of software engineering or machine learning engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex production systems from design through deployment and operation.

  • Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable infrastructure for experimentation, evaluation, or data-intensive applications.

  • Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and the ability to work effectively across a multi-language production stack.

  • Hands-on experience building, evaluating, or improving LLM-based applications or agents, including tool use and multi-step workflows.

  • Deep expertise in at least one of the following:

    • Evaluation infrastructure, benchmark design, and automated grading.

    • Agent harnesses, tool interfaces, and reusable skills for complex workflows.

    • Realistic test environments or simulations spanning multiple systems, datasets, permissions, and stateful workflows.

    • Model selection, routing, and inference efficiency, including context management and caching.

  • Strong experimental and statistical judgment, including choosing representative tasks, defining meaningful success criteria, diagnosing failures, and distinguishing real improvements from noise.

  • Sound technical judgment in balancing task quality, latency, reliability, and cost, with a track record of translating evaluation findings into shipped improvements.

  • A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture through production adoption, setting technical direction, and raising engineering quality through mentorship.

If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification. We value demonstrated impact, deep ownership, and the initiative to turn ambiguity into results.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Model Behavior)
description:
About the Role

We're hiring software engineers for the Model Behavior team to help shape how Perplexity’s AI products behave: the style of their responses, and the way they use tools, skills, and memory. The team designs prompt and context engineering strategies to deliver high-quality user experiences across multiple domains and models.

The ideal candidate for this role has a strong software engineering background, and an analytical, experiment-driven approach to solving challenging problems. You’ll work on context and prompt engineering to shape model behavior and style, and to guide how models use tools, skills, and memory across our products.

 

What you'll do

  • Context Engineering: Design, test, and optimize the prompts, skills, tools, and memory that shape Perplexity responses across products, features, and use cases. Build self-improvement loops to steer the prompt, improve tool/skill use, and improve the ability to draw on memory.

  • Model Releases: Help experiment with and release new models.

  • Research & Analysis: Identify inconsistencies and failure modes in model outputs through well-designed research projects, for both internal and production systems.

  • Knowledge Sharing: Help engineers across teams build intuition for prompt design and context engineering best practices.

  • Staying Current: Track the latest prompting, context engineering, and alignment techniques from industry and academia, and bring the best ideas back to the team.

 

What We're Looking For

Required

  • 2 to 10+ years of experience in software engineering or research.

  • Strong background in software engineering fundamentals, and a technical understanding of LLM-driven and agentic systems.

  • Experience shaping LLM behavior through prompts, tool and skill design, or memory systems.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly in explaining complex concepts to diverse stakeholders.

Nice to have

  • Recent experience working on modern LLM-driven products.

  • Experience working across teams or with external partners.

  • Experience designing evaluations or benchmarks for AI systems.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Android Engineer, Computer Growth)
description:
In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people now use Perplexity to transform knowledge into action, and a growing share of them meet us first on their phone. The Growth team owns the product loops that help people discover, adopt, and build lasting habits around our most important AI experiences — and on mobile that means owning everything from the App Store listing to the first task a user finishes to the moment they upgrade.

As an Android growth engineer at Perplexity, you'll work across the full mobile funnel — install, activation, onboarding, push and lifecycle messaging, conversion, retention, and in-app purchase moments — for Perplexity, Comet, and Computer on Android. Engineers are responsible for end-to-end projects: rebuilding onboarding as a series of experiments, wiring in-app purchase and paywall surfaces to our billing systems, shipping notification experiences people actually keep enabled, and turning ASO and deep-link work into measurable adoption.

Growth at Perplexity goes beyond incremental funnel optimization. The team sits close to the core product — we translate behavioral signals, model outputs, and fast experimentation into durable product surfaces used across consumer and enterprise workflows. You'll move fast, run many experiments in parallel, and own the outcome end-to-end, while respecting the constraints mobile brings: release cycles, store review, and version fragmentation.

Why Perplexity is different

  • Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

  • Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

  • Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.

  • Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.

  • Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, GPU Cluster Infrastructure)
description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month, and every one of them fans out into multiple AI inference requests running in real time. Behind that sits a large GPU fleet spread across several cloud providers. Today, our inference engineers and researchers build models while also managing networking, securing capacity, and operating the underlying GPU clusters, responsibilities we want a dedicated platform team to own. Your job is to take ownership of that infrastructure and hide its complexity behind a unified, self-serve platform for running training and inference workloads.

Responsibilities

  • Build a self-serve compute platform. Design and own the systems that let inference engineers and researchers launch training jobs and operate inference services without managing GPU provisioning, cluster configuration, or provider-specific infrastructure.

  • Operate the GPU fleet. Own provisioning, lifecycle management, reliability, and capacity integration across providers, giving teams a consistent way to use compute regardless of where it runs.

  • Solve for GPU scarcity. Build the scheduling and placement logic that finds available capacity across providers, packs it efficiently, and gets the right workload onto the right hardware under real constraints.

  • Support two very different workloads. Keep long-running distributed training jobs healthy while simultaneously guaranteeing the availability and latency of production inference services on the same fleet.

  • Own the Kubernetes for GPU orchestration. Write the operators and CRDs, and manage many clusters across providers so the platform behaves the same everywhere we run.

  • Make failure boring. Build the fault tolerance, autoscaling, and observability that keep the fleet utilized and let workloads survive node loss, provider hiccups, and capacity shifts without human intervention.

  • Set technical direction across teams. Partner with inference and cloud infrastructure engineers to turn operational constraints into a coherent platform architecture and roadmap.

Qualifications

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

  • Deep Kubernetes experience — custom operators, CRDs, and multi-cluster federation, not just running kubectl apply.

  • You've managed GPU clusters at scale: NVIDIA hardware, CUDA, and the networking that makes them fast (InfiniBand or RoCE).

  • You've orchestrated compute across multiple clouds (CoreWeave, AWS, GCP, or similar) and understand how different each one really is.

  • Strong distributed systems fundamentals: scheduling, resource allocation, and fault tolerance under load.

  • You write infrastructure and systems-level code in Go, Rust or C++.

  • You've supported both long-running training jobs and high-availability inference services, and you know why they pull infrastructure in opposite directions.

  • You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.

Additional experience we value

  • Inference serving stacks: vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.

  • Slurm or other HPC schedulers.

  • GPU kernel work in CUDA or Triton — not required, but notable.

  • High-speed interconnects: InfiniBand, RoCE, or RDMA in production.

  • Observability for ML workloads: Prometheus, Grafana, or Weights & Biases.

title: Principal Counsel, Corporate
description:
Summary of Role

Perplexity AI is looking for a Principal Counsel, Corporate to serve as the company’s primary lawyer for corporate governance, equity, and financing matters. In this role, you’ll own the full corporate legal lifecycle, from board and stockholder governance and equity administration to financings, secondary transactions, and entity management as we scale globally. You’ll work closely with our Finance, Accounting, Tax and People teams, as well as with our executive team and investors. You’ll drive transactions from term sheet through closing, build the governance infrastructure that keeps a rapidly growing private company well-run, and stand up the templates, playbooks, and records systems that let corporate work scale without adding headcount. The ideal candidate brings deep private-company corporate and securities experience, precision with cap-table and equity mechanics, and the judgment to make principled calls independently.

This is a high-impact, hands-on role for a corporate attorney who thrives in fast-paced environments, is comfortable being the first and only owner of a workstream, and is excited to help build a best-in-class legal function at one of the most consequential AI companies in the world.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead corporate governance for Perplexity and its subsidiaries, including board and committee meeting preparation, agendas, minutes, resolutions and written consents, charters, organizational documents, corporate policies, and the corporate records that keep the company well-governed as it scales.

  • Structure, draft, and negotiate equity and debt financings from term sheet through closing, including preferred stock financings, credit facilities, convertible instruments, and related diligence and closing deliverables.

  • Own secondary transactions and liquidity programs, including tender offers, company repurchases, direct secondaries, transfer approvals and the related stockholder communications and consents.

  • Partner with Finance, Accounting, Tax and People on equity compensation and cap-table administration, including option and RSU grant processes, 409A valuations, pool sizing and refreshes, fully diluted share reconciliation, and Carta hygiene.

  • Support M&A, acquihires, strategic investments, and other corporate transactions, including structuring, diligence, definitive agreement negotiation, closing, and post-closing integration, and manage outside counsel to budget and schedule.

  • Build and scale corporate legal infrastructure, including consent and resolution precedent libraries, grant and vesting exhibit templates, signature and approval workflows, entity management systems, and formation and foreign-qualification processes for domestic and international expansion.

  • Support corporate readiness workstreams, including audit support, internal controls over corporate approvals, subsidiary governance, and the sequencing of policies and processes that position the company for future financing or public-company requirements.

  • Monitor legal and market developments affecting private-company governance, equity, and securities matters, and translate them into practical guidance for the executive team and the board.

Qualifications

  • JD and in good standing with an active US state bar membership, , or eligible to register as in-house counsel in California

  • At least 9+ years of law firm and/or in-house experience

  • Track record leading venture or growth equity financings, secondary transactions, and corporate governance for high-growth private technology companies

  • Deep familiarity with cap-table mechanics, equity compensation administration, and charter and stockholder agreement provisions, with the precision to reconcile numbers before they reach the board

  • Strong business acumen and ability to partner with finance, accounting, people, and executive stakeholders

  • An ability to communicate clearly with business and technical audiences and effectively translate legal concepts for non-lawyers

  • Positive collaborative attitude, comfort with change and a fast pace, high level of integrity, and intellectual curiosity

title: Lead Product Designer, Enterprise

Perplexity is looking for a Lead Product Designer to own the design of our enterprise product. You'll design new experiences across enterprise and multiplayer use cases — making software that feels like the future but can be understood and used by anyone in the world today.

You'll work closely with product, engineering, and the broader design team, and you care about everything it takes to make a product great: product, interaction, brand, growth, copywriting, engineering, and marketing.

title: Business Operations Manager, Marketing and Communications
description:

That means keeping the wheels turning: the tool stack, agencies and vendors, budgets, contracts, and the dashboards leadership relies on. What you'll do

  • Own the marketing and comms tool stack: evaluate, procure, onboard, provision access, train the team, and retire what we've outgrown

  • Build and maintain internal tools such as calendars, intake forms, dashboards, trackers, and automations, and keep them reliable as more people depend on them

title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Model Platform)
description:
About Perplexity AI

In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. We’ve scaled beyond the millions of people using Perplexity every day for research, shopping, investing and curiosity into a new paradigm of using AI to transform knowledge into action.

As an engineer at Perplexity, your role will be to build products and systems that define how AI empowers humans to think, decide and act. You’ll ship fast and work between both product and infrastructure advancements in our technology.

Why Perplexity is different

  • Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

  • Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

  • Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.

  • Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.

  • Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.

About the Role

Perplexity is looking for a deeply technical software engineer to own and evolve our model serving platform, which is responsible for connecting our products and research systems with our inference layers. This mission-critical system gives teams one fast, reliable interface across providers.

You will work at the intersection of distributed systems, AI products, and infrastructure. You will make it dramatically easier for teams across Perplexity to adopt new models, run rigorous experiments, and ship dependable products.

The ideal candidate combines sound technical judgment forged in production systems with active curiosity around the rapidly changing capabilities and failure modes of frontier models. You will design core abstractions, lead high-conviction technical decisions, and write production Rust and Python for a service that serves hundreds of millions of model requests per day.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience building and shipping large-scale systems and services with high reliability, availability, and performance.

  • Strong software engineering craft, with special care for developer experience and designing future-proof systems that can evolve along with a rapidly advancing AI landscape.

  • Proficiency with a general-purpose backend language (Python, Rust, C++, Go) and cloud infrastructure (AWS, Kubernetes).

  • BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, or related fields (or equivalent experience).

title: Applied AI Architect, Perplexity Computer
description:
Perplexity is seeking an Applied AI Architect to help our customers turn Perplexity Computer into working solutions that drive measurable impact. This role is ideal for technical, consultative professionals who have led complex software implementations and can move comfortably between customer discovery, solution design, hands-on delivery, and executive communication.

About the role

Perplexity Computer is a new class of AI system that navigates tools, interacts with applications, and completes multi-step workflows end to end. Our customers are using Computer to transform work that traditional software has not been able to address.

Applied AI Architects work directly with customers across presales, onboarding, adoption, and strategic engagements. You will uncover the real business problem, determine what Computer can credibly support, design and configure the workflow, and lead the engagement to a clear outcome.

This is a hands-on, customer-facing role at the intersection of solutions architecture, technical consulting, and program delivery. You will work closely with Sales and Customer Success while serving as a quality filter for requests that require Product or Engineering.

What you'll do

  • Lead technical discovery. Work with customer business leaders, technical teams, account executives, and customer success managers to understand the users, current workflow, desired outcome, constraints, and decision-makers.

  • Design credible solutions. Map how people, data, tools, approvals, permissions, and decisions interact, then determine how Computer can support the workflow.

  • Support complex opportunities. Partner with account executives on technical deal strategy, demos, proofs of value, architecture and security coordination, and engagement scoping.

  • Drive value-backed consumption. Identify high-value, repeatable workflows; define the expected business outcomes and usage patterns; and partner with Sales and Customer Success to move customers from technical validation to sustained production use and expansion.

  • Build hands-on. Configure, prototype, test, and iterate on Computer skills and workflows, including connectors, permissions, and adjacent tooling.

  • Accelerate onboarding and adoption. Provide second-level technical consultation to customer success managers and deliver bounded technical work when customer needs exceed standard Customer Success coverage.

  • Run strategic engagements. Establish scope, customer commitments, milestones, success criteria, working cadence, and exit criteria, then lead the work through closure.

  • Improve technical escalation. Validate product and engineering needs and produce decision-ready requests with clear evidence, constraints, impact, and acceptance criteria.

  • Turn every engagement into leverage. Convert repeated customer needs into reusable workflows, implementation patterns, demos, guidance, and product feedback.

What we're looking for

The strongest Applied AI Architects combine technical depth, consultative problem solving, and disciplined engagement delivery. You should be comfortable working hands-on with the product, advising customer executives, and managing the details required to deliver a successful outcome.

Must-haves

  • 5+ years in a customer-facing technical role such as solutions architecture, senior sales engineering, AI implementation, forward deployed work, technical consulting, or technical program leadership.

  • Proven consultative discovery skills. You can turn an ambiguous request into a clear business problem, technical approach, and delivery plan.

  • Hands-on technical fluency. You are comfortable with APIs, integrations, authentication, identity, permissions, connectors, data flows, and technical troubleshooting.

  • Experience delivering complex implementations. You have managed scope, stakeholders, milestones, risk, expectations, and closure.

  • Strong solution judgment. You can distinguish education, configuration, implementation, support, product, and engineering problems and recommend the right path.

  • Commercial and consumption awareness. You can connect solution design and technical decisions to time to value, usage, credit consumption, customer economics, and expansion potential.

  • Executive-credible communication. You can explain technical trade-offs to senior decision-makers while working effectively with practitioners and engineers.

  • High agency in ambiguity. You can establish direction without waiting for perfect requirements, challenge weak assumptions, and make thoughtful decisions quickly.

  • AI-native working style. You use frontier models and AI tools regularly and have developed strong intuition for what current systems can and cannot do reliably.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience deploying agents or multi-step LLM workflows in complex enterprise environments.

  • Experience with Computer, MCP, enterprise identity, security, permissions, or workflow orchestration.

  • Experience in regulated or workflow-intensive industries such as legal, financial services, healthcare, or technology.

  • Prior forward deployed engineering, Applied AI, deployment strategist, solutions architecture, or technical consulting experience at an AI or enterprise software company.

  • A track record of turning customer implementations into reusable technical assets or product improvements.

title: Director, Litigation
description:
Perplexity AI is looking for a sharp, entrepreneurial litigation attorney to join our small legal team to help advance the business, protect the products we are building, and revolutionize the way people search and interact with the internet. This unique role offers significant responsibility, direct ownership of high stakes matters, and growth potential across an in-house practice group.

This is a unique role within a rapidly growing AI technology company. You will play a key role in safeguarding Perplexity’s interests by managing litigation files and pre-litigation disputes related to our AI answer engine, models, and technologies, while helping to build and scale our litigation function. You will oversee complex disputes in a fast-moving and often unsettled legal landscape, spanning intellectual property (including copyright), privacy, commercial, and regulatory matters, and you will work closely with our AI, engineering, and product teams to assess legal risk, develop litigation strategy, and provide guidance during disputes involving our products and services.

The ideal candidate combines deep substantive knowledge of litigation practice and procedure with strong business judgment and practical problem-solving abilities. You are comfortable confronting novel legal issues, including questions where the rules are still being written, and you bring intellectual curiosity about AI technology, adaptability in an emerging landscape, and exceptional collaboration skills. Success in this role requires a deep understanding of high-growth startup environments, where you will pair traditional legal expertise with sharp business risk assessment. We are seeking someone who is inquisitive, has an entrepreneurial drive, and the agility to thrive in our fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage litigation matters and pre-litigation disputes across all phases, including strategy, pleadings, motions, discovery, depositions, hearings, trials, and appeals, while developing comprehensive case strategies that align with business objectives.

  • Provide counsel across a broad range of disputes, including intellectual property (copyright, trademark, and trade secret), privacy, commercial, and regulatory matters, in both first-party and third-party contexts.

  • Evaluate and respond to litigation threats, demands, and disputes across jurisdictions, developing appropriate matter-resolution proposals that resolve issues with minimal disruption to the business.

  • Select, onboard, manage, and collaborate with outside counsel across all stages of disputes. Negotiate budgets and fee arrangements, monitor performance, and hold outside counsel accountable for delivering optimal results while maintaining cost efficiency.

  • Partner closely with AI, product, and engineering teams to proactively identify litigation risks in product development and go-to-market strategies, and to collect information efficiently in support of active matters. Translate complex legal requirements into practical, actionable guidance for technical teams.

  • Assist in responding to regulatory investigations and inquiries from government regulators and private organizations relating to our products and services.

  • Build internal litigation processes, policies, and tools, including legal-hold and discovery workflows, that support litigation and regulatory matters efficiently and can scale with company growth.

  • Monitor the evolving legal and regulatory landscape for AI, copyright, and privacy; translate court decisions, agency guidance, and legislative developments into timely, executive-ready advice; and communicate with business leaders about ongoing litigation, emerging risks, and preventive measures.

Qualifications

  • JD and in good standing with an active US state bar membership (California preferred)

  • At least 15+ years of law firm and/or in-house experience handling complex commercial litigation (with experience representing emerging technology companies preferred)

  • Deep substantive knowledge of litigation practice and procedure, with a demonstrated history of strong outcomes and effective case execution

  • Exceptional analytical, organizational, and collaboration skills, strong business acumen, and the ability to partner with business and technical teams

  • An ability to communicate clearly and credibly with business and technical audiences, including translating genuinely unsettled legal doctrine into concise, business-relevant advice for executives and engineers without over-hedging

  • Hands-on attitude to tackle projects large and small, and a low-ego, roll-up-your-sleeves approach to working across the organization

  • Excellent composure in stressful situations, high level of integrity, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to work independently with limited guidance while exercising good judgment about when to escalate

  • Thrive working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment

Nice to Have

  • Experience managing copyright and privacy litigation, as well as commercial disputes, for AI or other emerging technology companies

  • Experience managing regulatory responses or investigations, including both first-party and third-party responses

  • Experience building or scaling a litigation function at a growth-stage company, with creativity and an openness to novel solutions

  • Experience litigating cases in multiple jurisdictions, including internationally

  • A passion for supporting the development of AI that is both innovative and trustworthy

title: Strategic Finance Lead - Compute
description:
About the Role

We are seeking a Strategic Finance Lead for our GPU compute fleet. In this role, you will be a key partner to our inference and infrastructure teams, providing financial expertise to optimize our compute investments and drive capacity decisions.

In this role, you'll develop deep expertise in the economics of AI compute, from token-level serving cost to the long-range financial planning of our GPU fleet. You'll build the models that inform Perplexity's capacity and make-versus-buy decisions, own the internal-cost analysis that underpins internal and external token pricing, and translate complex infrastructure dynamics into clear financial narratives for leadership.

This is a high-impact role for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance and infrastructure, and who is energized by building frameworks from scratch in a fast-moving environment.

This position is based in San Francisco and requires in-person attendance 2-3 days per week.

Key Responsibilities

  • Finance lead for GPU compute spend, including budgeting, monthly forecasting, variance analysis, and financial plan maintenance

  • Build and maintain detailed bottoms-up financial models for the GPU fleet, including capacity forecasts, cost driver analyses, and investment scenario modeling

  • Develop deep expertise in GPU vendor contracts, pricing structures, and cost drivers, and surface optimization opportunities across the fleet

  • Serve as subject matter expert for Perplexity's compute capacity plan, owning source of truth on utilization, committed-versus-consumed spend, and capacity by vendor and cluster

  • Build internal token-cost curves distinguishing marginal from fully loaded serving cost, and translate them into internal and external token pricing

  • Analyze the ROI of in-house inference and training, including opportunity cost across chip types, cluster configurations, and workloads, distilled into a framework for capacity deployment

  • Partner closely with inference and infrastructure engineering to understand how serving and training workloads scale, and translate those technical dynamics into financial frameworks

You May Be a Good Fit If You Have

  • Exceptional analytical skills with an ability to synthesize data into compelling insights and develop complex financial operating models

  • Extraordinary problem-solving and critical thinking abilities to develop new frameworks for assessing utilization and capital efficiency in a rapidly evolving industry

  • Attention to detail and patience for getting to the source of truth on complex and interconnected contract and usage data

  • Comfort being the finance person in the room with engineering leads and vendor counterparts, and adept at communicating complex financial information to non-finance audiences

  • A proven track record of partnering with technical teams to drive financial optimization initiatives, building enough trust to become indispensable to their roadmap and resourcing decisions

  • A bias toward action, strong work ethic, and experience driving operational outcomes under tight timelines

  • Background in AI, ML, or high-performance, large-scale computing infrastructure, including data centers and cloud service providers

Preferred Qualifications

  • 4+ years of experience in strategic finance, infrastructure investment, private equity, growth equity, consulting, or investment banking, preferably with infrastructure or datacenter experience

  • Experience in cloud or GPU infrastructure financial management, including direct work with major cloud service providers or neoclouds

  • Direct experience with committed-use economics — reserved capacity, savings plans, committed-use discounts — and GPU procurement

  • Deep expertise in GPU vendor economics, contract structures, and pricing models

  • Experience with chip architecture economics and optimization strategies

  • Proficiency with financial modeling tools

title: Strategic Finance Lead - AI
description:

We are seeking a Strategic Finance Lead to help lead the economics of our AI products. In this role, you will be a key partner to our product, inference, and data teams, providing financial expertise to optimize model spend and drive pricing and margin decisions.

In this role, you'll develop deep expertise in the unit economics of AI products, from per-request serving cost to consolidated product-level margin across our portfolio. You'll build the models that inform Perplexity's pricing, packaging, and model-deployment decisions, own the product-margin methodology that reconciles revenue and inference cost from production data, and translate complex model economics into clear financial narratives for leadership.

  • Build and maintain product-margin models across the product portfolio, reconciling revenue, serving cost, and gross margin from production usage data

  • Extraordinary problem-solving and critical thinking abilities to develop new frameworks for assessing product margin and unit economics in a rapidly evolving industry

  • Attention to detail and patience for getting to the source of truth on complex and interconnected usage, revenue, and cost data

  • Comfort working cross-functionally and are adept at communicating complex financial information to non-finance audiences

  • A proven track record of partnering with technical and product teams to drive financial optimization initiatives

  • A bias toward action, strong work ethic, and experience driving operational outcomes under tight timelines
