title: Member of Technical Staff (TPM, Inference)
description:
Perplexity is looking for a technical program manager to be the connective tissue between our model providers, engineering, and product teams, driving our core inference platform forward.

Perplexity runs one of the highest-throughput inference stacks in the industry, serving Ask, Computer, and API traffic across a large and constantly shifting portfolio of first-party and third-party models. This role sits at the intersection of product, engineering, and finance: you'll orchestrate across model providers and internal teams to keep new models and capacity moving smoothly into production, while executing the roadmap for the inference platform itself. The ideal candidate has strong technical judgment, thrives coordinating across teams and external partners with competing timelines, and is energized by building the operating model for a function that doesn't have much precedent yet.

Our Mission

Perplexity's mission is to power curiosity. Curious people are the people who drive change in the world. Driving change is a continuous cycle of learning, building, and integrating.

Learn: curious people constantly learn new things by asking more. They question the status quo in their own expertise and they constantly learn outside of it. Research is essential to them and never ending.

Build: curious people make and create things, to show the world their new answers to problems no one else ever questioned. They take action on what they've learned. Makers need tools to create their products, their companies, their reality.

Integrate: they must interact with the world as it is to drive change and adoption. True leaders do not simply build something and hope. They must have armies of agents and workers who can constantly work in millions of small ways.

What You'll Do

  • Execute the roadmap for the inference platform request handling, rate limits and quotas, usage controls, and the reliability and observability surface engineering and product teams depend on

  • Be the connective tissue between model providers and Perplexity's engineering and product teams coordinating onboarding, launch readiness, and rollout for new models and capacity

  • Drive latency, throughput, uptime, and cost-efficiency as core execution metrics, surfacing tradeoffs between them rather than letting them become side effects

  • Run the operating model for model-release and optimization programs, including day-zero launches, across performance engineering, infrastructure, and product teams

  • Lead cross-functional delivery for inference-stack changes, from planning through launch and post-launch validation

  • Build the mechanisms that make releases predictable rituals, dashboards, launch checklists so inference releases stay low-risk at Perplexity's scale

  • Partner with GPU capacity and compute teams to reconcile execution decisions against cost, capacity, and vendor constraints

Qualifications

  • Strong experience with technical program management or product management in infrastructure, distributed systems, or ML/model-serving products

  • Direct experience with production LLM or ML inference understanding what makes serving fast, reliable, and cheap rather than just what a roadmap slide says about it

  • Comfort orchestrating across external partners and internal engineering teams with competing priorities and timelines

  • Experience with data and metrics, and the judgment to surface difficult tradeoffs between latency, throughput, uptime, and cost

  • Thrives in a small, agile team; has initiative and desire for ownership without much precedent to lean on

  • 6+ years of combined technical program management or product management experience

title: Virtual Events Manager
description:
Perplexity is revolutionizing how companies get work done. We are seeking a Virtual Events Manager to build the channel that shows people what our products can do and teaches them how to use them. You will develop a deep working knowledge of our products, turn that knowledge into compelling live experiences, and own the programs that convert audiences into active users and qualified pipeline.

This role has two sides. You are a charismatic host and product storyteller who can command a virtual room, and you are the operator who keeps every event on the rails. You will find and prepare the right experts from across Perplexity, work with Growth to build the audience, and measure whether each program produced a real business return.

If you have a passion for understanding how things work, thrive in taking something complex and making it engaging, and want to build a world-class virtual events engine from the ground up, this role is for you.

Responsibilities

  • Know the product cold. Develop a deeper working knowledge of our products than anyone else in events, using new features as they ship, building the workflows yourself, and staying close to the teams that built them.

  • Own virtual events end to end. Run the channel from program strategy and calendar planning through event briefs, speaker staffing, rehearsals, live production, follow-up, and retros. Build a reliable portfolio of onboarding programs, product launches, feature deep-dives, customer conversations, and use-case workshops.

  • Bring the product to life. Host, moderate, present, and demonstrate the product live with energy and clarity. Turn complex capabilities into specific, accurate stories that audiences can understand and put to work.

  • Find and prepare the right people. Build relationships across Product, Engineering, Research, Sales, Customer Success, Partnerships, and Marketing to identify the strongest speakers and subject-matter experts for each program. Brief them thoroughly, sharpen their stories, and make sure they are ready to deliver.

  • Build the audience. Partner with Growth, Lifecycle, Social, Comms, Sales, and Customer Success on full-funnel promotion plans that drive qualified registrations. Track pacing closely, identify gaps early, and run experiments across audience, creative, channel mix, timing, and follow-up.

  • Turn every event into an engine. Extend the value of each program through recordings, replays, clips, FAQs, demo flows, education materials, and sales follow-up. Build formats and templates that make the next event faster and better.

  • Measure outcomes, not just outputs. Instrument the funnel from registration through attendance, engagement, product activation, qualified pipeline, and revenue. Track cost per registration, cost per attendee, cost per qualified attendee, sourced and influenced pipeline, and channel ROI, then use the findings to improve the portfolio.

  • Build the operating system. Create the intake process, master calendar, production checklists, run-of-show templates, speaker bench, readiness gates, contingency plans, scorecards, and reporting cadence required to scale the channel without lowering quality.

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience in virtual events, product marketing, customer education, demand generation, or a related role, ideally within a high-growth technology company, or work that proves the skill regardless of title.

  • Proven ability to learn technical products deeply and translate complex capabilities into simple, specific, and accurate live demonstrations.

  • A polished, credible on-camera presence, with experience hosting, interviewing, moderating, or presenting to professional audiences.

  • Strong cross-functional instincts and the ability to find, recruit, brief, and coordinate busy experts without relying on formal authority.

  • Full-funnel growth fluency, including registration strategy, audience segmentation, campaign testing, conversion, and post-event nurture.

  • Analytical rigor, with experience defining channel metrics, working with CRM and marketing automation data, and calculating return on investment.

  • Excellent production judgment and attention to detail, including rehearsals, technical readiness, live moderation, and fallback planning.

  • High slope: you learn unfamiliar products and domains fast, and your rate of improvement is your standout trait.

  • Extreme comfort delivering clarity in high-velocity, ambiguous environments.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Infrastructure & Platform)
description:
About the Role

The Infrastructure team builds and operates the foundational systems behind Perplexity’s products. At Perplexity, infrastructure sits on the critical path of every answer, supporting real-time search, retrieval, model serving, and agent workloads where latency, reliability, and rapid iteration directly shape the user experience. This role is for strong infrastructure engineers whose experience spans multiple domains and who are energized by cross-cutting problems that do not fit neatly within a single platform team.

You do not need to be a specialist in every area. Scope ranges from owning major production systems to setting technical direction across teams, leading complex infrastructure programs, and shaping infrastructure strategy across the organization. If a specialized Cloud Infrastructure, Storage Platform, Backend Platform, Data Platform, Connector Platform, or AI Acceleration role clearly matches your expertise and interests, apply directly to it. If your experience spans several infrastructure domains or you are most energized by cross-cutting systems problems, apply here. Submit one application, and we will consider you across the Infrastructure organization.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own cross-cutting infrastructure problems that span compute, storage, networking, data, deployment, and reliability, including eliminating bottlenecks across retrieval and serving paths, building shared abstractions across deployment environments, and resolving failure modes that cross platform boundaries.

  • Design, build, and operate distributed infrastructure supporting Perplexity’s consumer, AI, and enterprise workloads, owning systems from architecture through production operation.

  • Identify gaps between existing platforms and build shared abstractions, automation, and tooling that make infrastructure easier and safer to use.

  • Improve system performance, availability, scalability, and cost-efficiency across online request traffic and background workloads.

  • Debug complex production issues across service and infrastructure boundaries, then turn the findings into durable architectural improvements.

  • Set technical direction for complex infrastructure systems, lead high-impact programs across teams, and establish durable technical standards through collaboration with infrastructure, product, AI, and security partners.

Qualifications

  • 4+ years of professional software engineering experience building and operating production backend, platform, or distributed systems.

  • A track record of owning complex production systems end to end and delivering sustained technical impact across teams.

  • Demonstrated ability to set technical direction, lead through influence, and raise the engineering bar through architecture, design reviews, and mentorship.

  • Strong software engineering skills in Python or other systems or backend languages such as Go, Rust, C++, or Java.

  • Meaningful experience across at least two infrastructure domains, such as cloud platforms, distributed systems, Kubernetes, storage, databases, networking, data systems, developer infrastructure, or production reliability.

  • Ability to develop depth quickly in unfamiliar systems, reason across software and infrastructure layers, and drive production incidents from diagnosis through durable resolution.

If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn’t match every qualification listed above.

title: Enablement Specialist, Perplexity Computer
description:
Perplexity is seeking an Enablement Specialist to help enterprise customers build the knowledge, confidence, and repeatable practices required to reach value with Perplexity Computer. This role is ideal for someone who combines technical fluency, strong facilitation, and a track record of building onboarding and adoption programs that scale.

About the role

Perplexity Computer enables customers to build AI-powered workflows that navigate tools, interact with applications, and complete multi-step work. Helping organizations adopt this new way of working requires more than a product demonstration or one-time kickoff.

Enablement Specialists design and deliver the programs that move customers from initial access to confident, sustained use. You will create onboarding journeys for different levels of readiness, lead customer workshops and office hours, diagnose adoption barriers, and turn repeated questions into scalable guidance.

This is a customer-facing role that works closely with Customer Success, Applied AI Architects, Product, Marketing, and Support. Customer Success retains ownership of the account, adoption strategy, and expansion strategy; you will own the enablement programs and interventions that help customers and customer success managers become self-sufficient.

What you'll do

  • Design customer journeys. Build onboarding and adoption programs for customers and user cohorts with different roles, goals, technical readiness, and levels of AI experience.

  • Deliver high-quality enablement. Lead technical kickoffs, workshops, office hours, remote sessions, onsite programs, webinars, and train-the-trainer experiences.

  • Make complex concepts accessible. Teach Computer and agentic-workflow concepts clearly to both technical and nontechnical audiences.

  • Guide customers through setup. Help customers understand access, members, permissions, connectors, credits, models, initial workflows, and the practices required to get started.

  • Diagnose adoption barriers. Determine whether a customer is blocked by knowledge, readiness, process, configuration, product capability, or technical complexity.

  • Route complex needs well. Recognize when a question requires an Applied AI Architect, Customer Success, Support, Product, or Engineering and provide a clear handoff.

  • Create scalable assets. Turn repeated onboarding and adoption needs into curricula, customer checklists, implementation guidance, lifecycle communications, videos, examples, and internal enablement.

  • Use evidence to increase adoption and consumption. Segment customers by readiness and usage behavior, identify where consumption stalls, deliver targeted interventions, and measure activation, time to first value, repeat usage, sustained credit consumption, and program effectiveness.

  • Build the learning loop. Bring customer patterns and feedback back to Applied AI, Product, Customer Success, Marketing, and Support.

What we're looking for

The strongest Enablement Specialists can teach, diagnose, and design for scale. You should be able to run a compelling customer session, understand the technical details behind a blocker, and build a repeatable program rather than solving the same problem one customer at a time.

Must-haves

  • 4+ years in technical onboarding, customer enablement, implementation, solutions consulting, customer education, or a technically oriented Customer Success role.

  • Proven program-building experience. You have designed and delivered onboarding, training, or adoption programs across live and self-service formats.

  • Strong facilitation and communication. You can explain complex product and AI concepts clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.

  • Technical fluency. You can guide customers through permissions, connectors, models, credits, workflows, and common integration concepts.

  • Strong diagnostic judgment. You can determine whether a customer is blocked by education, readiness, process, configuration, product capability, or technical complexity.

  • Data-informed growth mindset. You have used product and usage data to identify adoption gaps, trigger interventions, move customer cohorts toward sustained use, and evaluate impact.

  • Cross-functional operating ability. You can work effectively with Customer Success, Sales, Product, Marketing, Support, and technical teams.

  • High ownership. You set clear expectations, improve weak processes, and operate effectively in a fast-moving environment.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience with AI products, agentic workflows, enterprise SaaS, or other technically complex platforms.

  • Experience building technical onboarding or adoption programs for enterprise customers.

  • Background in adult learning, instructional design, customer education, or enablement operations.

  • Experience using product and usage data to trigger interventions and measure activation, time to value, and sustained engagement.

  • Experience developing customer-facing technical content, workshops, or certification programs.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Applied AI Engineer, Agent Capabilities)
description:
Perplexity Computer is one of the defining products of the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people use Perplexity to transform knowledge into action, and the Agent Capabilities team sits at the intersection of frontier AI research and product innovation, building the foundations that shape how users and agents solve increasingly complex tasks.

As every major breakthrough in AI models creates new possibilities, the Agent Capabilities team is responsible for turning frontier AI breakthroughs into reusable product capabilities. We are often the first to evaluate emerging model capabilities, determine where they create real user value, and transform them into reliable, scalable, high quality experiences for both users and agents. This is a highly leveraged role with broad ownership at the intersection of frontier AI research, agent systems, platform engineering, and product innovation.

Tech Stack: Python | Go | Rust | PostgreSQL | DynamoDB | AWS | TypeScript

Why Perplexity is different

  • Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

  • Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

  • Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.

  • Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.

  • Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.

What you'll do

  • Evaluate frontier models against real user tasks, identify useful behaviors and failure modes, and turn the most promising advances into production agent systems. Own the lifecycle from rapid prototyping and evaluation through launch, monitoring, and iteration.

  • Improve agents’ ability to plan, use tools, manage context, recover from errors, and complete long-running tasks reliably.

  • Apply state of the art ML and LLM techniques to design scalable agent capabilities such as skills, plugins, artifact generation, tools integrate and use, auto-research, and multi-agent collaboration. Shape the architecture, abstractions, and product experiences that enable both users and agents to compose increasingly sophisticated solutions for real-world tasks.

  • Own agent behavior and capabilities end-to-end, from user-facing products and interfaces to backend services. Define offline and online evaluations for task completion, correctness, safety, latency, cost, and user satisfaction. Iteratively improve across models, prompts, harnesses, and products for different problem spaces.

  • Build secure, observable, and reliable agent systems, including permissions and safeguards for sensitive actions. Develop tracing, replay, and monitoring infrastructure that makes agent failures reproducible and actionable.

  • Collaborate closely with PM, Data Science, Research, to identify high-impact opportunities in understanding and validating emerging model capabilities, and turn complex agent behaviors into simple, reliable product experiences.

  • Apply relevant advances in models, inference, evaluation, and agent architecture when they produce measurable improvements in production performance. Set technical direction on ambiguous problems and raise the bar through design reviews, mentorship, and technical leadership.

Qualifications

  • Typically 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a track record of building and owning robust AI-powered, large-scale, user-facing or data-intensive products. Exceptional candidates with less experience and an outstanding record of impact are encouraged to apply.

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, with experience building and operating AI/ML products, backend services, or distributed systems at scale.

  • Experience owning the AI product lifecycle, including data analysis, rigorous evaluation, production monitoring, and iterative improvement. Able to define metrics and use production data and user feedback to guide decisions.

  • Practical experience in one or more relevant areas, such as agent harnesses, tool use, context engineering, model evaluation, browser automation, or long-running task execution.

  • Strong product judgment and execution: you can translate ambiguous user needs into applied AI or ML problems and ship durable solutions with measurable user impact.

  • Genuine interest in frontier AI capabilities, agent systems, and excitement for rapidly exploring, evaluating, and productizing new model behaviors.

Nice to have

  • Experience with LLM context engineering or harness engineering, experience with subagents, coding assistants, long-running or autonomous task execution.

  • Deep familiarity with the strengths and limitations of current model families across reasoning, tool use, context management, and long-horizon tasks.

  • Experience building agent permissions, safeguards, evaluation infrastructure, or production observability systems.

  • Experience with mid-training, post-training, or reinforcement learning for frontier or open-source models, along with a strong understanding of model strengths and limitations across reasoning, tool use, context management, and long-horizon tasks.

  • AI/ML research experience demonstrated through publications, open-source contributions, or other meaningful research impact.

  • Time spent at a fast-growing startup or on a high-ownership engineering team.

title: Technical Customer Success Manager, API
description:
Perplexity's API Platform brings our work in AI, search, and agent orchestration to developers. Our customers range from AI-native startups to some of the world's largest technology companies. Working with them, alongside our own developments in building Perplexity’s core application gives our team direct exposure to how search, models, and tools are used to build and scale AI-native products and applications.

About this role

We are looking for a technically fluent Customer Success Manager to help our API customers succeed and shape how we support them as the business grows. You will own a portfolio of customers, understand what they are building, and help them move from evaluation to production and broader adoption.

Alongside your accounts, you will lead projects such as product and endpoint migrations, customer enablement, and communications for product updates and incidents. You will work directly with customers developing AI products and with the engineers building the APIs they depend on. As an early member of the team, you will help shape our customer success programs and bring what you learn from customers into product decisions.

Responsibilities

  • Own customer relationships across onboarding, adoption, retention, and expansion, building trust with developers, technical leaders, and business stakeholders.

  • Understand each customer's use case, integration, and success criteria. Help them evaluate the APIs, resolve adoption barriers, and establish a path to production.

  • Use account and product usage data to identify declining adoption, technical risks, and growth opportunities, then work with customers on specific next steps.

  • Investigate technical questions using API documentation, sample requests, and usage data. Coordinate with Engineering and Support on deeper issues and keep customers informed through resolution.

  • Lead customer-facing programs such as endpoint migrations, product rollouts, and enablement. Define milestones, coordinate internal owners, and track customer readiness and completion.

  • Manage customer communications for product changes, deprecations, and outages, partnering with technical teams to provide accurate updates and clear guidance.

  • Build and improve the API customer success playbook, including onboarding, account reviews, customer health signals, escalation paths, and sales-to-CS handoffs.

  • Partner with Sales and account owners on renewals and expansion, using adoption, consumption, and business outcomes to demonstrate value and surface risks early.

  • Bring customer feedback into product planning and work with Developer Relations and Support on documentation and enablement that address recurring needs.

What we're looking for

  • 4+ years of experience in customer success, technical account management, solutions engineering, or a related customer-facing role at a technology company.

  • Technical fluency: comfortable reading API documentation, making API requests, interpreting responses and errors, and discussing integration questions with developers.

  • A track record of driving adoption, retention, or growth across a portfolio of customers, with clear ownership of follow-through.

  • Experience creating or improving a customer program, playbook, or cross-functional process, not only operating an established one.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical issues clearly and communicate carefully when facts are still developing.

  • Sound judgment in balancing account needs with strategic projects, setting priorities, and moving work forward without a detailed brief.

Nice to have

  • Experience with APIs, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, or usage-based products.

  • Familiarity with AI applications, search, retrieval, or agents, including how customers evaluate quality, latency, and cost.

  • Working knowledge of Python or SQL for reproducing issues, analyzing usage, or automating recurring work.

title: Sr. Business Recruiter, Communications & Marketing
description:
Perplexity is hiring an experienced Communications & Marketing Recruiter to help build the teams responsible for how our company and products are positioned, launched, explained, and experienced.

You will lead searches across Communications, Marketing, Social, Editorial, Content, Events and related functions. These disciplines require different networks and different ways of evaluating talent. A strong product marketer may need deep technical fluency and launch experience. A communications leader may be judged by the quality of their counsel and writing. A growth marketer needs to show measurable business impact.

This is a hands-on, full-cycle recruiting role. You will work closely with Communications and Marketing leaders to define each search, build the market, assess candidates, and close the people who can raise the quality of the work. You should be comfortable reading portfolios and writing samples, digging into campaign results, and separating individual contribution from team output.

You will also help us use AI more effectively across recruiting. That means applying it to research, talent mapping, outreach, and workflow automation while maintaining a high bar for judgment and candidate experience.

What You’ll Do

  • Own full-cycle recruiting across the Communications & Marketing team.

  • Partner with Communications and Marketing leaders from intake through close. Turn early or ambiguous briefs into clear candidate profiles, interview plans, and sourcing strategies.

  • Build talent maps across technology companies, consumer brands, enterprise software, media organizations, and agencies.

  • Develop sourcing strategies specific to each discipline. Know where strong writers, communications operators, product marketers, and performance-minded marketers build their reputations.

  • Evaluate candidates beyond titles and company names. Review portfolios and writing samples, understand campaign context, clarify individual ownership, and probe for measurable results.

  • Help hiring teams build structured work-sample and portfolio reviews that reflect the actual work of each role.

  • Give leaders direct, useful reads on pipeline quality, candidate tradeoffs, compensation, and the state of the market.

  • Represent Perplexity clearly and credibly. Explain the product, the pace of the company, and the opportunity without relying on a generic AI pitch.

  • Run a thoughtful candidate process from first conversation through close, including senior candidates with competing offers and high expectations for the recruiting experience.

  • Use AI tools for research, sourcing, outreach, and recruiting operations. Identify where automation improves speed and where recruiter judgment needs to stay central.

  • Track pipeline health and search performance, identify gaps early, and adjust the strategy before a search stalls.

What You Bring

  • 7+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, including meaningful depth across Communications and Marketing.

  • Experience hiring across several of the following areas: Product Marketing, Corporate or Executive Communications, Editorial, Content, Social Media, Brand, Growth, Demand Generation, Field Marketing, or Events.

  • A track record of partnering closely with senior Communications or Marketing leaders on important and difficult searches.

  • Strong functional judgment. You understand the differences between product marketing, communications, editorial, brand, growth, and field marketing, including which backgrounds transfer well between them.

  • Comfort evaluating portfolios, writing samples, campaign work, and business results alongside the hiring team.

  • Strong writing and communication skills. You can sharpen a search brief, write credible outreach, and communicate clearly with candidates and executives.

  • Experience recruiting in a high-growth startup or similarly fast-moving environment.

  • Hands-on experience using AI tools to improve sourcing, research, outreach, or recruiting workflows.

  • Fluency with modern ATS and recruiting systems. Experience with Ashby is preferred.

  • Sound judgment, attention to detail, and the willingness to push back when the market or candidate evidence does not support the original brief.

  • The ability to manage several distinct searches without giving candidates or hiring teams a generic experience.

title: Perplexity Research Fellowship
description:
Welcome to the application portal for the Perplexity Research Fellowship!

The Perplexity Research Fellowship is our flagship program for enabling the best early-career STEM talent to shape the future of frontier intelligence.

  • Please refer to the program homepage for full details on the Perplexity Research Fellowship and application process.

  • When you're ready to apply, please complete and submit the application form. Make sure to carefully follow all instructions.

  • We'll evaluate applications on a rolling basis, with priority consideration for submissions received by September 30, 2026.

  • You should write your application without assistance from other humans or AI models. Submitting writing from other humans or AI models as your own will result in permanent disqualification from employment at Perplexity.

  • Please note that the Perplexity Research Fellowship is not an internship program for students seeking research experience between school terms. If you're currently a student and your requested Fellowship start date is before your graduation date, we will request verified proof of an approved leave of absence of 1 year or greater from your university as a precondition to any Fellowship offer.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Search Core, Indexing & Data Pipeline Stream)
description:
Perplexity is looking for a highly skilled Expert Systems Engineer to join our Search Core team. For the indexing and data processing stream. This role is critical to building next-generation search products and technologies.

Responsibilities

  • Design and build core search engine components, especially indexing pipelines, data storage formats that operate at the scale of billions of pages

  • Develop streaming and batch data processing with YT systems for search index construction in a high-load environment

  • Push the limits of hardware performance through low-level optimizations and systems-level tuning

  • Tackle challenges in multithreading, concurrency, and system-level optimization

  • Design and build core search engine components, including indexing pipelines, retrieval algorithms, and ranking systems that operate at the scale of billions of pages

  • Develop streaming and batch data processing systems for search index construction in a high-load environment

  • Push the limits of hardware performance through low-level optimizations and systems-level tuning

  • Tackle challenges in multithreading, concurrency, and system-level optimization

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience in systems programming (Rust, C++, C, or similar)

  • Ownership of full project lifecycle you don't just write a fast inner loop, you care about how the system is built, deployed, operated, and scaled in production

  • Knowledge of Python or other scripting languages

  • Knowledge of Data processing systems (YT/Kafka/Hadoop)

  • Passion for writing clean, efficient, and scalable systems-level code

  • Strong knowledge of algorithms and data structures, and the ability to apply them effectively

  • Deep understanding of multithreading, including various approaches, challenges, and trade-offs

  • Experience building high-load, distributed, and hardware-adjacent services

  • Solid understanding of Linux internals (syscalls, networking stack, memory model, kernel tuning)

  • Familiarity with low-level optimization techniques (memory management, cache efficiency, SIMD, profiling)

Nice to have

  • Experience developing core components of search engines, databases, or information retrieval systems

  • Understanding of search fundamentals: indexing, query parsing, ranking, and relevance

  • Experience with trading systems or other latency-sensitive real-time systems

  • Familiarity with cloud services, Kubernetes, and AWS infrastructure

title: Member of Technical Staff, AI Products (Early Career - Industry)
description:
NOTE ON ELIGIBILITY: this role is for industry candidates already working in software engineering for the past 1+ years. New grads and current students should NOT apply to this role (instead, visit pplx.ai/newgrads).

About the role

In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people now use Perplexity to transform knowledge into action, through Search, Comet, and Computer. Product Engineering owns those experiences end to end, from the interface a user touches to the search and model calls behind it, on top of roughly 200M queries a day and a 200B+ URL index.

This is a full stack role in the truest sense. There are no frontend or backend lanes here, and no one waits for a ticket before starting. It suits people who love to build and want the room to do it. What you have shipped and how quickly you learn tell us far more than years on a resume or where you went to school.

What you will do

  • Own a user-facing surface end to end, from the interaction, design, and frontend through the application logic, APIs, data models, and the search or model calls behind them.

  • Ship to production continuously. New engineers typically have code in front of users in their first week.

  • Build with AI as a primary tool, not a novelty. We expect you to use agents and coding models aggressively to move faster, and to have sound judgment about when their output is wrong.

  • Turn ambiguous product ideas into working prototypes, then use real usage data and evals to decide what survives.

  • Raise the quality bar on reliability, latency, and craft for the surfaces you own.

  • Work directly with designers, PMs, and research engineers, without unnecessary process in between.

What we look for

  • 1+ years of professional software engineering experience, or a track record of strong internships where you shipped production code at scale.

  • Strong in at least one backend language, such as Python or Go, with real experience across services, APIs, and relational data modeling. Comfortable working in React and TypeScript on the frontend.

  • Real evidence of building: production work you understand in depth, shipped side projects with actual users, meaningful open-source contributions, hackathon wins, or research you turned into working software.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and an instinct to start building incrementally rather than wait for a spec.

  • Hands-on experience with AI products, with opinions about their rough edges and what that means for the product you are building.

Nice to have

  • Experience with our stack: React or Next.js, Python, Go, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, AWS. You will not be expected to know all of it on day one.

  • Experience building on top of LLMs: AI orchestration, RAG, evals, agents, tool use.

  • Product taste. You can tell a good interface from a bad one and explain how to improve it.

  • A public track record we can read, such as GitHub, a technical blog, or a demo we can try.

title: Payroll Analyst
description:
Perplexity is looking for a detail-oriented Payroll Analyst to join our growing Finance and Accounting team. You will partner closely with the Payroll Manager to keep US and international payroll accurate, compliant, and timely as the company scales through rapid hiring, global expansion, and increasing complexity in equity and benefits administration.

 

This is a hands-on role with real ownership from day one, working closely with People Operations, Accounting, Tax, and Equity. The ideal candidate combines strong payroll and systems expertise with sharp attention to detail, a service-oriented approach, and the ability to bring structure to a fast-moving environment.

 

Responsibilities

 

  • US and international payroll processing: Own day-to-day processing support for US multi-state semi-monthly payroll and assist with international payroll cycles across approximately 16 countries, working primarily in Rippling.

  • Global contractor payroll: Run the monthly global contractor payroll cycle, including timecard submission tracking, manager approval follow-up, and on-schedule contractor payments.

  • Pre- and post-payroll audits: Reconcile benefit deductions, 401(k) deferrals, and employer match against payroll journals and deductions exports; flag and resolve discrepancies before paychecks post.

  • State tax account administration: Support state-level employer tax account registration and maintenance (SUI and withholding) as the company grows into new states, including migration of legacy accounts inherited from prior PEO arrangements.

  • Benefits and 401(k) support: Assist with 401(k) and benefits administration, including contribution monitoring, HCE and nondiscrimination testing support, and COBRA offboarding notices.

  • Equity payroll reporting: Support equity and stock-exercise payroll reporting by tracking Carta exercise data, applying correct NSO/ISO tax treatment, and preparing payroll-side entries at quarter-end cutoffs.

  • Reimbursements and systems integration: Manage the Rippling-to-NetSuite reimbursement approval chain, ensuring expense reimbursements route and post correctly across systems.

  • Employee support: Serve as a first point of contact for employee payroll inquiries, resolving routine questions and escalating complex cases with context.

  • Close and compliance support: Maintain clean, audit-ready documentation and support quarter-end and year-end close activities, including W-2s, ACA reporting, 401(k) true-ups, and year-end reconciliations.

  • Process improvement: Identify and help implement process improvements that reduce manual work and strengthen controls as payroll volume and jurisdictional complexity increase.

 

Requirements

 

  • 4+ years of hands-on payroll experience, ideally including multi-state US payroll; international or contractor payroll exposure is a plus.

  • Experience establishing and managing US state agency accounts, including troubleshooting agency mailings and invoices for payment, and related account maintenance.

  • Strong working knowledge of California wage statement requirements, meal and rest break premiums, final pay timing rules, and other state-specific compliance considerations.

  • Hands-on experience with a modern payroll/HRIS platform (Rippling, Workday, ADP, Gusto, or similar); Rippling experience preferred.

  • Comfort with detailed reconciliation work across benefits deductions, 401(k) match calculations, and payroll-to-GL tie-outs, including strong Excel and Google Sheets skills and the ability to work accurately with large datasets.

  • Working knowledge of US payroll tax compliance (SUI, SIT, federal and state withholding) and interest in learning cross-border payroll mechanics.

  • Familiarity with equity compensation payroll (RSU, NSO, and ISO taxation) is a plus.

  • Excellent attention to detail and follow-through — this role exists to catch errors before they reach employees, not just process transactions.

  • Clear communicator who can explain payroll and benefits topics to employees and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Ability to multi-task and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment.

title: Global Mobility Lead
description:
About the job

We're looking for an experienced Global Mobility Lead to build and run the programs that help employees join, move, and work across borders. You will own our mobility policies, immigration casework, and vendor relationships, and partner with Legal, Finance, and People Ops to make cross-border moves clear, compliant, and well supported.

What you’ll own

Global mobility

  • Own the mobility policy suite end to end: relocation, permanent transfers, short-term and long-term international assignments, remote/cross-border work arrangements, and business travel thresholds.

  • Run individual mobility cases from scoping to landing: package design, cost estimates, immigration sequencing, tax and social-security implications, payroll setup, relocation logistics, and post-arrival support.

  • Manage employment-based immigration casework in partnership with outside counsel: H-1B (including cap-subject and change-of-employer/AC21 timing), L-1, TN, E-3, O-1, F-1 OPT/CPT, and employer-sponsored permanent residence. Own the internal timeline, the start-date reality check, and the manager/candidate communication.

  • Own daily immigration intake and case execution, including employer questionnaires, supporting documents, employment verification letters, signatures, counsel follow ups, and case closure.

  • Own right-to-work compliance across jurisdictions: I-9 and E-Verify in the US, Home Office share-code checks in the UK, and equivalent checks in our EU and other markets.

  • Decide and document the entity/employment model for each new market (direct entity, EOR, or non-resident payroll registration) with Finance and Legal.

  • Own our mobility vendor stack (immigration counsel, relocation, tax, EOR/global payroll): scope, SLAs, cost, and performance.

  • Model and track mobility cost, including sponsorship and premium-processing fees, so leadership can make go/no-go calls with real numbers, and obtain and document required approvals before committing sponsorship or spend

Data and systems

  • Build the tracking layer: mobility case pipeline, immigration deadlines and expirations, compensation comparisons, etc.

  • Stand up mobility dashboards: case volume, cycle time, cost per move, band penetration, offer-to-band variance, and equity-gap trend.

  • Write the employee-facing documentation so moves and pay decisions are predictable and explainable, not one-off negotiations.

What we’re looking for

Required

  • 6+ years of experience in global mobility, with real ownership of cross-border moves and immigration casework, not just vendor hand-offs.

  • Working fluency in US employment-based immigration and at least one other major jurisdiction’s work-authorization regime (UK, EU, or Canada).

  • Strong analytical skills: comfortable in spreadsheets and HRIS reporting, able to build a defensible model and explain the assumptions behind it.

  • Judgment about risk. You know when to escalate to Legal, when to flag classification or permanent-establishment exposure, and how to say no clearly.

  • Excellent written communication: you’ll draft policies, verification letters, offer rationales, and executive-facing recommendations.

  • Comfort with ambiguity, high volume, and shifting priorities.

title: Member of Data Staff (Analytics Engineer)
description:
Perplexity is AI for people who expect more. On the data team, that means building the systems that make our data reliable, understandable, and usable by both humans and AI.

We're looking for an analytics engineer or data engineer who wants to build the foundation for an AI-native data organization. You'll design core data models, pipelines, semantic layers, data quality systems, governance practices, and warehouse workflows that power the entire company: helping teams make strategic decisions, operate the business, and move faster with trusted data. You'll also make sure those systems are secure, privacy-aware, and legible to AI agents, data scientists, and the rest of the company.

This role is for someone who can operate at the boundary of analytics engineering, data engineering, data governance, and internal product. You care about dimensional modeling, dbt standards, cost-aware warehouse design, access controls, privacy, and the details that make data trustworthy. You also believe AI should make the data stack faster, easier to maintain, and more accessible across the company without weakening security or governance.

What You'll Do

  • Build the core data foundation - design and maintain high-quality data models, marts, and pipelines that make analysis fast, reliable, and reusable.

  • Manage the data warehouse - help own warehouse architecture, environments, permissions, performance, cost, data lifecycle, and operational hygiene so the platform scales cleanly.

  • Make the warehouse AI-readable - own the documentation, semantic context, metadata, lineage, and retrieval patterns that AI systems depend on to understand and query Perplexity's data correctly.

  • Own data modeling standards - define and champion dbt patterns, dimensional modeling practices, naming conventions, tests, and review processes.

  • Lead data governance practices - define standards for access, ownership, lineage, documentation, retention, quality, and sensitive data handling across the analytical warehouse.

  • Build with security and privacy in mind - partner with engineering, security, legal, and finance where needed to ensure data access, sharing, and AI-enabled workflows are appropriate and controlled.

  • Automate data quality and maintenance - build AI-assisted workflows that detect issues, explain root causes, suggest fixes, generate tests, and reduce manual firefighting.

  • Improve data team productivity - automate repetitive workflows, improve tooling, streamline development, and make it easier for data scientists and stakeholders to answer questions.

  • Partner across the company - work closely with data scientists, engineering, product, finance, and GTM teams to translate analytical needs into durable data systems.

  • Shape tooling decisions - evaluate build-versus-buy tradeoffs, manage vendor relationships when needed, and choose tools that scale with the team.

What We're Looking For

  • 6+ years of experience as an analytics engineer, data engineer, data scientist, or closely related role.

  • Deep SQL expertise - you can reason about correctness, performance, joins, grain, and edge cases in complex warehouse queries.

  • Strong data modeling experience - you've worked hands-on with dbt (or a similar transformation framework) in production, and you understand dimensional modeling, data contracts, testing, and how analytical schemas should evolve.

  • Pipeline ownership - you've built, maintained, debugged, and improved production data pipelines.

  • Warehouse management experience - you've worked with warehouse administration, access patterns, permissions, performance tuning, cost management, or operational ownership.

  • Governance mindset - you think clearly about data ownership, access controls, privacy, retention, lineage, auditability, and the risks of making data too easy to access.

  • AI-native working style - you already use AI to speed up development, documentation, QA, exploration, and repetitive workflow automation.

  • Stakeholder fluency - you know how to turn messy analytical requirements into trusted models, metrics, and reusable data assets.

  • Autonomy and execution - you can take projects from ambiguous problem to production-quality system with minimal oversight.

  • Operational judgment - you care about reliability, governance, security, cost, and long-term maintainability.

Bonus

  • Snowflake administration, optimization, cost management, or warehouse performance tuning.

  • Experience with RBAC, PII handling, data classification, retention policies, audit workflows, or privacy/security reviews.

  • Experience with Databricks or other modern data infrastructure.

  • Experience building semantic layers, metrics layers, metadata systems, or data catalogs.

  • Python experience for data tooling, automation, orchestration, or quality checks.

  • Previous experience as an early analytics engineer or data engineer at a high-growth startup.

Why This Role

  • Own the foundation - your work will determine how fast and confidently the company can use data.

  • Build for humans and AI - the next generation of data infrastructure needs to be understandable by agents as well as analysts.

  • High leverage - better models, pipelines, and tools multiply every data scientist and every stakeholder who depends on data.

  • Small team, broad scope - you'll have room to define standards, choose tools, and ship systems that become company-wide defaults.

title: Member of Technical Staff (New Grad)
description:
APPLICATIONS CLOSED

The general application portal has closed for 2026. We will reopen applications at some point in 2027. Thank you for your interest in Perplexity careers!

Welcome! This is the general application portal for university students and recent graduates who wish to be considered for full-time Member of Technical Staff positions at Perplexity. Our elite new grad cohorts enjoy unparalleled mentorship, top-of-market compensation, and the chance to tackle some of the deepest, thorniest challenges in frontier intelligence.

NOTE: if you attend one of our focus schools listed below, please do not apply via this portal as it is infrequently monitored due to high volume. Apply instead via the school-specific application portal below to ensure your application receives priority attention.

Focus schools (United States) - application portals

Caltech | Columbia | Cornell | CMU | Duke | Georgia Tech
Harvard | MIT | Michigan | Northwestern | NYU | Penn
Princeton | Purdue | Stanford | UC Berkeley | UChicago
UCLA | UIUC | UNC Chapel Hill | UT Austin
UWashington | Yale

Focus Schools (Canada) - application portals

McGill | UBC | UToronto | Waterloo

Early Career Talent @ Perplexity

​Perplexity believes that exceptionally talented individuals at any stage can thrive in our high-velocity, high-ownership culture. ​Our early career talent program revolves around:

  • ​Breadth: New grads at Perplexity work across the stack, from Perplexity's agent harnesses to our AI inference and training systems. Many of our most beloved features and most important systems were shipped by individuals fresh out of school.

  • ​Depth: New grads are entrusted (and expected) to dive deep into whatever problem domains you work on. Often, your work will require you to become a world expert in some problem space that few others in the world have encountered.

  • ​Mentorship & Growth: We keep the size of our entering new grad cohorts at well below 10% of our technical team. Each individual enjoys a rich network of mentors to help them grow, and our new grads have a track record of becoming some of Perplexity's most senior and prolific team members.

  • ​Recognition: We select for the best and we recognize them accordingly. We set our early career compensation to rise well above that of top tech companies and startups. Post-hire, we aggressively recognize and reward growth in role.

  • ​Mission: Perplexity is AI for people who expect more. Our mission is to build frontier intelligence for the world's most discerning users, and each contribution you make will directly advance that mission.

Academic requirements

If you're not applying from a focus school listed above, we typically require you to possess the following qualifications:

  1. GPA of ≥3.92, averaged across all CS and Math classes; and

  2. Grade of A or A+ in your school's upper-level algorithms course.

Additional advanced coursework in areas such as systems, AI/ML, advanced math, and other rigorous subjects is highly welcome.

 

Non-qualifying applications - evidence of exceptional ability

While you're welcome to submit your application if you don't meet these criteria, we will be looking for other evidence of exceptional ability. You are encouraged to briefly describe this evidence in response to the "Anything Else" question at the bottom of the application form.

Note on fellowship opportunities

This portal accepts applications for full-time roles at Perplexity. Internship applications are not accepted via this portal. If you're interested in short-term opportunities with our team, you may instead be interested in the Perplexity Research Fellowship. The Fellowship has a separate application process detailed here. Note that Fellowship applications are extremely competitive; in particular, we don't expect to admit any undergraduate students to the Fellowship before their final year of study.

title: Global Workplace Business Operations Lead
description:
Overview

The Workplace Experience team powers and connects the workday for all Perplexity employees across our global offices.

We are hospitality and experience-driven at the core. We are made up of People people, meaning that we love supporting each other and all of the People in our workplace. We take on the good and the bad with optimism and with a positive, kind approach to solving problems, dealing with the obstacles handed to us, and proactively creating good around us. We think about each moment through the lens of our colleagues (our customers) so that we can create thoughtful and memorable experiences no matter what task we have at hand.

As our Global Workplace Business Operations Lead, you will manage the business operations and cross-functional program delivery that enable our global Workplace Experience team to scale. In collaboration with the Head of Workplace Experience, you will set the operating framework for your areas, make decisions within agreed priorities and approval limits, and remain hands-on in delivering results. You will own the effectiveness of portfolio operating processes and internal project delivery.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the Workplace operating framework: Lead annual and quarterly planning for your areas, translate team strategy into priorities and resource plans, and establish clear decision rights, delivery commitments and measures of success. Resolve sequencing and capacity trade-offs within agreed parameters and recommend when to add people, vendors or technology.

  • Lead internal capital-project delivery: Take accountability for integrated delivery plans across office openings, refreshes and other capital initiatives. Direct the work of external PMs within agreed scopes, align internal workstreams, resolve delivery issues and hold partners accountable for schedule, cost, quality and operational readiness.

  • Own portfolio controls and insight: Establish dependable lease administration, obligation tracking, space and occupancy information, and portfolio reporting. Set data and control standards, ensure actions have owners, and turn trends and risks into recommendations before deadlines or capacity constraints become problems.

  • Drive financial planning and performance: Own the processes and quality of operating and capital forecasts, commitments, actuals and variance analysis in partnership with Finance. Challenge assumptions, recommend corrective actions and investment trade-offs, and give the Head of Workplace Experience a reliable basis for budget and commitment decisions.

  • Set the systems and reporting roadmap: Own business requirements, governance and improvement priorities for workplace tools such as Envoy. Establish useful performance measures, improve data quality, and automate repeatable work while maintaining appropriate controls and keeping processes practical for the team.

  • Lead EHS program governance: Establish a risk-based plan, clear responsibilities and a review cadence with qualified vendors and internal teams. Drive follow-through on assessed obligations and remediation across offices and remote populations, maintain evidence of completion, and escalate material risks without substituting for specialist advice.

  • Set standards for delivery and handover: Own the development and use of project playbooks, planning processes and operational-readiness criteria. Bring together design standards and occupancy requirements, and ensure completed projects transfer to local operations with the documentation, training, vendor arrangements and issue ownership needed to run well.

  • Serve as a senior operating partner: Lead cross-functional operating and project reviews, surface decisions with clear recommendations, and represent your areas with internal and external partners. Drive resolution within your authority, escalate material changes with options, and build accountability without adding unnecessary layers.

What You Bring

  • Senior functional leadership: 8+ years in workplace business operations, corporate real estate, facilities programs or a closely related field, with increasing responsibility for complex, multi-site programs and their outcomes. You have operated with substantial autonomy, not only administered plans set by others.

  • Project and program management expertise: You are a project manager at the core. You are quick and agile, but methodical when it comes to planning for, organizing, tracking, and executing on a project in a way that keeps everything and everyone aligned and on task.

  • Relevant delivery depth: You have a record of delivering office buildouts, relocations or capital improvements as an internal owner, with accountability for scope, financial performance, schedules, change control and external delivery partners.

  • Strong financial and analytical judgment: You have experience driving forecasting and reporting processes, challenging assumptions and translating portfolio data into resource or investment recommendations; strong spreadsheet and analytical skills.

  • Experience building an operating framework: You have established planning, governance, performance measures and systems that helped a growing function deliver more predictably. You know when structure improves execution and when it becomes unnecessary process.

  • Leadership across organizational boundaries: You can secure commitments, challenge constructively and resolve competing priorities across teams and vendors. You communicate risks and recommendations credibly to senior leaders and know which decisions to make independently and which to escalate.

  • Hands-on ownership and sound judgment: You can move between portfolio-level trade-offs and project details, deliver through others without losing accountability, handle sensitive information responsibly, and maintain a kind, service-oriented approach under pressure.

  • Helpful, not required: International portfolio experience, workplace technology ownership, EHS program governance, or a relevant project-management credential.

title: Director of Events and Experiences
description:
Perplexity is seeking a Director of Events to own our external events worldwide: the ones we host, the stages we speak on, and the ones we sponsor. You will set the strategy, run production, manage the budget, and build the team. If you have produced a flagship and a dinner in the same week, know what a good sponsorship deal looks like, and want to build an events function from the ground up, this role is for you.

Responsibilities

  • Own events. Hosted, speaking, sponsored. Strategy, budget, production, results.

  • Set the calendar. Decide which events we run, which we speak at, and which we skip.

  • Produce hosted events. Launches, dinners, summits, roadshows. Concept, programming, venue, vendors, run of show.

  • Run the speaking program. Pick the stages. Prepare the speakers.

  • Manage sponsorships. Negotiate terms, design our footprint, and account for the spend.

  • Run field events with Sales. Get the right customers in the room. Make sure someone follows up.

  • Be Perplexity. Our events should look and feel like our product. Work with Brand and Creative on every one.

  • Lead the team. Equal parts IC and manager.

  • Build the system. Playbooks, event tiers, intake, vendors, agencies, budgets.

  • Measure. Attendance, coverage, pipeline, signups. Know which events worked and stop doing the ones that didn't.

  • Be on site. For the events that matter, you are in the room.

Qualifications

  • 12+ years producing events, including large hosted events, sponsorships, and field programs, ideally in-house at a technology company.

  • Has built or led an events team.

  • Has owned large budgets, agency relationships, and vendor contracts.

  • Has negotiated sponsorships and knows a bad deal when they see one.

  • Has run an executive speaking program: selecting stages, preparing speakers, managing the day.

  • Knows production: run of show, staging, AV, registration, staffing, security, permits.

  • Drives measurement. Has built event attribution and tracked brand sentiment, and reports what each event returned.

  • Can partner with Sales, Product, Comms, Brand, Finance, Legal, and executives.

  • Power user of AI tools. Most of your work already runs through them, and you can show us how.

  • Based in San Francisco or New York. Willing to travel internationally.

title: Engineering Manager (Enterprise)
description:
Perplexity is continuing to rapidly scale our Enterprise Engineering Organization and seeking Engineering Managers with deep expertise across the Enterprise domain to help lead the next wave of growth.

As an Enterprise Engineering Manager, you will combine technical judgment, product intuition, and people leadership to help large organizations adopt AI at scale. We are hiring across the enterprise control plane, enterprise data plane, and connector marketplace and activation. Depending on your area of focus, you will lead and grow a team in one of these areas, addressing challenges such as:

Enterprise Control Plane: Building the identity, security, and governance foundations that enable large organizations to deploy Perplexity confidently, including SSO, SCIM, role-based access, customer-managed encryption keys (BYOK), admin APIs, and enforceable policies governing access to data, models, and tools. Supporting regulated-industry requirements, including SOC 2, HIPAA, data governance, and residency, with audit logs and analytics that give administrators visibility into how Perplexity is used.

Enterprise Data Plane: Building the connector platform and semantic data layer that give Computer reliable, permission-aware access to enterprise systems and knowledge, including managed authorization, private-system access, and data freshness.

Connector Marketplace and Activation: Building discovery, recommendations, onboarding, and marketplace experiences that help customers find and adopt integrations, while working with partners to expand the connector ecosystem.

Across these areas, you will translate enterprise customer needs into scalable technical solutions across Perplexity’s products.

Responsibilities

  • Set technical direction for your team and guide architecture decisions across the enterprise platform.

  • Build the foundational systems that enable large organizations to deploy Perplexity broadly and confidently.

  • Shape roadmaps with product and design, applying strong technical judgment and product intuition.

  • Set a high bar for reliability, code quality, testing, and maintenance. Lead incident response and ensure platform changes and connector migrations are rolled out safely.

  • Partner with engineering teams across the company to ensure the platforms we build are extensible and easy to adopt.

  • Represent engineering in strategic enterprise customer conversations, partnering with sales and customer success to understand requirements and remove barriers to adoption.

  • Oversee hiring, onboarding, and mentorship for a rapidly growing team. Develop rigorous interview pipelines and work closely with recruiting to source candidates.

  • Work with Perplexity’s co-founders to deliver enterprise engineering priorities.

Qualifications

  • Strong technical judgment and experience building enterprise platforms or products, with an understanding of the reliability, security, and usability requirements of enterprise customers.

  • Domain expertise in at least one of the following areas:

    • Enterprise control plane: identity and access management, SSO/SCIM, role-based access, key management, admin APIs, policy enforcement, audit logging, data governance, or compliance and residency requirements for regulated industries.

    • Enterprise data plane: connector and integration platforms, including authentication, source-system permissions, data synchronization, and reliability at scale; or semantic data layers and knowledge platforms that make enterprise data accessible and useful to AI.

    • Connector marketplace and activation: discovery and recommendation systems, integration onboarding, marketplace product UX, or technology partner ecosystems.

  • Ability to deliver in a fast-moving environment while balancing customer needs, technical quality, and long-term maintainability.

  • Detail-oriented and quality-focused - our customers run critical workflows on Perplexity, and our product needs to stay robust and reliable.

  • Ability to translate enterprise customer needs into clear technical priorities and communicate tradeoffs effectively.

  • Experience building and managing high-performing engineering teams, with a strong management practice grounded in clear feedback, effective 1:1s, career development, and recruiting and retaining high-caliber talent.

  • Ability to lead parallel technical initiatives, align strong technical perspectives, and make clear prioritization and tradeoff decisions.

  • Experience with AI/ML products, enterprise AI adoption, or scaling enterprise platforms at a startup is a plus.

  • 8+ years of engineering experience, with at least 4 of those years as an engineering manager.

title: Product Manager, Platform
description:
What you’ll do

  • Understand the needs of the teams that use our platforms and the customers who depend on them. Use product data, operational feedback, and recurring quality issues to identify the highest-impact problems, and then solve them.

  • Turn recurring needs into shared services, tools, and workflows that reduce duplicated work. Exercise judgment about when to build a reusable capability, use an existing solution, or take a simpler approach.

  • Work directly with product, engineering, and operational teams to understand their workflows, identify recurring problems, and anticipate the capabilities they will need next.

  • Prioritize platform investments across new product enablement, reliability, efficiency, and technical debt. Make clear tradeoffs between near-term delivery and long-term flexibility.

  • Define and track success through business impact, reliability, cost to serve, and reduced manual work, connecting these measures to customer and business outcomes.

  • Partner closely with engineering on technical tradeoffs, build-versus-buy decisions, and rollout plans. Write clear requirements and drive delivery from problem definition through launch and iteration.

Qualifications

  • Experience owning product strategy and execution on technical products and platforms, or shared systems used by multiple teams such as billing and monetization, identity and access, developer platforms, data and experimentation, internal tooling, support, etc.

  • Strong technical fluency. You can reason about APIs, data flows, system dependencies, and failure modes, and work closely with engineers on consequential tradeoffs.

  • Strong analytical skills. You can investigate problems independently, define meaningful metrics, and evaluate the impact of platform investments.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to align teams around priorities and make difficult decisions when their needs compete.

  • High ownership and sound judgment in a fast-moving environment. You are comfortable moving between long-term strategy and hands-on execution without adding unnecessary process.

  • A focus on customer outcomes and product quality, including when your immediate users are internal teams.

Where this person needs to spike

  • Systems thinker, detail-oriented, problem solver. This person needs to have experience wrangling thorny, complex problems. We need someone that is excited about diving into messy workflows, reading through dozens of support tickets, thinking through edge cases no one’s thought of, assuming different behavior across platforms, proactively considering enterprise vs. consumer workflows, etc.

  • Experience working on platforms with multiple stakeholders and non-trivial tradeoffs. This person is building products simultaneously for customers, agents, and other internal employees.

  • Is “AI-native.” Can build AI products whose outputs require evaluation, safeguards, and human-in-the-loop design.

  • Strong analytical skills and experience defining metrics in ambiguity, breaking down workflows, and using quantitative and qualitative evidence to prioritize.

  • Some experience working on critical software: support platforms/agents, legal/compliance tooling, identity and account tooling, billing, fraud, trust-and safety, etc.

  • High-ownership. This person needs to feel dissatisfied by the current support flow, and hungry to do whatever it takes to clear the backlog.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Machine Learning Engineer, Search Agent RL)
description:
Perplexity is seeking an experienced Machine Learning Engineer to advance how AI systems search, reason, and work together to solve complex problems. Our work spans search and retrieval, LLM post-training, multi-agent training, and the harnesses that make these systems effective.

We control the full stack: the models, the agent harnesses, and the search infrastructure underneath. That gives us the freedom to develop new approaches across all three training models to use search more effectively, designing tools and execution environments around learned behavior, and improving retrieval to support how agents actually work.

Responsibilities

  • Push search and agent quality forward through improvements to models, training data, tools, and system design.

  • Develop LLM post-training methods, including reinforcement learning, to improve reasoning, search, tool use, and task completion.

  • Train and evaluate multi-agent systems, exploring how agents divide work, share information, and coordinate effectively.

  • Design and build agent harnesses around the tools, context management, execution environments, and orchestration that support reliable work over many steps.

  • Improve retrieval and ranking models and the search interfaces agents use to find and assess information.

  • Build datasets, reward signals, and evaluations that expose meaningful failures and guide improvements.

  • Own experiments end to end, from a clear hypothesis to scalable training, deployment, and measurable gains in quality, latency, and cost.

  • Collaborate with AI, Search, Infrastructure, Data, and Product teams to bring new capabilities into production.

Qualifications

  • A strong track record of building and shipping ML systems, with deep experience in one or more of LLM post-training, reinforcement learning, search and retrieval, or agent systems.

  • Strong software engineering skills and the ability to work across model training, experimentation infrastructure, and production systems.

  • Experience designing rigorous evaluations, diagnosing failures, and translating experimental results into practical improvements.

  • Comfort with open-ended problems that require both research judgment and hands-on engineering.

  • A strong sense of ownership, curiosity, and the drive to carry an idea through to a working system.

Nice to have

  • Experience with training models to use tools or complete tasks over many steps.

  • Multi-agent training, coordination, or evaluation.

  • Building agent harnesses, distributed training systems, or scalable inference infrastructure.

  • Large-scale retrieval, ranking, or recommendation systems.

title: Billing Operations Lead
description:
Perplexity is looking for an experienced Billing Operations Manager to join our Finance and Accounting team as we scale our enterprise business. You will own the enterprise billing lifecycle, translating complex commercial agreements into accurate, timely invoices and building the processes and controls that support our growth.

This is a hands-on role working closely with Deal Desk, Enterprise Sales, Legal, and Customer Success. The ideal candidate combines strong billing and systems expertise with sound judgement, a customer-focused approach, and the ability to bring structure to a fast-moving environment.

Responsibilities

  • Enterprise and reseller billing: Own enterprise billing operations from customer and subscription setup through recurring invoicing, renewals, amendments, and cancellations, ensuring accurate and timely billing in accordance with executed agreements.

  • Contract review: Partner with Enterprise Sales and Deal Desk to review nonstandard billing terms before contracts are signed, assess operational feasibility, and route exceptions for approval.

  • Complex billing arrangements: Translate approved pricing and contractual terms into billing configurations and schedules, including seat changes, tiered discounting, prorations, co-terminations, prepaid credits, and usage billed in arrears.

  • Billing inquiries and disputes: Serve as the primary point of contact for enterprise billing questions from customers and internal teams. Investigate discrepancies, coordinate approved credits and rebills, and address underlying causes to prevent recurring issues.

  • Reconciliations and close support: Reconcile contract, subscription, and usage data to billing output and investigate any billing discrepancies. Support month-end close and audits through billing completeness checks, reconciliations, and supporting documentation.

  • Integration management: Identifying and resolving any billing system integration failures.

  • Customer Success and renewal support: Partner with Customer Success, Enterprise Sales, and Deal Desk on renewals, expansions, and changes to customer commitments. Prepare seat, usage, and billing analyses; calculate renewal credits and true-ups; and translate approved agreements into accurate subscription, credit, and invoice updates. Coordinate the resolution of billing issues that could delay renewals or disrupt the customer experience.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in Accounting or Finance.

  • 7+ years of experience in billing operations, order management, order-to-cash, revenue operations, or a related finance function, including hands-on ownership of enterprise SaaS or subscription billing.

  • Billing expertise: Demonstrated ability to interpret complex customer agreements and translate them into accurate billing schedules, invoices, and adjustments, including subscription and usage-based arrangements.

  • Systems proficiency: Hands-on experience with NetSuite, Salesforce, tax engines, and subscription or usage-based billing platforms, with the ability to investigate issues across connected systems.

  • Accounting fundamentals: Working knowledge of accounts receivable, deferred revenue, and revenue-recognition concepts, including ASC 606.

  • Resourcefulness, detail-oriented and a motivation for solving problems and finding solutions.

  • Excellent communication skills, as frequent interaction with both internal and external stakeholders will be required.

  • Ability to multi-task and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment.

title: Enterprise Sales Manager
description:
About the role

As an Enterprise Sales Manager at Perplexity, you'll lead a team of Account Executives selling Perplexity Enterprise and Computer to Enterprise accounts. You'll be responsible for hiring and ramping the team, coaching sellers through complex enterprise sales cycles, and owning team revenue targets.

Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Account Executives, providing regular feedback to drive individual and team performance

  • Own team revenue targets, with accountability for pipeline creation, deal execution, and forecast accuracy

  • Hire, onboard, and ramp new Account Executives in partnership with Recruiting and Enablement

  • Coach the team on outbound prospecting, account planning, and converting existing self-serve customers into Enterprise relationships

  • Support AEs in complex, multi-stakeholder deals, including executive alignment, technical evaluation, security review, and negotiation

  • Run a regular cadence of 1:1s, pipeline reviews, and deal reviews, maintaining accurate Salesforce data and forecasts

  • Partner with Enablement, Product, Marketing, Customer Success, and RevOps to translate field feedback into action

You may be a good fit if

  • 7+ years of enterprise software sales experience, with 3+ years directly managing quota-carrying Account Executives

  • A track record of meeting or exceeding team revenue targets in a high-growth environment

  • Experience hiring, ramping, and developing sellers
