  • Experience coaching teams to generate their own pipeline through outbound and account-based prospecting

  • Strong command of Salesforce, pipeline management, and forecasting

  • Background selling technical products, ideally AI, data, or infrastructure

  • Comfort operating without an established playbook

title: Commercial Sales Manager
description:
About the role

As a Commercial Sales Manager at Perplexity, you'll lead a team of Commercial Account Executives selling Perplexity Enterprise and Computer to small and mid-sized organizations. You'll be responsible for hiring and ramping the team, coaching sellers through efficient, high-velocity sales cycles, and owning team revenue targets.

Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Commercial Account Executives, providing regular feedback to drive individual and team performance

  • Own team revenue, logo, and activity targets, with accountability for pipeline creation, deal velocity, and forecast accuracy

  • Hire, onboard, and ramp new Account Executives in partnership with Recruiting and Enablement

  • Coach the team on outbound prospecting, account prioritization, and converting existing self-serve customers into Enterprise relationships

  • Help AEs qualify with discipline and run efficient sales cycles from discovery through close, partnering with Enterprise AEs when an account warrants a larger motion

  • Run a regular cadence of 1:1s, pipeline reviews, and deal reviews, maintaining accurate Salesforce data and forecasts

  • Partner with Enablement, Product, Marketing, Customer Success, and RevOps to translate field feedback into action

You may be a good fit if

  • 5+ years of SaaS sales experience selling to small and mid-sized organizations, with 2+ years directly managing quota-carrying Account Executives

  • A track record of meeting or exceeding team revenue targets in a high-growth environment

  • Experience hiring, ramping, and developing sellers

  • Experience coaching teams to generate their own pipeline through outbound and product-led signals in a high-velocity sales motion

  • Strong command of Salesforce, pipeline management, and forecasting

  • Background selling technical products, ideally AI, data, or infrastructure

  • Comfort operating without an established playbook

title: Member of Technical Staff (Search Crawler Analyst)
description:
The internet is vast, containing trillions of URLs. Perplexity’s crawling and storage system is complex and has multiple stages (URL discovery, crawling, parsing, indexing). Each stage offers many opportunities for improvement and room for intricate bugs. You’ll work at the intersection of data analysis and engineering — designing metrics, building data pipelines, and improving the quality of our search and answer systems.

Responsibilities

  • Find and diagnose quality issues in our crawling pipeline

  • Train small models that optimize particular aspects of the pipeline (e.g. parsing quality)

  • Build datasets for model training, including LLM-as-a-judge labeling pipelines

  • Improve page selection algorithms for indexing

  • Design and analyze experiments to validate improvements

Qualifications

  • 4+ years of experience as a data analyst, ML engineer, or in a related role

  • Strong coding skills: you should be able to write production-grade code at the level of a mid-level backend engineer

  • Experience designing metrics from scratch

  • Experience training ML models that shipped to production with measurable metric improvements

Nice to have

  • Direct experience working on web crawling or indexing pipelines

title: Customer Success Lead
description:
As Customer Success Lead at Perplexity, you’ll lead the team responsible for helping enterprises adopt Perplexity Computer and our API products, turning adoption into measurable business value. You’ll own the customer success strategy and operating model, lead CSMs across customer segments, and be accountable for gross and net revenue retention across the post-sale book, with expansion targets shared with Sales.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll stay close to customers and the product while building the team, programs, and cross-functional partnerships that help us scale.

Responsibilities

  • Own gross and net revenue retention for the customer base, including renewal forecasting, risk management, and expansion targets shared with Sales

  • Set the customer success strategy, and coverage model across high-touch Enterprise, scaled SMB and Mid-Market, and technical API customers

  • Hire, coach, and develop CSMs across customer segments, establishing a regular cadence of 1:1s, account and renewal reviews, and a clear bar for performance and product expertise

  • Build the playbooks the team runs on, including Sales-to-CS handoffs, onboarding, customer success plans, health scoring, executive business reviews, and escalations

  • Partner with Applied AI and Enablement to build onboarding, workshops, champion programs, and scaled education that help customers reach first value and sustain adoption

  • Help customers connect adoption and consumption to business outcomes, understand usage and cost trade-offs, and build a clear case for renewal and expansion

  • Partner with Sales to identify self-serve customers ready to move to Enterprise and to plan expansion in named accounts

  • Work with RevOps and Finance on capacity planning, account assignment, book-of-business design, and accurate reporting in Salesforce

  • Partner with cross-functional teams to deliver a cohesive customer journey, with clear ownership and handoffs from onboarding through adoption, renewal, and expansion

  • Coordinate customer readiness and communications for product launches, migrations, pricing and usage changes, and incidents, partnering with Product, Marketing, Support, and Engineering on accurate guidance

  • Bring customer needs and recurring friction into product planning, and close the loop with customers on decisions and progress

  • Engage executive sponsors at our largest accounts and step in personally on strategic adoption efforts, high-stakes renewals, and escalations while building the team’s ability to own day-to-day execution

You may be a good fit if

  • You have 10+ years in customer success, account management, or post-sales roles at enterprise software companies

  • You have 5+ years leading CS teams, with a track record of hiring, coaching, and developing high-performing CSMs

  • You’ve owned GRR and NRR targets and can show how your team moved them

  • You’ve built or rebuilt a CS function during rapid growth, not only run an established one

  • You’ve run both high-touch and scaled or digital coverage models and know when each one fits

  • You can show how your team helped customers move from initial onboarding to sustained adoption and measurable business outcomes

  • You’re comfortable with usage and consumption data, and ideally have supported usage-based or API products

  • You have strong command of Salesforce, forecasting, and customer health tooling

  • You’re hands-on with AI products and can build enough product fluency to understand customer workflows, diagnose adoption barriers, and earn trust with business and technical stakeholders

  • You communicate clearly with executive buyers, administrators, and technical teams, including during sensitive product changes or escalations

  • You’re comfortable operating without an established playbook, using AI and automation where they improve execution and knowing where human judgment matters

title: Strategic Finance Lead - GTM
description:
We are looking for a Strategic Finance Lead to help scale Perplexity’s consumer and enterprise businesses. You will partner with Marketing and Growth leaders to identify growth opportunities, understand customer economics, and turn investment decisions into measurable business results. You will build our marketing-finance capabilities while helping shape how we acquire customers and generate enterprise pipeline.

This role starts as a hands-on individual contributor position for someone who enjoys open-ended problems and turning analysis into action. You will work closely with business leaders and cross-functional teams, with room for your scope to evolve as the company grows. We value someone who can set direction, dig into the details, and follow through.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop the customer economics and investment recommendations that guide how we acquire and retain customers, grow enterprise pipeline, and scale marketing spend. Use CAC, LTV, and payback to evaluate investment returns.

  • Partner with Marketing and Growth leaders to build and scale growth initiatives, identify constraints, and determine the resources and changes needed to produce more business.

  • Build models and analyses to guide growth investments, translate plans into resource requirements and spending forecasts, and track commitments as plans evolve.

  • Collaborate with data and business partners to strengthen measurement and attribution, connecting marketing activity to business outcomes. Help teams make investment decisions with incomplete information, making assumptions explicit and using results to refine where we invest.

  • Take ownership of emerging strategic questions across GTM, bringing clear recommendations and adapting as priorities change.

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years of experience in strategic finance, business operations, growth analytics, or a related field, with experience supporting growth-oriented decisions.

  • Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, with a deep understanding of customer economics and investment returns.

  • Ability to work directly with data and build financial models, using AI tools to accelerate analysis and improve workflows. You can validate outputs, interrogate assumptions, and explain the business logic behind your recommendations.

  • Experience making growth investment decisions across both consumer or self-serve acquisition and enterprise demand generation, with a strong understanding of customer economics and the connection between marketing activity, pipeline, and bookings.

  • A track record of independently identifying growth opportunities, building the analysis needed to act, and working with partners to implement decisions and learn from results. You move quickly, learn fast, and are willing to do the detailed work yourself.

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to build trust, challenge assumptions constructively, and work across teams.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Enterprise Trust & Governance)
description:
About the Role

The Enterprise Trust & Governance team builds the control plane that lets the world’s largest organizations deploy Perplexity broadly and with confidence. Computer and our agents work across a growing share of our customers’ environments, tools, and models. For administrators, that makes precise, enforceable control essential: who can do what, with which data, through which agents, and within what usage limits. This team makes those controls easy to manage, reliable and consistent across every product, and transparent to the people accountable for them.

This is a product and platform engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from shaping the architecture and policy models to shipping the experiences our customers’ administrators and security teams use every day. You’ll work across product and infrastructure teams to turn complex enterprise requirements into reusable primitives and intuitive controls. The scope spans identity and provisioning, fine-grained role-based access across connectors, tool actions, and models, customer-managed encryption keys, admin APIs, audit logs, and policy and usage controls. Strong governance helps enterprises move from pilots to company-wide rollouts and gives them the confidence to entrust agents with greater responsibility over time.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own enterprise identity and provisioning, including SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM, WorkOS integrations, and support for identity providers such as Okta and Microsoft Entra ID.

  • Build the permissions platform, with fine-grained roles and permissions for connectors, tool actions, models, and model effort levels, enforced consistently across products and agent workflows.

  • Design and ship secure, well-documented admin APIs for audit logs, members, groups, roles, and settings.

  • Build policy controls for model and feature availability, staged rollouts, model deprecations, usage and spend limits, alerts, and cost-center allocation.

  • Build admin-facing analytics for adoption, usage, spend, and policy enforcement, helping organizations measure value and manage their deployments.

  • Deliver audit logs and change notifications that help administrators investigate activity, track configuration changes, and support compliance.

  • Set the technical bar for authorization correctness and reliability, with fast, consistent, explainable permission checks, well-defined failure behavior, and strong tenant isolation.

  • Partner with Product, Design, Security, Sales, and Customer Success to translate complex enterprise requirements into reusable platform capabilities and intuitive admin experiences.

Qualifications

  • 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex backend systems from design through production operation.

  • Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable, multi-tenant SaaS platforms with clear security and isolation boundaries.

  • Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure such as AWS and Kubernetes.

  • Deep expertise in at least one of the following:

    • Enterprise identity and provisioning, including OAuth, OIDC, SAML, and SCIM.

    • Permissions platforms, fine-grained authorization, and policy enforcement.

    • Encryption, customer-managed keys, and key lifecycle management.

    • Enterprise admin platforms, audit infrastructure, or usage and spend analytics.

  • Experience building or integrating enterprise identity and access systems, including platforms such as WorkOS, Okta, or Microsoft Entra ID.

  • Sound technical judgment in security-sensitive systems, balancing threat models, authorization correctness, and failure behavior with usability and delivery speed.

  • A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture through adoption, setting technical direction for shared platforms, and raising engineering quality through mentorship.

If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification. We value demonstrated impact, deep ownership, and the initiative to turn ambiguity into results.

title: Global Treasury Manager, Investments & Risk
description:
About the Role

This is a foundational treasury role within the Finance team. As we continue with rapid growth, you will own the day-to-day mechanics of cash, optimal capital allocation, banking, and liquidity at a company that commits significant capital to compute and infrastructure. The role sits between Accounting and Strategic Finance with direct exposure to the VP of Strategic Finance. You should want to build the function, not inherit one.

Responsibilities

Cash and Liquidity Management

  • Own daily cash positioning across operating accounts and entities across various banking and treasury partners, and maintain the rolling cash forecasts

  • Own bank account administration across all entities and banking partners, including account openings and closures, signer updates, KYC requests, and portal access reviews.

  • Oversee payment controls, including approval workflows, segregation of duties, and review of high-value or unusual wires.

  • Manage the company’s investment portfolio, including money market funds, bank deposits, and separately managed accounts, in line with the investment policy, and oversee the external managers who run it.

  • Design and build an in-house investment and hedging program, including direct fixed income, compute price hedging, and yield rates

  • Develop management reporting covering portfolio performance, market conditions, and policy compliance for leadership and board

  • Monitor FX exposure from international entities and vendors, and support hedging analysis and execution.

  • Automate repeatable treasury work such as cash positioning, bank reconciliations, and reporting using AI and workflow tools, while keeping people accountable for every approval and movement of money.

  • Prepare FBAR filings, manage letters of credit and bank guarantees, and support audit requests related to cash and investments.

Qualifications

  • 4-7 years in corporate treasury, cash management, banking, audit, or strategic finance; high-growth technology or startup experience preferred

  • Experience with developing and managing an in-house investment program and market hedging

  • Working knowledge of cash forecasting, bank operations, payment rails, and short-duration fixed income.

  • Strong controls mindset and attention to detail: this role touches money movement, and accuracy is non-negotiable.

  • Clear written communication, sound escalation judgment, and comfort building process from scratch.

  • Nice to have: FX hedging, treasury management systems, debt or credit facilities, IPO and SOX readiness, or CTP, CFA, or CPA progress.

title: Sr. Workplace Coordinator
description:
Overview

The Workplace Experience team powers and connects the workday for all Perplexity employees across our global offices.

We are hospitality and experience-driven at the core. We are made up of People people, meaning that we love supporting each other and all of the People in our workplace. We take on the good and the bad with optimism and with a positive, kind approach to solving problems, dealing with the obstacles handed to us, and proactively creating good around us. We think about each moment through the lens of our colleagues (our customers) so that we can create thoughtful and memorable experiences no matter what task we have at hand.

Our San Francisco office of approximately 200+ seats is located in SOMA. The SF Sr. Workplace Coordinator will be a part of the global Workplace team, and will be responsible for all office operational, coordination, and administrative tasks while cultivating a beautiful, positive, and productive workplace.

 
 

What You’ll Do

  • Keep the SF office running in partnership with the Workplace Coordinator, covering day-to-day reception, operations, vendor relationships and services, employee health and safety compliance, and facility maintenance

  • Create a wonderful workplace experience for employees, visitors, recruits, customers and vendors, keeping the office tidy, clean, organized and polished throughout the day

  • Open and close the office daily (8:30am - 5:00pm), and be on site when no one else is for special projects, maintenance or moves

  • Administer SF office access and visitor management, including badge setup and removal, guest registration and building-security lists, in partnership with Physical Security and IT

  • Manage team mail and deliveries, from small packages to large and freight deliveries, by triaging, distributing and keeping it all organized

  • Manage inventory and order all office and kitchen supplies while tracking spend and working within the office budget, and help remotely with supply ordering for small neighboring offices

  • Build relationships with building management, maintenance and cleaning staff, and external parties such as contractors and suppliers, including quality control, vendor accountability and delivering feedback

  • Manage vendor and contractor paperwork and logistics, including insurance certificates, contractor access and freight elevator bookings

  • Help coordinate design and construction projects and act as the on-site contact

  • Own the SF and Palo Alto workplace ticket queue, triaging, resolving and routing requests in a kind and timely manner and keeping requesters updated through close

  • Own SF office communications and documentation, including the office guide or wiki, Slack announcements to employees and leaders, and building notices

  • Organize, monitor and communicate facility and building safety preparedness to employees

  • Produce thoughtful and inclusive office experiences and events, working with the Workplace team to stay consistent with other offices and the global strategy

  • Visit the Palo Alto office as needed to support on-site operations, supplies and employee requests

  • Help with ad-hoc projects when time allows, and contribute in ways beyond this high-level overview of the role

 
 

What You Bring

  • 5-7 years of experience working in facilities, workplace operations, office administration, or hospitality fields

  • Proficiency with G-Suite Products or the ability to learn software quickly

  • Excellent organization, planning and prioritization skills

  • Exceptionally strong ownership and can-do attitude with an operational mindset

  • Comfortable working autonomously, juggling multiple tasks under tight deadlines, switching gears at the drop of a hat, and having a “no task too small” mentality

  • Willingness to jump in where needed, picking up projects and checking things off lists even when it lands on your plate unexpectedly

  • Excellent written, non-verbal, and verbal communication skills; the ability to work well with various personality types, and are receptive to feedback...all while maintaining a high degree of professionalism and confidentiality

  • Genuine passion for supporting others and a contagiously positive attitude

  • The capability to anticipate others' needs and act with patience, kindness, and firmness

  • An eye for detail with regards to all things from process to projects to space to events

  • The ability to maintain a professional and kind game face even when things aren’t going as planned or desired; a propensity for problem solving quickly and quietly

  • A solid sense of self awareness and the desire for feedback to adapt and grow

title: Member of Data Staff (Data Acceleration)
description:
Perplexity is AI for people who expect more. This role brings that same standard to how our data team works, with AI at the center of everything we do.

We're looking for someone who's been a great data scientist, analytics engineer, or data engineer: the kind of person who knows which metric actually matters, can design an A/B test that answers the real question, has gone deep on a data model because something didn't add up, and has decided that the highest-leverage thing they can do next is build AI systems that fundamentally change how data science gets done.

You'll build AI agents and internal systems that can increasingly handle end-to-end analysis workflows: forming hypotheses, writing and running queries, interpreting results, and drafting recommendations with the right evaluation, review, and guardrails. You'll build the retrieval infrastructure and evaluation loops that let AI systems query the warehouse reliably. You'll create workflows that detect, diagnose, and help fix data issues before they become company-wide problems. You'll build the infrastructure that multiplies what a small data team can ship.

You'll join a data team that's already using AI across its work. The next step is turning those individual workflows into scalable systems, shared tools, and an AI-native operating model that becomes a benchmark for how modern data teams work.

 

What You'll Do

  • Build AI agents that do data science - not just SQL copilots, but systems that can safely explore data, form hypotheses, run queries, interpret results, and generate actionable recommendations with clear evaluation and human review loops.

  • Make AI systems query the warehouse reliably - build the retrieval infrastructure and evaluation loops that let agents use our semantic context and metadata accurately.

  • Accelerate the AI-native data workflow - turn the best existing AI-assisted workflows into repeatable systems, reusable tools, and patterns the whole data team can adopt.

  • Automate the data lifecycle - build self-healing pipelines, automated dbt model generation and validation, data quality agents, and diagnosis workflows that reduce manual firefighting.

  • Ship AI-powered experiment analysis - build agents that interpret A/B test results, flag statistical issues, identify likely drivers, and draft ship/no-ship recommendations.

  • Turn the data team into a product team - build internal data products that stakeholders use every day, replacing ad hoc requests with self-serve AI interfaces.

  • Own the full lifecycle - identify high-leverage problems, prototype with LLMs, evaluate accuracy, design the UX, ship to production, and monitor quality over time.

What We're Looking For

  • 6+ years in data science, analytics engineering, data engineering, or a related role. You've been close enough to real data work to know what should and should not be automated.

  • Deep SQL and analytics judgment - you can reason through metrics, experiments, data models, and messy warehouse reality without relying on a tool to think for you.

  • Strong product sense - you understand what stakeholders actually need, what makes a workflow adoptable, and how to turn a prototype into a product people use.

  • Hands-on LLM experience - you've built with frontier models, agents, RAG systems, evals, or AI-powered workflows and have opinions about where they work and where they fail.

  • Pipeline and modeling fluency - you've worked with dbt, warehouse schemas, data quality issues, and the practical tradeoffs behind durable data systems.

  • Builder mentality - you see a manual process and immediately think about how to systematize it. You ship fast, measure quality, and iterate.

  • Autonomy - this is a new function. You'll help define the roadmap as much as execute it.

Bonus

  • Experience building production AI agents or agent evaluation systems.

  • Experience with Snowflake, semantic layers, or metadata systems.

  • Experience building internal tools, Slack bots, CLIs, or developer productivity products that people actually used.

  • Strong experimentation background, including metric design and statistical interpretation.

  • Experience with BI tools and the judgment to know what should be automated versus kept human-reviewed.

  • Early-stage startup experience.

Why This Role

  • Set the standard for the industry - Perplexity's data team is already using AI across its work. You'll turn that into something other data teams look to as the benchmark.

  • Build AI with AI - Perplexity builds AI for people who expect more. You'll bring that same level of ambition to how the company works with data.

  • Frontier models, day one - you're at an AI company with access to frontier infrastructure and people who deeply understand what's possible.

  • Massive leverage - the systems you build will multiply the output of every data team member and every stakeholder who needs data.

  • Direct impact - small team, no layers of approval. Idea to shipped system in days, not quarters.

title: Member of Technical Staff, (Software Engineer, Experience)
description:
The charter of Perplexity’s Core Experience team is to create a cohesive, intuitive, and delightful user experience by integrating cutting-edge AI capabilities and research into a unified system. The Core Experience team works closely with product design teams to ship a world-class web app that’s used by millions of people every day. We imagine and build the interfaces through which people experience the promise of AI.

We are seeking a talented engineer with an uncompromising dedication to the craft of frontend web development. You’ll help us to define the future of human-agent collaboration: establishing intuitive mental-models, patterns, and state-representation. You’ll work closely with design to prototype, architect, and engineer novel interfaces for interacting with AI collaborators.

What you’ll do

  • Build and ship polished, high-craft, intuitive web interfaces

  • Constantly improve high-visibility surfaces like agent chat threads, artifact editing, and message composition

  • Partner directly with design to turn visionary ideas into production implementations

  • Solve complex problems across architecture, state-management, animation, and performance-optimization

  • Collaborate with capabilities and research teams to synthesize the latest research into coherent production experiences

  • Support other product teams by designing reusable libraries and SDKs to maintain a high quality-bar across all surfaces of the product

What we’re looking for

  • Strong proficiency in modern web technologies: React, TypeScript, CSS, etc.

  • Exceptional taste: relentless attention to detail, from aesthetics to performance to code-quality

  • Comfortable owning projects end-to-end, working at high velocity in an ambiguous environment where the industry changes by the day

  • Keen product sensibilities: being able to reason about what will work, what won’t, and articulate why

  • Customer obsession: always thinking about how what you’re building will touch the person on the other side of the screen

title: Member of Technical Staff (AI Software Engineer, Agent Engine)
description:
Perplexity is seeking energetic engineers to join our highly driven Agent Engine team. The Agent Engine team designs and builds powerful agentic experiences including Perplexity Computer, the Comet ecosystem, our Agent API, and more. In short, we build frontier intelligence systems for the world's most discerning users.

As an engineer on our Agent Engine team, you'll bring AI expertise, sharp product intuition, and a tinkerer's mindset to advance the frontier of what agents can accomplish for our millions of devoted users. You'll work across engineering and applied research to solve many open problems in AI, including:

  • Designing frontier agent harnesses and systems to perform high-stakes, mission-critical work for our users;

  • Leveraging action and decision models that determine, based on complex multimodal states, how to accomplish user-specified objectives;

  • Providing consistently excellent experiences across local execution, headless cloud, custom executors, and other environments through sound system design and flexible abstractions;

  • Developing permission architectures, payload classifiers, and other methods to implement secure-by-design agentic capabilities;

  • Designing optimal data representations and modes of interaction between agents and their environments;

  • and much, much more.

Qualifications

  • Strong foundational familiarity with the AI systems stack.

  • Proficiency in Python (bonus points for TypeScript, Go, and/or Rust).

  • Significant experience in at least one of the following areas:

    • Harness engineering

    • Agent Skills and plugin architectures

    • Model training and reinforcement learning

    • Browser technologies (CDP, Playwright, extension development, etc.)

  • Strong technical intuition and taste for user experience excellence.

  • Comfortable working with a small, fast-moving team; bias toward ownership.

  • A passion for shipping products that surprise and delight.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Fraud Prevention)
description:
About the role

Perplexity's fraud prevention team protects our products, users, and infrastructure from fraud and abuse across the whole lifecycle: sign-up, authentication, payments, API usage, and product features. We build and operate a real-time decisioning platform together with the surrounding systems: data pipelines for detection and model training, integrations with product and payment systems, and internal tooling for investigation and response. As a software engineer on the team, you will own services end to end, from design to production operations, and work closely with fraud analysts, ML engineers, and product teams to make abuse expensive and legitimate usage frictionless.


Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate high-throughput, low-latency backend services for fraud detection and prevention

  • Build data pipelines and real-time feature computation that power detections and ML models

  • Collect and process trust signals

  • Integrate fraud decisions into product, auth, and payment flows across Perplexity

  • Own reliability of production services: observability, alerting, safe rollouts, incident response

  • Build internal tooling for investigation, enforcement, and auditability

  • Partner with fraud analysts to turn new abuse patterns into production detections quickly

Qualifications

  • 5+ years building and operating high-throughput, latency-sensitive backend systems in production

  • Strong systems programming skills; Rust, Go, or C++ experience preferred (we write Rust)

  • Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, Terraform and cloud infrastructure

  • Solid data fundamentals: stream/batch computations, caching and storage trade-offs

  • Pragmatic, ownership-driven approach: ship incrementally, measure, and make failures degrade safely

Nice to have

  • Fraud prevention, anti-abuse, or payments-risk domain experience

  • Experience serving ML models in production

  • Client-side experience (web or mobile) for signal collection

title: Engineering Manager (Agent Engine)
description:
Perplexity is seeking an Engineering Manager to lead and grow our highly driven Agent Engine team. The Agent Engine team designs and builds powerful agentic experiences including Perplexity Computer, the Comet ecosystem, our Agent API, and more. title: Senior Commercial Counsel, Enterprise
description:
Perplexity is looking for a senior commercial attorney to join our Legal team. We are looking for an independent, business-practical yet diligent-minded professional who can carry live deals, extend the infrastructure we have already built, and hold the line on the terms that matter as deal volume, complexity, and regulatory surface all grow.

You will negotiate directly with large enterprise customers across a large variety of industries including financial services, healthcare, government, and other regulated industries, partner daily with Enterprise Sales, Partnerships, Deal Desk, Security, Privacy, Product, and Finance, and advise on the legal questions that come with agentic, retrieval, and API products deployed inside enterprise environments. This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who is genuinely a self starter.

This role is for you if you get energy from ambiguous, first‑of‑their‑kind problems and enjoy designing repeatable approaches that scale. You default to enabling the business, frame risk in practical terms, and focus on durable structures rather than one‑off fixes.

Responsibilities

  • Independently lead end-to-end drafting, review, and negotiation of Enterprise customer agreements across our suite of offerings: Enterprise Pro, Enterprise Max, Computer, and API product lines, including MSAs, order forms, SaaS and API terms, DPAs, BAAs, security exhibits, customer-paper redlines, product-specific addenda, and public-sector vehicles such as GSA MAS orders and federal RFP responses.

  • Serve as a trusted legal partner to Enterprise Sales, Partnerships, Deal Desk, and Customer Success, providing fast, practical, business-aligned counsel that accelerates deal velocity, protects the terms that matter, and scales as the Sales organization grows.

  • Extend and maintain the existing Enterprise negotiation playbook, DPA and Privacy Notice architecture, product-specific term libraries, and fallback positions as our product surface, customer mix, and regulatory environment evolve, so that positions compound into reusable precedent rather than being re-litigated deal by deal.

  • Advise on AI-specific contract terms for enterprise deployments, including bespoke data postures; negotiate output ownership and liability, agentic-feature risk allocation and translate product operations into enterprise contract commitments.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Security, Privacy, Finance, and Compliance to surface and address legal risk early, particularly on customer-data flows, enterprise integrations, model routing, and customer-specific compliance requirements.

  • Monitor the evolving regulatory landscape for enterprise AI, data protection, and public-sector procurement (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, HIPAA, DORA, EU AI Act, sector-specific frameworks) and translate emerging requirements into practical contractual positions and updated playbook guidance.

  • Represent Perplexity Legal externally on customer negotiation calls with counterparty counsel at sophisticated enterprises.

What we are looking for

  • Exceptional communicator who owns deadlines, proactively manages internal and external expectations, and escalates early and clearly to protect deal timelines and momentum.

  • A proactive problem‑solver who defaults to “yes, and” when engaging with internal stakeholders: you look for ways to make deals work, frame risk clearly, and design long‑term, scalable solutions.

  • A disciplined drafter who favors surgical, minimal‑footprint edits over wholesale rewrites, grounds positions in documented rationale, and preserves material legal meaning and risk allocation under time pressure.

  • Someone who can articulate complex legal risk and concepts in the form of simple, actionable terms for non‑legal stakeholders, leads with practical “how to make this work” advice, and designs creative, long‑term solutions to novel, cutting‑edge challenges.

  • Someone genuinely excited by novel, cutting‑edge challenges in AI products and the commercial and regulatory questions they surface, and who enjoys turning ambiguity into clear, reusable approaches.

Qualifications

  • JD and in good standing with an active U.S. state bar membership.

  • At least 7+ years of combined law firm and in-house experience, with a substantial in-house component, and a demonstrated track record of independently owning complex enterprise SaaS or API deals from the vendor side, including work with regulated-industry customers (financial services, healthcare, or government).

  • Experience advising on commercial terms and pricing structures for high‑growth SaaS/API businesses, including usage‑based and tiered pricing, pilots, and expansion frameworks.

  • Familiarity with data protection and security frameworks (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, DORA, EU AI Act) and hands-on experience negotiating DPAs.

  • Strong business acumen and the ability to partner effectively with Sales, Deal Desk, Product, Security, and executive stakeholders on live deals under time pressure.

  • Proven ability to triage and progress multiple concurrent deals under tight timelines while maintaining rigorous diligence, clear risk assessment, and high‑quality documentation.

  • Demonstrated ability to build and extend durable legal infrastructure — playbooks, templates, precedent repositories, or self-serve tools.

  • Ability to communicate clearly with business and technical audiences and to translate legal concepts into usable guidance for non-lawyers, including Sales and Deal Desk.

  • Hands-on, can-do approach to tackle projects large and small, low-ego approach to working closely with the Director and across the organization, and judgment about when to escalate and when to close.

  • Positive collaborative attitude, comfort with ambiguity and a fast pace, high level of integrity, and intellectual curiosity about AI technology.

Nice to have

  • Prior experience with public-sector contracting or with on-prem deployment structures.

  • Experience with AI-native contracting questions related to agentic products

  • Experience with contracting with regulated entities (financial institutions or health care), especially in the EU/UK.

title: Legal Response Specialist
description:
We're hiring a Legal Response Specialist on Perplexity's Support team to handle legal and other sensitive tickets. You'll help Legal answer routine requests for information and support Governance, Risk & Compliance, or GRC, on privacy and security requests.

You'll review cases, write responses, and follow up until the work is done. Support Engineering owns the routing and safeguards that keep these tickets from being missed, answered by AI, or automatically closed.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor designated Support and Legal channels, assess urgency, and route requests for human review. Promptly escalate government, court, law enforcement, and legal-threat requests according to approved procedures.

  • Respond to routine requests using Legal-approved templates and guidance. Escalate matters requiring legal interpretation or disclosure of user information.

  • Answer routine requests for information under Legal's guidance. Gather account history and draft responses for matters that need review.

  • Help GRC process data subject requests and meet deadlines. Follow approved identity-verification and data-handling procedures.

  • Coordinate security questionnaires and data protection agreements, with Legal and GRC responsible for substantive review and approval.

  • Track each case through completion, including after handoffs. Record decisions, follow up on deadlines, and confirm the work is done before closing.

  • Work with Support Engineering to test routing, AI bypass rules, auto-close protections, and alerts. Investigate missed cases and verify fixes.

  • Keep approved replies and handoff instructions current with Legal and GRC. Arrange backup coverage so cases keep moving when you're out.

  • Handle other sensitive support escalations. Report backlog, response times, overdue cases, and recurring problems to Support, Legal, and GRC.

Requirements

  • 5+ years in support, trust and safety, legal or privacy operations, or compliance, ideally at a technology company.

  • Experience handling legal, privacy, or law enforcement requests.

  • Working knowledge of GDPR, CCPA, and data subject requests.

  • Judgment about when to involve Legal or GRC, and care with confidential and privileged information.

  • Clear writing, including in sensitive customer conversations.

  • Ability to manage competing deadlines and follow through without reminders.

  • Experience improving support processes with technical teams, including automation and AI safeguards.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Intercom, Decagon, Linear, or Kodex.

  • Paralegal, privacy, or compliance experience or certification.

  • Experience with security questionnaires, SOC 2, ISO 27001, or HIPAA.

  • Familiarity with AI products or data tools for case reviews.

title: Compensation Lead
description:
We're hiring a Compensation Lead to build Perplexity's compensation function and own its day-to-day execution. You'll build the programs and processes that support how we hire, recognize, and retain people.

You should be comfortable moving between program design and an individual offer, building longer-term structure while keeping today's decisions moving. The goal is a compensation approach that is competitive, financially sound, and clear enough for people to use, without adding unnecessary complexity.

What you'll own

  • Build the compensation foundation. Assess existing practices, data, and tools; prioritize the gaps; and develop recommendations on compensation philosophy, market positioning, and cash and equity guidelines.

  • Develop salary ranges and market benchmarks. Establish a consistent approach to pricing roles across functions and locations. Partner with People and business leaders on job scope and leveling, and explain where market data is useful or incomplete.

  • Own day-to-day compensation decisions. Be the primary partner for offers, promotions, pay adjustments, and compensation questions. Evaluate recommendations against market data, internal equity, and budget, with clear approval paths for exceptions.

  • Design and run compensation reviews. Build the calendar, planning models, manager guidance, and approval process. Coordinate with Finance, People Operations, Payroll, and equity partners to carry decisions through to accurate implementation.

  • Inform leadership decisions. Model the cost and employee impact of proposed changes to salary and equity programs. Present a recommendation and its trade-offs, then own execution once approved.

  • Identify and address inconsistencies. Assess pay compression and potential inequities across teams, levels, and locations. Partner with People leadership and Legal on appropriate reviews and recommend actions.

  • Build processes people can use. Establish decision records, recruiter and manager guidance, and clear explanations of compensation programs. Improve recurring workflows so consistent decisions don't depend on individual knowledge or one-off conversations.

  • Own the data and tools behind the work. Establish reliable compensation records, select and manage benchmarking resources, and improve reporting and quality checks. Use approved automation and AI tools where they help, with appropriate protection for employee information and verification of results.

What you bring

  • Experience building compensation programs: You've established or substantially rebuilt compensation frameworks and processes with limited infrastructure, and stayed accountable for running them after launch.

  • Technical compensation depth: Hands-on experience with market pricing, salary ranges, cash and equity programs, compensation reviews, and individual pay recommendations.

  • Strong analytical judgment: You can build and audit models, reconcile imperfect data, and explain your assumptions. You know when a benchmark is a useful comparison and when it misses the role.

  • Ability to influence decisions: You can turn analysis into a clear recommendation, discuss trade-offs with leadership, and constructively challenge an approach that isn't working.

  • Independent, hands-on execution: You can set priorities, build a workable process, and manage urgent requests without losing progress on longer-term work. You're comfortable being both the person designing the program and the person checking the data.

  • Discretion and clear communication: You handle sensitive information carefully and explain compensation decisions in language that recruiters, managers, and employees can understand.

title: Member of Technical Staff (AI Policy and Strategic Initiatives)
description:
Perplexity is seeking an intrepid Member of Technical Staff to take on one of the AI industry's most unique engineering roles. You'll work directly with Perplexity's senior leadership to spearhead a broad portfolio of strategic technology initiatives across policy, law, operations, and corporate affairs.

As a Member of Technical Staff in the Policy & Strategic Initiatives group, you'll occupy a front-row seat to the foremost policy issues animating the AI ecosystem. You'll also get a panoptic view of how leading AI companies operate, make decisions, and engage with broader society.

Those seeking to marry technical expertise and broader interests in law, policy, and corporate affairs will find a home in this role. You'll make contributions to Perplexity that defy traditional boundaries, with a bench of mentors who will push you to learn and grow day after day.

What you'll do:

Your work will be both highly interdisciplinary and firmly grounded in engineering rigor. On any given day, you might:

  • Harness AI agents to research high-stakes policy and regulatory issues pertaining to Perplexity.

  • Build automated platforms for harvesting, prioritizing, and patenting Perplexity's inventions, in collaboration with our AI researchers and intellectual property attorneys.

  • Work hands-on with our Legal team and outside counsel in support of high-tech litigation matters in U.S. federal court.

  • Engineer privacy and compliance systems that efficiently scale with our growing portfolio of frontier AI products (such as Comet and Computer).

  • Contribute to regulatory filings and responses that require impeccable command of AI technology, Perplexity's own systems, and the broader policy landscape.

  • Embed with our People team to implement first-party software solutions for recruiting, labor compliance, and performance management.

  • Participate in meetings with Capitol Hill, executive branch officials, international partners, and civil society as a subject-matter expert on both AI technology and policy.

The above is a small sampling of activities; no two days will be the same, and your work will take you to all corners of our company. You'll interact each day with Perplexity's senior leaders, who will come to rely on you as a creative problem solver for simple and complex matters alike.

Who we're looking for:

No single profile defines our ideal candidate for this role. Here are some examples of people who might thrive here:

  • Exceptionally talented early-career engineers (new grads welcome) who are (1) well-read in law, tech policy, or economics, and (2) wish to grow in both technical and non-technical disciplines.

    • We welcome candidates who plan to attend law school or PhD programs in the future; we ask for a minimum 2-year commitment (i.e., you would apply for the entering class of 2028 or later).

  • Experienced engineers at top tech companies who wish to develop policy, business, and operations chops.

  • Lawyers or economists (new JD or PhD grads welcome) who've kept their engineering skills sharp and are excited to reimagine their fields in the age of AI.

  • This is a non-exhaustive list; other profiles may also be great fits.

No matter which profile describes you, we'll also be looking for:

  • Evidence of exceptional ability and 99th-percentile work ethic.

  • Strong technical skills at or above Perplexity's hiring bar for software engineers.

  • Fluency with frontier intelligence tools (such as Perplexity Computer).

  • High intrinsically-enforced standards for the craft and quality of your work.

  • Strong communication and writing skills, ideally demonstrated via samples of past written work product.

  • Curiosity and excitement about new and unfamiliar fields; eagerness to redefine your job every 3-6 months.

  • Ability to quickly dive deep in any given field and develop mastery rivaling that of domain experts.

  • Unimpeachable judgment, integrity, and discretion to be entrusted with the company's most important matters.

  • A service-oriented attitude that continually questions how company systems and processes might better serve stakeholders.

title: Procurement Lead
description:
We're hiring a Procurement Lead to build Perplexity's procurement function. You'll design how Perplexity buys, from the workflow and policies teams follow to the agreements we sign and the vendor relationships we manage after signature. You'll be a key partner to teams across the company, helping them choose the right vendors and structure strong agreements without becoming a bottleneck, and making sure every dollar we commit to third parties earns its keep.

This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who thrives in fast-paced environments and wants to build the function, not inherit one, with room for your scope to grow as the company does. We value someone who can set direction, dig into the details, and follow through. This position is based in San Francisco and requires in-person attendance 2-3 days per week.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead our highest-impact vendor deals across software, cloud services, data, and professional services, from competitive alternatives through pricing, terms, and signature

  • Structure committed-spend, usage-based, and multi-year agreements that scale with our usage and preserve our flexibility

  • Own relationships with our most important vendors, including performance tracking, business reviews, and renewal negotiations

  • Design an efficient procurement workflow, policies, and approval thresholds, and implement the tools and AI automation to run them

  • Use AI workflows and agents to automate procurement, from intake and contract review to spend analysis and reporting

  • Build visibility into vendor spend and contracts, and drive savings through consolidation, right-sizing, and renegotiation

  • Partner with Legal, Security, and Accounting on contract terms, vendor risk reviews, and audit-ready controls

What You'll Bring

  • 5-7+ years of experience in procurement or strategic sourcing at a high-growth technology company, including building or scaling the function.

  • A track record of personally negotiating multi-million dollar software, cloud, or data agreements, managing those vendors and renegotiating at renewal, and delivering measurable savings

  • Experience building procurement processes, policies, and systems from scratch

  • Ability to run multiple deals at once with incomplete information, and sound judgment about when to move fast and when to escalate

  • Comfort using AI tools to accelerate your work and improve workflows

  • A low-ego, roll-up-your-sleeves approach to projects large and small and to working across the organization

  • Strong communication skills, the ability to influence senior leaders, and a reputation for being commercially tough and fair

title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure)
description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast.

Responsibilities

  • Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost.

  • Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load.

  • Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers.

  • Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested.

  • Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back.

  • Prepare for failures. Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works.

  • Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice.

  • Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure.

  • Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team.

Qualifications

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

  • Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them.

  • Production Kubernetes at scale: cluster upgrades, CNI, CoreDNS, autoscalers like Karpenter, and debugging a misbehaving node at 3 a.m. Writing Helm charts alone doesn't count.

  • Terraform mastery. You've designed module structures, managed state across many accounts, and run large refactors and imports without taking production down.

  • Strong networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, load balancing, routing).

  • You write real code in Python, Go, or Rust for automation, tooling, and controllers, and you'd rather automate a runbook than follow it.

  • Fluency with observability tools like Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and the judgment to turn metrics, logs, and traces into SLOs and alerts that matter.

  • A track record of leading production incidents and turning root-cause analysis into durable fixes.

  • You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.

Additional experience we value

  • Multi-region active-active or failover architectures, and disaster-recovery programs with real recovery targets.

  • Proxies, service meshes, and kernel-level networking: Envoy, Istio, Cilium, or eBPF.

  • GitOps and progressive delivery: Argo CD, Flux, or similar.

  • Enterprise and compliance environments: single-tenant or BYOC deployments, KMS/BYOK, SOC 2 or similar controls.

  • Running stateful systems in production: Postgres, Redis, or search engines like Vespa or Elasticsearch.

  • Multi-cloud or neocloud operations (GCP, CoreWeave, or similar).

  • FinOps: cost attribution, Savings Plans and reservations, and making infrastructure cheaper without making it fragile.

title: Sales Enablement Operations Manager
description:
Perplexity's sales organization is growing fast, and our sellers need the right content, tools and AI workflows to win. As our first Sales Enablement Operations Manager, you'll be the strategic partner and builder behind how Perplexity's sales team finds, uses and learns from content.

This role is both strategic and hands-on. You'll work with the Sales Enablement Lead to define our content management strategy, including whether to build on Perplexity's own AI platform or buy a dedicated tool. Then you'll build it, run it and keep improving it. You'll also build AI skills, plugins and workflows that make reps and managers faster and more effective every day.

This is a foundational hire. We're looking for someone who can grow into a leadership role as the enablement function scales.

Responsibilities

Help shape content and knowledge strategy

  • Partner with the Sales Enablement Lead to define the long-term content management strategy for the sales team, from requirements to the build-vs-buy decision.

  • Work alongside the Sales Enablement Lead on the evaluation: gather stakeholder needs, assess options (including Perplexity Computer and third-party platforms), model costs and tradeoffs, and shape a joint recommendation to sales leadership.

  • Design the content architecture: taxonomy, ownership, governance, approval workflows and lifecycle (create, review, update, retire).

Help build and run the enablement stack

  • Own the implementation and maintenance of the sales content hub, call library and training platform, leveraging Perplexity throughout.

  • Help coordinate with Revenue Operations, Product Marketing, Product and Legal so content is accurate, approved and available where sellers work (Salesforce, Slack, call-recording tools).

  • Own enablement reporting: content usage, training completion, certification status and how they relate to ramp and performance.

Build AI tools for the sales team

  • Design, build and maintain AI skills, plugins and agent workflows for account executives, BDRs and sales managers, such as account research, call prep, deal reviews, coaching and pipeline hygiene.

  • Turn repeated seller and manager tasks into reusable AI workflows, then drive adoption through training, documentation and feedback loops.

  • Develop training materials for sellers and managers on using AI tools well, and keep a shared library of best practices.

Lead and scale

  • Set the standards for how enablement content and AI tools get built, contributed and maintained across the GTM organization.

  • Act as a trusted thought partner to enablement leadership on priorities, operating model and tooling.

  • Help shape the enablement operations function as the team grows, with a path to leading it.

What we're looking for

  • 4–6 years in go-to-market roles, with at least 2 years owning sales enablement operations, revenue operations, GTM systems or sales content strategy.

  • Experience owning a sales content or knowledge system end to end, including taxonomy, governance, adoption and measurement.

  • A track record of leading or heavily shaping a tooling decision, such as a platform evaluation, migration or in-house build.

  • Real, hands-on AI fluency: you've built AI tools or workflows (custom GPTs, Claude or Perplexity skills, MCP connectors, n8n, Zapier, Clay or similar) that other people use regularly, and you can show examples.

  • Systems thinking: you understand how content, CRM, call-recording and communication tools connect, and you design for how sellers actually work.

  • Strong judgment and the ability to make a clear recommendation and defend it with leadership.

  • Experience driving cross-functional projects without formal authority.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, and a bias toward shipping, measuring and iterating.

Nice to have

  • Experience as the first enablement operations or GTM systems hire, building the function from scratch.

  • Hands-on experience with enablement platforms such as Highspot, Seismic, Guru, Mindtickle or Showpad.

  • Background as an AE, SE or BDR before moving into enablement or operations.

  • Experience managing or mentoring contractors, interns or direct reports.

  • Experience at a high-growth AI or SaaS company.

What success looks like

  • First 90 days: You've assessed current content and tools, interviewed sellers and managers, made a build-vs-buy recommendation with the Sales Enablement Lead, and shipped the first AI skills the sales team uses every week.

  • First 6 months: A governed content hub and call library are live and adopted, enablement reporting is in place, and a growing library of AI tools is measurably saving time for reps and managers.

  • First year: Enablement operations is a scalable function with clear standards, and you're ready to lead it as the team grows.

title: Sales Onboarding Manager
description:
Perplexity is hiring sellers fast, and every new seller has to learn a fast-moving product line: Enterprise, Comet, Computer and the API. We're looking for a Sales Onboarding Manager to own how new sellers go from their first day to selling on their own. You'll build the program, keep it current, run it, and certify that each seller is ready before they sell independently.

This is a high-ownership, highly visible role on a small Sales Enablement team. You'll partner with the Sales Enablement Lead and work closely with sales leaders, frontline managers, Product, Product Marketing, Solutions and Revenue Operations. Your goal is a robust, relevant, progressive and measurable ramp that gets faster as we scale.

About the role

The Sales Onboarding Manager owns the onboarding experience for Enterprise and Commercial Account Executives (AEs) and Business Development Representatives (BDRs), from Day 1 through field certification. You'll design the curriculum, keep it up to date as the product changes, lead the sessions yourself, manage the logistics of placing each cohort into the right sessions, and run the certifications that decide when a new hire is ready.

Company-wide new-hire orientation is owned by a separate onboarding role. Ongoing training for ramped sellers is owned by Sales Enablement. You'll partner with both so new sellers move smoothly from orientation into their sales ramp and then into working independently with ongoing training from Enablement.

Responsibilities

  • Own the sales onboarding program. Co-design and run role-based ramps for BDRs and for Enterprise and Commercial AEs, including learning objectives, milestones and time-to-productivity targets for each stage. Where BDRs and AEs need the same foundations, they learn them together. Where the jobs differ, each gets its own track.

  • Build the BDR ramp. Teach new BDRs prospecting and outbound: ideal customer profile and persona research, account and territory rules, multi-channel sequences, cold calling, cold email, qualification, and clean handoffs to AEs. Get BDRs productive in the prospecting stack, including Salesforce, Apollo and the dialer.

  • Build and maintain content. Create and update modules, playbooks, talk tracks, demo guides, knowledge checks and self-paced content. Update materials as products, pricing, positioning and process change, and retire anything out of date.

  • Facilitate live sessions. Lead engaging, interactive sessions (virtual and in person) on Perplexity's products, sales process, customer personas, discovery, demos, objection handling and tools. Bring in subject-matter experts from Product, Product Marketing, Solutions and top sellers.

  • Run cohort logistics. Work with Recruiting and sales leaders to track incoming hires, assign each one to the right sessions for their role, segment and start date, and manage calendars, attendance, make-ups and pre-work.

  • Certify field readiness. Design and run role-specific certifications using clear rubrics. For BDRs, that means cold-call, email and qualification certifications. For AEs, it means pitch, discovery and demo certifications. Both roles also certify on tools. Calibrate scoring with BDR and sales managers, give actionable feedback, and decide when a new hire is ready to sell on their own.

  • Partner with frontline managers. Give managers visibility into each new hire's progress, flag risks early, and equip managers to reinforce onboarding through coaching and call reviews.

  • Measure and improve. Track completion, certification pass rates and ramp attainment. For BDRs, also track activity, meetings booked and accepted, and pipeline sourced. For AEs, also track time to first meeting, pipeline and closed business. Use the data and new-hire feedback to improve the program each cohort.

  • Scale with leverage. Use AI tools, including Perplexity's own products, to build content faster, personalize learning paths and automate repetitive logistics so the program keeps up with hiring.

What we're looking for

The best candidates are strong facilitators who also design programs and run operations well. You can command a room, build a curriculum from a blank page, and keep a complicated cohort calendar running smoothly. You hold a high bar for readiness and know how to tell a manager when a seller isn't there yet.

Must-haves

  • 2–4 years in sales enablement, sales onboarding or sales training, ideally at a high-growth B2B SaaS or AI company. Experience carrying a quota or managing sellers is a strong plus.

  • A track record of designing and running a sales onboarding or ramp program end to end, with measurable impact on ramp time or productivity.

  • Excellent live facilitation, virtual and in person, with sellers at different experience levels, from early-career BDRs to seasoned AEs.

  • Experience designing and running certifications or skills assessments (such as cold-call, pitch, discovery or demo) using rubrics that sales managers trust.

  • Strong program management and operational rigor. You can run several overlapping cohorts, schedules and stakeholders without dropping details.

  • Working knowledge of modern sales methods (such as MEDDICC, Command of the Message or similar), outbound prospecting and the full sales cycle from first touch to close.

  • Comfort learning technical products quickly and explaining them clearly. You can learn an AI product well enough to teach and demo it.

  • Fluency with the sales tech stack, such as Salesforce, a conversation-intelligence tool and an LMS or content-management platform.

  • High ownership and comfort with ambiguity in a fast-moving environment where the product changes weekly.

Nice to have

  • Experience onboarding sellers for AI, developer or other technically complex products.

  • Background in instructional design or adult learning.

  • Previous experience as a BDR/SDR or as a BDR/SDR manager.

  • Experience building onboarding for both Enterprise and Commercial/velocity sales motions, or for Customer Success roles.

  • Experience standing up enablement tooling (LMS, content hub, call library) or reporting on ramp metrics.

  • Experience using AI to build content or automate enablement operations

description:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

As a member of Ramp's Risk Strategy & Operations team, you will leverage data to develop and optimize credit strategies.

Credit is one of Ramp's most consequential products. Every policy change affects how customers can grow their usage, and how responsibly Ramp scales up while managing risk. Credit Risk Strategy owns these tradeoffs end to end.

In this role, you will own or help build strategy across credit risk areas like credit limits, payment speed, and collections. You'll take ambiguous problems, get to the data, prototype the solution, and push the change with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Risk Operations, Finance, Customer Experience, and Compliance.

AI fluency is required. We use AI as a core pillar of our risk management stack, and you will be prototyping and managing related Agents and tools. You should already be using tools like Claude Code, Codex, or similar AI tools to write code, explore data, prototype apps, automate workflows, and check your own work. You do not need to be a software engineer, but you do need to use AI to ship something runnable or inspectable enough to test, improve, and hand off.

We are looking for builders with high agency and high urgency: people who prototype the workflow, not just write the recommendation for someone else to build.

What You'll Do

  • Own credit risk strategy for areas like model prototyping, credit limits, payment speed, collections, etc.

  • Use SQL, quantitative reasoning, and credit risk judgment to investigate patterns, size opportunities, define policy changes, and pressure-test recommendations.

  • Build the first useful version when the workflow does not exist: a tool, app, dashboard, agent, notebook, QA loop, monitor, or decisioning process.

  • Use AI tools every day to move faster on research, analysis, coding, synthesis, writing, verification, and follow-through.

  • Build AI into credit risk workflows: feature exploration, policy monitoring, case review, exception handling, decision support, documentation, and human-in-the-loop QA.

  • Investigate new data sources and model features; evaluate signal quality, coverage, failure modes, and how they would change credit decisions.

  • Make ambiguous credit risk decisions within your surface area, balancing loss, customer experience, operational burden, growth, compliance, and risk-adjusted returns.

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Design, to execute and build the risk management infrastructure

What You Need

  • Minimum 2 years of experience in credit risk management or quantitative strategy role

  • Minimum 2 years of experience using SQL or Python for data retrieval and manipulations

  • AI fluency you can demonstrate live: name the tools, show an artifact, explain a recent failure mode, and walk through how you verified the output before using it in a credit risk decision.

  • Ownership in ambiguity: you define the question, get the data, make the call, communicate the tradeoffs, and drive follow-through without waiting for perfectly scoped work.

  • Strong communication: you can compress a complex credit risk decision into a clear narrative that leadership and cross-functional partners can act on.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Previous experience building credit risk in similar Card or expense management products

  • Previous experience in high-growth startups or environments where the operating model changed quickly.

  • Previous experience with Operations teams

Compensation

We are open to hiring at multiple levels for this role (Analyst, Associate, or Senior Associate). Level is determined during the interview process.

The expected base salary ranges are:

  • Analyst: $108,000 to $148,000

  • Associate: $140,000 to $192,000

  • Senior Associate: $160,000 to $200,000

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

About the Role

As a Product Designer at Ramp, you are accountable for outcomes, not just artifacts. You work with PMs, engineers, and other designers to define the right problems, explore and validate solutions, and ship product experiences that change customer behavior.

Design at Ramp is AI first and builder led. Work starts in an LLM, moves into tools like Claude and Cursor to explore flows and interactions, and then comes into Figma for systems and polish. Designers prototype early, test with real customers, and stay involved through launch and iteration.

We are looking for multiple product designers who are excited to work this way and who want to use AI as a core part of how they design.

What You’ll Do

  • Own product work end to end: Partner with PM and engineering to define problems, explore solution spaces, validate concepts, and ship product improvements that move key metrics. Stay involved through launch and iteration, not just handoff.

  • Start in an LLM: Use tools like Claude to clarify intent, draft short PRDs, and surface risks, edge cases, and initial approaches. Use this work to align quickly with your team.

  • Validate assumptions with self-serve research: Talk directly with customers, run quick tests, and use what you learn to adjust direction. Treat research as a velocity tool, not a gate.

  • Prototype using AI tools: Use Cursor and Claude Code to build and iterate on flows and simple interfaces. Let AI generate code while you guide structure, behavior, and UX quality. Partner with engineers to decide what moves into the product.

  • Bring work into Figma: Translate validated concepts into Figma for full state coverage, system alignment, and production readiness.

  • Design for the 80 / 20: Encode judgment and complexity under the hood while keeping the default experience simple and successful for most customers.

  • Contribute to patterns and culture: Share prompts, patterns, and learnings with the design org. Participate in crits and reviews that raise the bar for quality.

What You Need

  • Experience as a product designer working on complex products, ideally in B2B, fintech, or other systems-heavy environments

  • Ownership of projects from problem definition through launch and iteration

  • Active use of LLMs such as Claude or ChatGPT in your design workflow

  • Comfort working in tools like Cursor or Claude Code, even if you are not writing production code by hand

  • A portfolio that shows strong product thinking, interaction design, and craft

  • Ability to work with PMs to define success metrics and adjust based on results

  • Clear communication and comfort collaborating directly with engineers and PMs

  • Based in or open to relocate to NYC

Nice to Haves

  • Experience planning and running customer interviews or usability tests

  • Familiarity with design systems and extending shared components

  • Comfort with basic front-end concepts such as components and states
