About the role

Lifecycle Growth's job is to get more people using Grok, Grok Bot, X, Cursor and the API every day, and to turn that use into revenue. We own everything after signup: getting people to value, converting them to paid, growing their teams and keeping them coming back. We do it with lifecycle marketing, in-product messaging and a steady stream of experiments, and much of the work runs on agents we build ourselves.

This isn't a traditional marketing role. You'll do the work of a product manager, a product marketer and a marketing engineer, often in the same day. You'll own lifecycle growth for one or more of our products. You'll figure out where the biggest opportunity is, design the program, build it and show whether it actually moved the number.

The job spans consumer and business, self-serve and sales-led, so you'll need to think as clearly about a solo user's first week as about a team's path to an enterprise deal. You'll go deep on the systems underneath, like who's eligible, what triggers a message, how events and attributes are modeled, and how data moves from the warehouse into our messaging tools. When the best fix lives in the product or the data, you'll make the case and either build it yourself or work with engineering to ship it.

This is an in-person role based in our San Francisco office.

What you’ll do

  • Strategy and roadmap: Own lifecycle end to end across our suite of products: Grok, Grok Bot, X, Cursor and the API, from activation and conversion to paid through team expansion, retention and winback.

  • Data and audiences: Use SQL and product data to size opportunities, build the audiences and triggers behind each program, and prove what actually drove revenue.

  • Journeys: Architect multi-step, cross-channel programs across email, push and in-app, with event-based triggers, branching and suppression logic, and personalization drawn from product usage, plan and billing state, and company and role enrichment.

  • Systems: Drive and continuously improve the data model lifecycle runs on, including identity, events, attributes and eligibility, and partner with engineering on the warehouse syncs, APIs and webhooks that keep it accurate in real time.

  • Measurement: Run every program as an experiment with a proper holdout, measure incremental lift, and make judgment calls when a result is inconclusive.

  • Portfolio: Manage lifecycle as a portfolio of programs, putting more behind what works and retiring what doesn't.

  • In-product: Own in-product messaging and experiments, from onboarding and upgrade prompts to post-purchase plan tours, and partner with product and engineering to improve our in-app comms systems.

  • Tooling: Use code and agents to build the internal tools, templates and automated QA the team runs on, so each new program ships faster than the last.

You may be a fit if

  • 8+ years in Lifecycle, Growth PMM or Product Growth at a high-growth product company.

  • The range to think fluently about lifecycle for consumers and businesses, self-serve and sales-led, and to know how each one changes the right move.

  • Real technical depth. You write SQL, you know how events, identity and attributes fit together, and you're comfortable with APIs, webhooks and warehouse syncs. Coding is a plus.

  • Hands-on experience running complex programs in a major lifecycle platform, such as Braze, Customer.io or Iterable.

  • A history of building lifecycle systems with engineering, not just running campaigns on top of them.

  • Programs you can point to that moved revenue, paid users or retention, with holdouts to back it up.

  • Good experimentation judgment, focused on incrementality, cohort quality and lifetime value rather than opens and clicks.

  • Experience shipping in-product messaging or experiments alongside product and engineering.

  • The ability to set direction, bring product, engineering, data and design with you, and explain your thinking clearly to leadership.

  • A habit of using AI agents and code to get more done than a team your size should.

This role requires being in-office in San Francisco.

Our customers vary in type and size, and our goal is to unlock exceptional value for everyone. You bring an analytical mindset and an orientation toward rapid experimentation. The teams you will support are technical and experienced. They need a strategy and operations partner who brings insight and rigor that helps them make the right big bets and move with pace in bringing them to life.

You’ll be a thought partner to senior leadership and a hands-on operator who builds the models, insights and systems that help our teams stay agile and deliver on our goals. This isn’t a pure strategy role or a pure analyst role: you’ll set direction with leadership in one meeting and build the model behind it in the next.

What you’ll do

  • Design segmentation and coverage models so each customer gets the service model that drives growth

  • Build headcount and capacity models so we invest in the right places at the right time

  • Guide and define the metrics that matter for the CS org, and the compensation models that reward the right outcomes

  • Track business performance, find what’s driving the trends, and turn it into specific actions and strategies with owners

  • Build the leadership operating cadence (business reviews, planning, decision forums) so decisions get made quickly with good data

  • Build repeatable metrics, dashboards and applications that put the right KPIs in front of the right people to drive decisions and actions, from frontline teams to leadership

  • Analyze product usage to find the patterns that predict activation, expansion, retention and churn

  • Help design and run rapid experiments with clear hypotheses and control groups, then scale what works and retire what doesn’t

  • Help build the scaled engagement model as a system: how data, tooling, digital touchpoints and human coverage fit together

You may be a fit if

  • You have experience in revenue strategy & operations, customer strategy & operations or business operations

  • You have experience supporting digital, scaled, self-serve customer strategy, and/or technical services teams

  • You have strong analytical and modeling skills, and you ground your recommendations in data

  • You have worked with product usage data and built/run experimentation frameworks to evaluate causation and efficacy

  • You think holistically and systematically: how multiple touchpoints may influence the journey, and how to build solutions that will scale

  • You solve problems end to end and run programs that keep people informed and moving

  • Data science or analytics background

  • Customer-facing experience

We’re hiring Solutions Architects to help strategic customers make AI-native work real in production on the Grok platform, using Grok Bot for knowledge work and business workflows and Grok Build (Cursor) for AI-native software development. This role will be based in Sydney.

This is a hands-on technical role within the Customer Success organization, where you’ll partner with AI Deployment Managers (ADMs) to own the technical track across architecture, workflow redesign, and enterprise security while helping organizations rethink how they operate and how they build software with AI.

You’ll help customers move from excitement to workflows teams rely on every day by discovering real job friction, integrating Grok Build into codebases, CI pipelines, and code review, and designing scoped Grok Bot workflows with human-in-the-loop judgment.

The best Solutions Architects pair technical credibility with product instincts and extreme ownership, and they are as comfortable debugging a CI workflow or leading an architecture review as helping executives, from CTOs to the CRO, CMO, CFO, and COO, understand where AI changes how the business runs and how software is built.

What You’ll Do

Help Engineering Teams Adopt AI-Native Development with Grok Build (Cursor)

  • Roll out Grok Build across strategic engineering organizations and integrate it into real codebases and production workflows rather than isolated demos.

  • Configure developer environments, repository rules, and conventions, and run hands-on enablement that drives fast, durable adoption.

  • Bring agentic SDLC practices into the customer’s delivery process, from planning and implementation through testing, CI, and code review, and clear developer workflow friction along the way.

  • Keep a strong hands-on Build baseline by shipping runnable, convention-driven work in Grok Build yourself.

Engage Customers on the Grok Bot Journey

  • Use Grok Bot to turn a business user’s problem into an accepted user story and requirements that flow into Jira and through the agentic SDLC in Grok Build.

  • Lead discovery for knowledge-work and business-process use cases and redesign high-value workflows around AI agents, enterprise tools, data, and human judgment.

  • Establish a data governance and security framework that lets leadership adopt the Grok platform top down across the enterprise.

  • Help engineering organizations move from isolated usage to company-wide adoption by turning successful deployments into reusable patterns and rollouts for new teams and platform groups.

  • Partner with ADMs and Account Executives to find and drive major expansion opportunities for the Grok platform.

Become a Trusted Technical Partner

  • Build multi-threaded relationships with developers, platform teams, engineering and business leaders, and executive sponsors, and turn skeptics into champions.

  • Lead architecture reviews and working sessions, and advise on what to build, developer productivity, workflow design, governance, and adoption strategy.

  • Prototype alongside customers by connecting systems, designing agents and workflows, and debugging failures until ambiguous ideas become working systems.

  • Reason about trust boundaries with CISOs and platform owners, covering identity, permissions, data access, connectors and MCPs, execution environments, network controls, auditability, and human approval, and know when to escalate to specialists.

  • Partner with ADMs from meeting prep through active participation, and coordinate with Sales, Product, and Engineering to unblock customers.

Drive Real Customer Outcomes

  • Translate adoption into measurable impact, from faster iteration, developer productivity, and engineering quality to workflow efficiency, and help customers communicate that value internally.

  • Help teams standardize on the Grok platform and embed it deeply in core workflows, and lead recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction.

  • Shape new capabilities alongside lighthouse customers whose deployments set the standard for the market.

  • You bring a working grasp of security and compliance, or a clear path to one, and can walk customers through scenario-based guardrails.

  • You bring a passion for developer tooling and for how AI will reshape software engineering and knowledge work.

About the role

As the Head of Finance, you will build and lead Braintrust’s finance function from the ground up. You’ll sit at the center of our most critical decisions, owning planning, stress-testing bets, and partnering directly with our leadership team to allocate capital against our biggest opportunities.

You’ll play a critical role in how Braintrust scales. In the early stages, this is a hands-on role where you will build financial models, manage forecasting, and establish operational discipline. Over time, you will define our strategic finance function, build repeatable processes, and scale a high-performing team.

You’ll partner closely with GTM, Marketing, Engineering, and Operations to ensure decisions are grounded in sound economic principles and long-term value creation, while feeding insights back into how we improve our business model.

  • Strategic Planning & Forecasting: Manage forecasting, financial planning, and capital allocation. Own our quarterly and annual planning cycle end-to-end, guiding overall company strategy and resource allocation.

  • Financial Discipline & Budgeting: Ensure financial discipline and set budgets across the organization. Establish and uphold rigorous financial principles, ensuring teams make decisions grounded in strong unit economics.

  • Performance Monitoring: Monitor KPIs and performance across teams and the overall company. Build dashboards and identify the right levers to accelerate growth and efficiency.

  • Headcount & Hiring Strategy: Collaborate closely with the recruiting team and managers on headcount planning, hiring prioritization, and organizational scaling.

  • Treasury & Cash Management: Manage treasury strategy, monitor cash flow, and optimize our capital structure to support hyper-growth.

  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Operate cross-functionally by design, partnering deeply with Sales, Marketing, and Engineering, to ensure aligned priorities and data-driven decision-making.

  • Leadership: Proven track record of building or leading a finance function, with the ability to operate both strategically and hands-on in an early-stage or scaling environment.

  • Analytical Rigor: Deep expertise in financial modeling, long-range planning, and capital allocation. You can build from scratch, stress-test assumptions, and translate complex data into clear strategic insight.

title: Founding Data Engineer
description:
About the company

Braintrust is the agent observability platform. By actively applying intelligence to agent traces and automatically surfacing the most critical patterns, Braintrust gives teams the visibility to understand how agents behave in production and the tools to improve them.

Teams at Notion, Stripe, Box, OpenAI, and Cloudflare use Braintrust to trace their agents, find the issues in their observability data, and run evals that tell them how to improve.

About the Role

Braintrust is growing quickly across enterprise and self-serve customers, and our internal systems need to scale with us. You will establish our data foundation, make architectural decisions, work directly with our executive team, and help shape the data function as it grows. This is a founding, hands on role. You will decide what good looks like, and be able to build it.

The core of the job is analytics engineering. That means defining the business entities and metrics the company runs on, modeling them so they can be trusted, and making them accessible without a data person in the loop. Around that core, you will own the ingestion pipelines that feed it, the architecture decisions that hold it together, and the reliability of the whole path.

You'll partner with stakeholders across the business, and directly with executives. You will work with Product and Engineering on usage data and event schemas, with Finance on revenue and consumption reporting, and with Sales, RevOps, and Marketing on the pipeline and customer data they operate from.


What You Will Do

  • Define the business entities, metrics, and semantics that Product, Finance, and GTM all build on

  • Design and build the core data models in SQL and dbt

  • Build and own ingestion from product events, CRM, and other business systems, including vendor APIs, webhooks, and sync gaps

  • Make architectural decisions by determining how storage, orchestration, and transformation evolve from here

  • Stand up self-serve analytics that includes building semantic models and trusted metrics that stakeholders can query without filing a ticket

  • Partner with Engineering and Product on usage data and event schemas as the product surface grows

  • Treat governance and reliability as part of the data model

  • Use AI to accelerate your own build, and keep the foundation clean and well-described enough that AI tooling on top of it has something reliable to stand on.

Where You’ll Work in the Stack:

  • Ingestion: Product events, CRM, and other business data sources

  • Modeling: SQL, dbt, business entities, and shared metric definitions

  • Storage and orchestration: The current environment includes Snowflake; you’ll help determine how the architecture evolves

  • Analytics: Semantic models and self-serve access to trusted metrics

  • Governance and reliability: Data quality, access controls, lineage, monitoring, and debugging

About You

  • You've defined business entities and metrics, and built the models behind them

  • Strong command of SQL and dbt, and experience with a cloud warehouse (Snowflake or equivalent) and an orchestrator (Dagster, Airflow, or similar)

  • Enough engineering depth to own pipelines end to end. You can write and maintain production code, not only transformation models.

  • Clear judgment about data modeling, schema evolution, contracts, and lineage

  • Strong debugging instincts across a multi-system path, and the patience to trace a wrong number to its source

  • Ability to work directly with executives and functional leaders: clarifying vague requests, explaining how the data works, and negotiating priorities and tradeoffs

  • Comfort operating as the only data hire, balancing foundational architecture against urgent business needs

Bonus Points

  • You've built a data foundation from scratch, rather than inheriting a mature one

  • Startup experience, especially as an early or first data hire

  • Experience across multiple business functions that includes Product, Finance, and GTM

  • Familiarity with usage-based pricing, consumption models, or PLG-plus-sales-assisted funnels

  • Experience with our stack, or close equivalents: Snowflake, dbt, Dagster, AWS Batch/Lambda, Fivetran, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Soda, or semantic-layer tools like Omni or Looker

  • You've built or used agents for internal workflows and analysis

  • Braintrust user :)

What Success Looks Like

  • Braintrust has a governed set of core entities and metrics that Product, Finance, and GTM all build on

  • Product usage data is reliable enough that people act on it without checking it against something else first

  • Stakeholders can answer their own questions through trusted, self-serve models

  • Every automated decision and every metric has a traceable path back to its source

  • The foundation is documented and maintainable. Simple enough for a startup team to run solo, structured enough to hand to a larger data team as it grows.

  • Flexible time off

description:
About the company

Teams at Notion, Stripe, Box, OpenAI, and Cloudflare use Braintrust to trace their agents, find the issues in their observability data, and run evals that tell them how to improve.

About the role

Our largest customers don't just use Braintrust — they run it. They deploy our stack inside their own AWS, Azure, and GCP accounts, behind their own VPCs, under their own compliance requirements, at their own scale. When a hybrid deployment stalls, when ingest backs up, when a query that was fast last week isn't, they come to us. Platform Support is the team that owns that. We're the technical front line for infrastructure, performance, and reliability.

We're hiring Platform Support Engineers at both mid and senior levels to join a small, high-ownership team. You'll work shoulder to shoulder with our Cloud Infrastructure and Engineering teams, and alongside our Developer Support Engineers, who own the SDK and API side of the customer experience. If you like hard infrastructure problems, and you like them more when a real customer is on the other end, this is the role.

What you'll do

  • Own customer-facing support for hybrid and self-hosted Braintrust deployments across AWS, Azure, and GCP — from first install through steady-state operation.

  • Debug real infrastructure problems: Kubernetes workloads, Terraform state, networking and VPC configuration, IAM and permissions, TLS, and cloud-provider quirks.

  • Diagnose performance and reliability issues in the backend — ingest throughput, query latency, database and object-store behavior — using logs, metrics, and traces to get to cause rather than symptom.

  • Lead incident response for customer-impacting issues: triage, communicate clearly while it's still on fire, and drive it to resolution.

  • Ship fixes. Submit PRs to our backend services, Terraform modules, and deployment tooling rather than handing every problem to Engineering.

  • Build the tooling that makes the next one easier — diagnostics, health checks, preflight validation, and self-service paths that let customers unblock themselves.

  • Write and maintain the runbooks and deployment documentation that turn one hard-won answer into a permanent one.

  • Feed patterns back to Engineering and Product, so the recurring failure modes stop recurring.

  • Participate in an on-call rotation for critical customer issues.

What we're looking for

  • Experience in a customer-facing technical role — Support Engineering, SRE, DevOps, Solutions Architecture, or Infrastructure Engineering — or backend/infra engineering experience with real appetite for customer work.

  • Strong Kubernetes fundamentals: you can deploy, debug, and scale actual workloads, and read a failing pod's story from its events and logs.

  • Hands-on Terraform, and depth in at least one major cloud (AWS strongly preferred).

  • Comfort in a backend codebase — Python, TypeScript, or Go — enough to reproduce a bug, trace it to its source, and fix it.

  • Fluency with observability tooling, and the instinct to reach for data before opinion.

  • Clear, calm, direct communication under pressure, especially when the customer is technical, blocked, and losing time.

  • Ownership. You take a problem personally and follow it until the customer is running again.

Bonus points for

  • Supporting self-hosted or on-prem enterprise software, especially in regulated environments.

  • Multi-cloud experience, particularly Azure or GCP alongside AWS.

  • Database and data-infrastructure depth — Postgres, ClickHouse, or similar analytical stores.

  • Experience with observability, ML infrastructure, or developer platforms.

  • Familiarity with LLM APIs and how teams are building and evaluating agents in production.

  • Having built support or diagnostic tooling that measurably reduced ticket volume.

Why join Braintrust

  • Work on genuinely hard infrastructure problems, at the scale and pace of the teams building the best AI products in the world.

  • Join a team early enough to shape how it operates — its standards, its tooling, and its bar.

  • Sit close to both the customer and the code, with the mandate to fix things in either direction.

Benefits include

  • Daily lunch, snacks, and beverages

  • Flexible time off

  • Competitive salary and equity

  • Wifi & cellphone stipend

Equal opportunity

description:
About the company

About the role

We’re looking for a Software Engineer, Billing to build the systems that make Braintrust’s pricing, usage, and payments accurate, scalable, and transparent.

Braintrust helps teams observe, evaluate, and improve production AI agents. Our customers generate large volumes of traces, run automated and human evaluations, use AI-powered product features, and retain data under different plans and policies. Billing needs to turn those product activities into clear, reliable customer experiences—from usage measurement and plan enforcement to invoices, credits, and account state.

You’ll work across the billing stack: usage metering, subscriptions and entitlements, payment integrations, invoicing, credits, and the internal systems that reconcile them. This is a deeply technical IC role. It is not a finance-operations role, and it is not a backend generalist role that contributes to billing occasionally.

You’ll be a technical authority on billing correctness and scale, helping Braintrust launch pricing models that let customers adopt the platform with confidence as their AI workloads grow.

What you'll do

Core responsibilities:

  • Own Braintrust billing architecture end-to-end, including metering, plans, subscriptions, entitlements, invoices, credits and payments.

  • Design our billing architecture to solve immediate needs and simplify billing for new features as they are developed and released.

  • Ensure Braintrust accurately measures and bills for product usage, including processed data, evaluation scores, model usage, and data retention.

  • Partner with product, infrastructure, finance, and customer-facing teams to introduce new pricing models and billing workflows with confidence.

Build the systems that power Braintrust billing, such as:

  • A reliable usage-metering and aggregation pipeline that turns product activity into accurate customer usage.

  • A subscription, limits, and entitlement system that supports plan allowances, feature access, trials, upgrades, and on-demand usage.

About the Role:
Kong is the AI Connectivity Company. We build the infrastructure that lets enterprises govern APIs and AI traffic at scale — and that infrastructure is becoming critical to how India's government and public sector modernize their systems.
We're hiring an Account Executive to own a defined patch of PSU (Public Sector Undertaking) and Government accounts across India. You'll work the full government buying cycle — tenders, GeM listings, System Integrator relationships, empanelment — to bring Kong's platform into major public-sector modernization programs.


This role is based in Delhi and reports to a Country Manager.


What You'll Do:

  • Own the sales cycle, government-style. Lead deals from first conversation through RFP response, technical and financial bid submission, and contract award. Track PQ (pre-qualification) criteria, EMD requirements, and L1 bidding dynamics. Keep your pipeline accurate to what's actually documented in the tender process — not what looks good in a forecast.

  • Work the ecosystem, not just the account. Government and PSU deals rarely close direct. Build real relationships with the System Integrators (SIs) and OEM partners who carry the technical bid, and make sure Kong is positioned — and empanelled — before the tender drops.

  • Navigate multiple stakeholders. IT Secretaries, CTOs and CIOs at PSUs, nodal officers, procurement and finance committees — each has different priorities and a different definition of "done." Map them accurately and plan around all of them.

  • Build account plans for your patch. Identify which departments and PSUs are actively modernizing, where their budget cycles sit, and what a realistic path to close looks like. Then execute against it.

  • Get fluent in the platform and the landscape. Know Kong's API and AI governance platform well enough to defend it in a technical bid, and know where competitors are already empanelled.

  • Meet your number. Consistently hit quota. Government cycles are long — consistency across quarters matters more than any single deal.

  • Bring in the rest of Kong early. Loop in sales engineering, legal, and the channel team before compliance and certification requirements (STQC, data residency, MeitY empanelment) become a bottleneck late in the deal.

  • Travel. Expect real time in government offices and PSU sites across India. This is a relationship business, and relationships in this sector are built in person.

What You'll Bring:

  • 8-12 years in B2B SaaS or enterprise technology sales, with direct experience selling into Indian government departments or PSUs. This isn't optional — the public-sector buying process is different enough that generalist enterprise experience alone won't carry you.

  • A track record of consistently hitting quota (typically in the ₹2–5 Cr / $300K–$750K range) sold through longer, multi-stakeholder government cycles.

  • Working knowledge of India's government tendering lifecycle — GeM, RFP/RFI processes, technical and financial bids, PQ criteria, EMD — and how empanelment with bodies like MeitY or NIC actually works in practice.

  • Established relationships with System Integrators and OEM partners active in India's public-sector technology space.

  • Process discipline and patience. Government deals move on their own timeline. You bring structure to that timeline — you don't try to force it.

  • Executive presence with senior government officials and PSU leadership, along with the judgment to know when to push and when to wait.

  • Ownership with collaboration. You run your patch, but you know when to pull in your manager, sales engineering, or a partner. In the public sector, this isn't a solo sport.

What You'll Do:

  • Design and implement advanced token management systems, including refresh token rotation, proof-of-possession tokens, and custom token introspection with real-time revocation capabilities.

  • Lead development of Kong Identity's extensible claims engine supporting dynamic attribute resolution, contextual claim injection, and complex business logic evaluation at token issuance.

  • Architect global identity infrastructure with edge optimization, intelligent token caching, and cross-region replication strategies for sub-millisecond authentication latency worldwide.

  • Design sophisticated rate limiting, anomaly detection, and fraud prevention systems to protect against credential stuffing, token abuse, and distributed attacks.

  • Build enterprise identity federation capabilities, including SAML bridge patterns, external IdP chaining, and custom protocol adapters for legacy system integration.

  • Lead technical strategy for Kong Identity's developer experience, including SDKs, webhooks, audit logging, and real-time analytics dashboards for token lifecycle visibility.

  • Architect advanced client management systems supporting dynamic client registration, automated credential rotation, and programmatic policy enforcement.

  • Design Kong Identity's plugin architecture enables custom grant flows, protocol extensions, and third-party integrations while maintaining security boundaries.

  • Drive implementation of compliance frameworks (SOC 2, FedRAMP, GDPR), including comprehensive audit trails, data residency controls, and privacy-preserving token designs.

  • Lead technical initiatives for Kong Identity's integration with observability platforms, supporting distributed tracing, metrics collection, and security event correlation.

  • Mentor engineering teams on advanced identity concepts including zero-trust architectures, workload identity, and service mesh integration patterns.

     

What You'll Bring:

  • 7+ years of experience building production identity platforms at leading identity providers or enterprise software companies, with proven track record of handling millions of authentication requests daily.

  • Deep expertise in advanced OAuth 2.0 extensions (PKCE, mTLS, JWT bearer assertions, token exchange), OpenID Connect profiles, and emerging standards like OAuth 2.1 and GNAP.

  • Proven experience architecting multi-tenant identity platforms with complex isolation requirements, tenant-specific configurations, and enterprise feature sets.

  • Strong background in cryptographic protocols including advanced JWT patterns, key rotation strategies, Hardware Security Module (HSM) integration, and post-quantum cryptography considerations.

  • Experience building identity platforms with sophisticated analytics, real-time monitoring, and security event detection capabilities at enterprise scale.

  • Expertise in global identity infrastructure including edge deployment strategies, geo-distributed token validation, and cross-region data consistency patterns.

  • Deep understanding of enterprise identity integration patterns including SAML federation, LDAP/AD bridges, SCIM provisioning, and custom protocol adapters.

  • Proven track record building developer-first identity platforms including comprehensive SDKs, webhook systems, and extensible API designs.

  • Experience with identity platform security including threat modeling, penetration testing coordination, and implementation of advanced attack prevention mechanisms.

  • Strong background in compliance and regulatory requirements for identity systems including audit trail design, data residency controls, and privacy engineering.

  • Experience building identity platforms supporting complex organizational structures, delegated administration, and fine-grained permission models.

  • Expertise in high-performance system design including horizontal scaling strategies, caching architectures, and latency optimization for identity operations.

  • Knowledge of service mesh identity patterns, workload identity bootstrapping, and integration with container orchestration platforms.

  • Experience with identity protocol extensions, custom grant flows, and building extensible identity platforms that support diverse use cases.

  • Proven ability to lead technical initiatives in complex, regulated environments while balancing innovation with security and compliance requirements.

Why Kong?

The Role

AI hasn't just changed what we sell, it's changed how we sell it. As an Account Development Representative (ADR) at Kong, you'll be one of the first voices prospects hear about the next generation of API and AI Agent management, and you'll do it using the same class of AI-native tooling and signal-based workflows we sell.

You won't be grinding through generic call lists. You'll operate inside a signal-based pipeline built on tools like Nooks, Octave, and ZoomInfo, surfacing accounts showing real buying intent (competitor churn signals, funding events, tech-stack shifts, hiring patterns) and turning that intelligence into sharp, personalized conversations.

- Qualify and convert inbound interest quickly, applying a modern qualification framework built for fast-moving AI buying cycles (tension, economic impact, buying mandate, proof, and optionality) rather than legacy checklist selling.

- Continuously test messaging, sequencing, and calling approaches, treating your pipeline like an experiment you're always optimizing.

- Build a point of view and public presence in the API/AI infrastructure space, becoming a trusted resource for prospects navigating this shift.

- Feed market and competitive intelligence back to GTM leadership to sharpen targeting and messaging over time.

- Deepen your product fluency by partnering closely with Sales and Product, especially on how enterprises are approaching AI Gateway and token governance.

Your pipeline directly fuels a company at the center of one of the biggest infrastructure shifts in software.

Essential Skills

- 1-2+ years of SDR/ADR experience in high-growth B2B SaaS, ideally selling a technical or infrastructure product within the Public Sector.

- Genuine AI curiosity - you've used (or are eager to master) modern AI-native prospecting tools, not just traditional sequencers.

- Growth mindset - you treat skill as something built through reps, feedback, and iteration.

- Comfortable on the phone and unafraid of cold outreach; you track and improve your own conversion rate.

- Resilient and self-driven - rejection is data, not a verdict.

- Coachable - you actively seek feedback and adapt quickly to new plays and tooling.

Who Thrives Here

You'll fit right in if you:

- Get energized by fast-moving AI and infrastructure markets.

- Want ownership over your process from signal to sequence to booked meeting.

- Value a culture of experimentation over rigid scripts.

- Care about the quality of every touch, not just the volume.

*Bonus points if you've got exposure to APIs, cloud-native platforms, or AI/agent tooling but curiosity and drive matter more than a specific resume line.

Life at Kong

- 401(k) program

- Flexible PTO + company holidays

- Wellness and mental health support

description:
Are you ready to unlock intelligence?

If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria below but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others.

About the Role:

Kong is hiring an ADR Team Lead to support our NEMEA region: the UK, Benelux, and Nordics. This is a player-coach role. You'll carry your own pipeline targets while taking an active hand in developing the team around you, especially the newer ADRs still finding their footing.

You'll work closely with, and report into, the Senior Manager for NEMEA. You're shaping how the team operates, not running it solo. Think of this as a high-impact individual contributor role with a leadership layer built in: the natural next step for an ADR who's ready to start making other people better, not just themselves.

Our NEMEA team is already strong. Driven, independent, hitting their numbers. What they need isn't more oversight. They need someone who sharpens how the team works, especially around process and tooling, while making sure newer reps get the support to ramp fast.

You'll report to Oscar Winberg. He moves fast, sets a high bar, and expects people to bring solutions, not just flag problems. He's direct, so you'll always know exactly where you stand, and he expects that same directness back: if you disagree, he wants the pushback, backed by data, not silence. Earn his trust and he'll hand you real ownership. What he won't do is hand-hold, so this role suits someone who'd rather be given room to run than told exactly what to do.

What You'll Do:

Carry your own number. You'll hit your own pipeline targets as an active ADR. Your activity and results set the standard for everyone watching. You'll contribute to weekly forecasting alongside the Senior Manager.

Support newer ADRs. You'll be the first point of contact for less tenured reps, helping them ramp faster and build good habits early. You'll help with onboarding alongside the Senior Manager and Enablement, and run regular 1:1s with newer ADRs. Different reps need different things from you, so you'll read where each person is and adjust your coaching accordingly rather than running the same playbook on everyone. You'll help build individual development plans grounded in a real read of each rep's attitude, process, and results, and you'll flag underperformance early, with context, instead of letting it fester.

Coach and upskill the team. You'll support team coaching sessions: live dialling, pitch practice, feedback loops. You'll run or contribute to upskilling initiatives, on your own or with Enablement. You'll share what's working, best practices, sequences, outbound approaches, with the wider team, and give direct, specific feedback often, recognizing strong work and not letting bad habits slide.

Sharpen process and tooling. You'll help spot where the team's workflows and tooling could run more efficiently, and support the Senior Manager in rolling out improvements without stripping reps of their autonomy. You'll be the go-to person for best practice on Salesforce, Outreach, and the team's automation tools.

Contribute to the wider GTM motion. You'll keep strong alignment with your AE partners and take part in pipe review cadences. You'll support the Senior Manager in preparing performance updates and regional insights, and join bi-weekly RD cadences where it makes sense.

What You'll Bring:

  • Hands-on ADR or SDR experience. You know what this job feels like from the inside, not just what it looks like from a deck.

  • A real coach's instinct. You get energy from making other people better, not just from hitting your own number.

  • The ability to juggle competing priorities without dropping the ball. Your own quota, coaching newer reps, and process work will all pull on your time in the same week, and you know how to decide what actually matters right now.

  • Strong time management. This is one we screen for directly, not something we assume comes with experience.

  • A bias for building. You spot what needs fixing and go build it, rather than working only through a list of tasks someone else handed you.

  • Analytical rigor. You make calls based on data, not gut feel, and you're comfortable being specific about why a number moved, including when that number is going the wrong way.

  • A track record of top-tier performance that holds up on both counts: the day-to-day discipline that drives it (activity, sequence execution, pipeline hygiene), and the results that discipline produces, quarter over quarter, not just once.

  • Real trust with your AE and RD partners, earned through consistency, not just alignment on paper.

  • Transparency, especially with leadership, especially when something isn't on track. We'd rather hear it early than find out later.

  • The kind of presence the team actually looks up to, not just reports to.

  • Comfort in an allbound model with a heavy outbound emphasis.

  • Self-awareness and a genuine investment in growing as a leader.

  • Language skills relevant to the UK, Benelux, or Nordics are a bonus, not a requirement.

Culture and Value:

The EMEA SDR team are weather makers. We don't wait for opportunity, we create it. We're accountable, relentless, and we invest in each other like no other team does.

- Deepen your product fluency by partnering closely with Sales and Product, especially on how enterprises are approaching AI Gateway and token governance.

- Genuine AI curiosity - you've used (or are eager to master) modern AI-native prospecting tools, not just traditional sequencers.

- Coachable - you actively seek feedback and adapt quickly to new plays and tooling.

- Get energized by fast-moving AI and infrastructure markets.

- Want ownership over your process from signal to sequence to booked meeting.

- Value a culture of experimentation over rigid scripts.

- Care about the quality of every touch, not just the volume.

About the Role:

Kong is the connectivity layer of AI. We're a 6-time Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader and a Forrester Wave Leader, running in production at Fortune 500 scale. Every enterprise moving from “we're piloting AI” to “AI is in production” runs into the same wall: governance, security, and connectivity for a traffic pattern nobody built for. That's the opportunity in front of this team, and it's why Professional Services is one of the fastest-growing parts of this company right now.

We're hiring a Professional Services Manager to lead a team of Field Engineers and Engagement Managers across Kong's US Professional Services organization. This is a leadership role, not a delivery role: you're directly responsible for delivery outcomes, staffing, and the growth of the people who sit hands-on with customer engineering teams every day.

You own the full engagement lifecycle for your book of business — staffing the right Field Engineers and Engagement Managers on every account, holding the team to go-live dates and technical quality, and driving resolution personally on the highest-risk or highest-value accounts. You're operating at the intersection of people leadership, technical delivery, and enterprise account management, and you're judged on outcomes, not activity.

We want leaders who've done the implementation work themselves and now want to multiply that impact through a team: coach the engineers, clear the blockers and build the delivery muscle that lets Kong keep pace with enterprise demand for API and AI connectivity.

You'll work daily with Solutions Architects, Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Product Engineering — scoping engagements correctly before they land on your team, and feeding what you learn in the field straight back into how Kong builds and sells.

This is a rare seat: AI connectivity is a land grab right now, and the person who builds this team's delivery model in the next 18 months owns a track record that doesn't come around twice.

Impact

Lead the team that turns Kong's platform into production reality for some of the world's largest enterprises — the ones deciding right now how AI gets governed, secured, and scaled across their business.

Growth

Build your leadership craft against the fastest-moving category in enterprise software: AI connectivity, cloud-native architecture, and distributed systems at Fortune 500 scale. Prove out this team's model and the case for more scope writes itself.

Opportunity

Join a Professional Services organization growing as fast as the AI adoption curve it's built to serve — market-leading credibility behind every conversation you walk into, and a direct hand in building the delivery model while it's still being written.

What You'll Do:

  • Manage and grow a team of Field Engineers and Engagement Managers — hiring, coaching, career development, and performance management.

  • Own delivery outcomes across your book of business: go-live dates, technical quality, and customer satisfaction. Report on them with the same rigor you'd demand from your team.

  • Staff the right Field Engineer and Engagement Manager to every engagement based on account complexity, technical scope, and team capacity.

  • Be the senior escalation point on at-risk or high-complexity engagements — drive resolution and direct the team's response personally.

  • Run your team's operating cadence: staffing reviews, at-risk reviews, 1:1s, and status reporting up to Professional Services leadership.

  • Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Solutions Architecture to scope new engagements accurately and take clean handoffs from pre-sale to delivery.

  • Set and enforce delivery standards across your team — reusable accelerators, reference architectures, and best practices that outlive any single engagement.

  • Feed what your team learns in the field back to Kong Product and Engineering — real customer signal shapes our roadmap.

  • Lead your team's work on the strategic initiatives that matter most right now: AI connectivity, governance, platform modernization, and cloud-native transformation.

What You'll Bring:

Experience

  • 8+ years in customer-facing engineering, professional services, or platform engineering, including 2+ years directly managing a technical, customer-facing team.

  • A track record of delivery leadership in API gateways, API management, integrations, or distributed systems platforms — deep enough that you can direct and evaluate your team's work, not just review it.

  • Experience managing staffing, capacity, and prioritization across a portfolio of concurrent enterprise engagements.

  • Strong Kubernetes and cloud-native infrastructure fluency — enough to unblock your team and hold your own with customer architects and executives.

  • Experience with major cloud providers: AWS, Azure, or GCP.

  • Comfort directing and evaluating automation frameworks, deployment tooling, CI/CD pipelines, or migration tooling built by your team.

  • Prior experience in API Management, Open Source, Middleware, SaaS, or Infrastructure software companies is a strong plus.

  • A decisive leadership mindset — you make the staffing and prioritization call and drive it to resolution without needing to do the work yourself.

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguous, fast-moving enterprise environments where the right call today beats the perfect call next week.

  • Real enthusiasm for AI, modern infrastructure, and cloud-native technology — this team is living the shift, not reading about it.

title: Product Manager, Billing (Senior Staff)
description:
Are you ready to unlock intelligence?

If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria below but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others.

The Mission:

Kong is building the future of AI connectivity, empowering developers to connect, secure, and scale their applications with speed and intelligence. We are hiring a Product Manager, Billing to lead the product and systems work behind how Konnect makes money: entitlements, metering, checkout, invoicing, provisioning, and the enterprise and marketplace motions that surround them.

In this role you are the product owner of Konnect's commercial operating layer: the systems that translate what Sales sells and what customers use into what ends up on an invoice. That means plan and entitlement design, the usage metering pipeline, self-serve checkout and subscription lifecycle, customer organization and billing admin experiences, enterprise billing workflows (CPQ sync, custom contracts), and cloud marketplace billing. You will work hand-in-hand with Product Growth, Pricing & Packaging, Finance, GTM, Sales, and Engineering.

This role reports to the Sr Director, Product (Platform) and sits at the intersection of two multi-year transformations: Kong's move from a single-product API gateway company into a multi-product enterprise, and Monetization's company-wide overhaul of pricing and packaging. The Billing, Provisioning, and Fulfillment program has historically been manual and relationship-driven. Your job is to turn it into a product, so Sales can sell more, Finance can bill more accurately, and customers get an experience that matches the quality of what they are paying for.

What You’ll Do:

  • Platform Vision: Set a multi-year direction for how Konnect prices, meters, entitles, and invoices. Decide what becomes shared platform capability versus what stays feature-specific, and sequence delivery so near-term work lands without creating long-term drag.

  • Unified Entitlements: Build the entitlements model that determines what every customer can access within Konnect. Make entitlements a first-class concept that is consistently defined in contracts, enforced in-product, honored by provisioning, and reflected in billing.

  • Pricing & Packaging Delivery: Act as the product and systems counterpart to Monetization. Translate pricing and packaging decisions into production reality: configuring plans, reshaping metering, updating contracts, coordinating customer migrations, and making sure a rollout doesn't disrupt existing revenue.

  • Metering & Usage Visibility: Run the event pipeline, aggregation layer, and reporting experiences that show customers what they consumed and what they are being charged. Hold a financial-grade bar on accuracy, auditability, and reconcilability.

  • Checkout & Subscription Lifecycle: Own how customers self-serve onto a plan, change plans, renew, lapse, and recover. That covers plan discovery, checkout, the underlying payments integration, subscription state, retries and dunning, and the admin surfaces where customers manage their own billing.

  • 5+ years of professional software development experience.

title: Engineering Manager, Managed Gateways Infrastructure
description:
Are you ready to unlock intelligence?

If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria below but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others.

The Mission:

Kong Cloud Gateways is Kong's foundational cloud-native SaaS platform, powering its managed API and AI Gateway offerings. It provides a multi-tenant control plane, automation, and platform services that let customers securely deploy, operate, and scale dedicated gateway infrastructure with the simplicity of a fully managed cloud service. Behind that experience sits a distributed platform responsible for provisioning, fleet management, software lifecycle, zero-downtime upgrades, observability, security, and multi-region operations across globally distributed cloud infrastructure - built to a target of 99.99% availability, balancing reliability, performance, operational excellence, and infrastructure efficiency at global SaaS scale.

As a Software Engineering Manager for Managed Gateways Infrastructure, you will own and grow Kong's Bangalore-based engineering team, taking full accountability for this multi-tenant SaaS platform. Kong Cloud Gateways is growing 100% YoY, and as enterprises increasingly adopt AI alongside traditional APIs, this platform becomes an increasingly important part of Kong's API and AI strategy - every improvement in automation, scalability, and operational excellence you drive accelerates new platform capabilities and lets product teams innovate faster. Beyond the technical charter, you play a key role in shaping a dynamic engineering culture - one built on urgency, ownership, and first-principles thinking - as the team scales to match the pace of the business.

This is a highly technical, hands-on leadership role - you're expected to stay close to the systems, dig into hard problems alongside your team, and not hesitate to get into the trenches when it matters.

What You'll Do:

  • Own and grow Kong's Managed Gateways Infrastructure engineering team in Bangalore - scaling the team's capability, raising the technical bar, and staying hands-on in critical implementations and incidents, not just directing from a distance.

  • Own the reliability and scalability of a multi-tenant SaaS infrastructure platform serving customers across regions and clouds - every architectural decision has to hold up under multi-tenant load, isolation, and blast-radius considerations, not just single-tenant assumptions.

  • Drive 4-9s (99.99%+) availability across Kong's global infrastructure footprint - owning capacity, resilience, and failure-mode design across multi-region, multi-cloud deployments (AWS, Azure, GCP) so Cloud Gateways stays up for customers everywhere, at any scale.

  • Act as a direct technical contributor when it counts - complex incidents, architecture reviews, and high-stakes implementations that materially move the needle on Managed Gateways' growth and reliability.

  • Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing engineering team building and operating Kong's SaaS infrastructure for Managed Gateways, in direct support of our critical enterprise customer base globally.

  • Architect and implement robust, scalable, and fault-tolerant cloud-native systems using technologies like Kubernetes, Golang, and major cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP).

  • Own the complete operational lifecycle end-to-end - infrastructure, reliability, on-call, incident response, and blameless post-mortems - as one integrated engineering charter, not a separate function.

  • Drive developer delight and operational efficiency through automation, self-service tooling, and streamlined workflows for deploying and managing API gateways, while proactively preventing technical debt and reducing operational toil.

  • Define, track, and report on key SLOs and SLIs, and advocate for architectural best practices that keep Managed Gateways performant and resilient as it scales.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, engineering, and support teams to influence roadmap decisions and ensure operational readiness for new features.

What You'll Bring:

The Toolkit:

  • Proven experience leading and managing software engineering teams responsible for infrastructure and reliability in a fast-paced, high-growth environment, with a track record of staying technically hands-on rather than purely delegating.

  • Deep, current expertise in designing, deploying, and operating highly available distributed systems on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) - this role needs someone who can still open a terminal and debug production, not just review architecture diagrams.

  • Extensive hands-on experience with Kubernetes (k8s) and container orchestration in production environments.

  • Proficiency in Golang or similar modern programming languages for infrastructure automation and service development.

  • Strong understanding of observability principles and experience with tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar.

  • Demonstrated ability to manage critical incidents personally when needed, perform root cause analysis, and implement effective preventative measures.

  • Familiarity with API gateway technologies, service mesh, or network proxies is a significant plus.

The Kong DNA:

  • Ownership: You take full responsibility for the reliability and performance of systems, driving initiatives from conception to completion.

  • Urgency: You thrive in dynamic environments, prioritizing critical issues and delivering impactful solutions with speed and precision.

  • Collaboration: You build strong relationships, foster open communication, and work effectively across global teams to achieve shared goals.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with open-source contributions or active participation in SRE/cloud-native communities.

  • Certifications in cloud platforms (e.g., AWS Certified DevOps Engineer) or Kubernetes (e.g., CKA, CKAD).

  • Background in companies focused on developer tools, infrastructure software, or API management.
